member of the commission. − mr president, i would first like to thank the rapporteur, mr cercas, and the shadow rapporteurs for their constructive approach to this own-initiative report. the commission has followed the debates on this issue in the european parliament with great interest, given the importance and topical nature of this subject. the report is very timely, coming as it does at a time of severe economic and financial hardship across the european union with a heavy impact on society. the commission shares the view that a renewed dynamism from all relevant actors is needed to minimise the social impact of the crisis. most of all they need to pursue strategies, policies, practices and whatever is in their power to invest in human capital and create jobs, including for those who have become redundant due to restructuring, and provide them with training and re-skilling to facilitate their quick reintegration into the labour market. in the past months, a number of restructuring processes have been announced in many industrial sectors throughout europe. for the third quarter of 2012, according to the latest data of the european restructuring monitor, 274 restructuring cases were registered. these cases amount to a net job loss of more than 74 000, thus showing a reversed situation compared to the pre-crisis one. before the crisis, in the third quarter of 2007, for the same number of restructuring cases there were 6 600 net job creations – less than one tenth of the current figure. these figures actually reflect a structural change in the european economy and the labour market. this requires a clear policy action. for this, the eu can provide a wide range of support, including through policies and also through funding. in recent initiatives, such as the employment package, the youth employment package and the updated industrial policy communication, specification actions are envisaged to improve timely anticipation of skills and training needs and facilitate the necessary human capital investment. i may also mention vice-president tajani’s new initiative, entrepreneurship 2020, supporting new businesses in crucial phases of their life cycle and helping them grow, and specific initiatives in sectors which are in difficulty and experiencing major restructuring, such as the automotive industry, with our recently adopted cars 2020 action plan, but also the steel and shipbuilding industries, on which dialogues with all stakeholders involved have been set up and for which we are working together very closely. moreover, various eu funds can be used to better prepare and manage the restructuring processes and to help workers find new opportunities on the labour market. in particular, the european social fund and the european globalisation adjustment fund have a proven track record which shows that, if used well, they can make a real difference on the ground. in this context i remain concerned about the tendencies to weaken those instruments in the next mff or even to scrap them, as with the egaf. this would of course make it more difficult for the eu to play a relevant role in addressing the restructuring challenge. the commission shares parliament’s concerns regarding the ongoing restructuring operations, expressed on many occasions and reiterated in this report. more than ever, good anticipation of change and responsible management of restructuring, with the involvement of the social partners, are crucial. if not managed properly, restructuring operations can have negative consequences for the surrounding economy, incurring high social costs across regions, and can negatively affect workers and their families. evidence shows that timely anticipation of skills and training needs within companies, intelligent investment in human capital – also supported by eu financial instruments – and fully-fledged social dialogue can significantly add to companies’ competitiveness and facilitate intra-company and labour market transition of workers, while substantially mitigating the social costs resulting from downsizing. the commission has for a long time been acting to encourage proactive and anticipative stances towards change and restructuring, and is convinced of the need to ensure widespread observance of the best practices of well-prepared restructuring, which also aims to minimise the social costs. in the past ten years, a number of commission initiatives have contributed to the eu-level debate on this matter. these initiatives notably include the checklist on restructuring processes, which was adopted in june 2009, but also the 2003 orientations for reference in managing change and its social consequences, as well as a number of seminars and forums which contributed to identification and dissemination of good practices. more recently, the green paper of january 2012 has renewed the debate and made it possible to identify successful practices and policies in the field of restructuring and anticipation of change. following parliament’s vote on this report, the commission will incorporate parliament’s contribution and requests in the current assessment of possible further actions on the basis of the green paper. the commission will keep the european parliament informed on the follow-up it intends to give to parliament’s request.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, over the last ten years, companies in europe have had to adapt to increasingly tough competition and to an economic and financial crisis which has resulted in the closure or restructuring of many of them. the development of a basic framework that covers all the problems and does not impede the modernization and competitiveness of enterprises is very complicated, since there are many differences between the countries of the european union, not only in terms of legislation but also in terms of what is meant by restructuring. for some, it means deindustrialization and the relocation of manufacturing outside. for the new states, it means the privatization of state-controlled industries. and others focus on the dependence on multinational companies. it is not easy to find a balanced text which recognises and seeks to protect the parties concerned, both the company itself in terms of competitiveness or viability and the workers in terms of labour rights and safety at work, and which can also be useful for member states and local authorities in the absence of regulation, but i think the rapporteur's report makes very positive points. one of them is anticipation of change, as the commissioner has said. it is true that in many cases restructuring cannot be foreseen and is the consequence of events external to the company, but it must be borne in mind that a correct initial forecast can help the company to avoid and minimise the negative effects that it may cause, especially in terms of collective redundancies. the information and involvement of all local economic actors, especially smes that are dependent on the company to be restructured, is essential for its survival. finally, proper training of workers, adapted to new trends and technologies, is equally essential for the worker and for the undertakings, also with the help of the structural funds, as the commissioner has said.

the european union solidarity fund was set up in 2002 to respond to major natural disasters affecting member states or countries that were in the process of joining the european union. until then, there was no other element or instrument that could intervene in the event of disasters. these ten years have been a success for this fund. they have made the principle of solidarity of the european union a principle that has taken on life and form. but in these ten years we have also been able to determine, by experience, exactly what this fund was lacking. we have seen that in the case of major natural disasters, those causing damage above the threshold for fund intervention in the country concerned, it has worked reasonably well. but we have also seen that in the case of regional disasters, those which occur and alter conditions in a particular region and affect the daily lives of people, their living conditions, and which have serious and lasting repercussions, many requests have been made by the regions which have not been accepted. more than 60% of the applications were related to this type of disaster and, as the concept was a very vague concept with unclear indicators, many expectations have been created by different regions that have not been met. this has led to the fact that, when we were able to draw up this new report today, we were able to correct this indeterminacy and this lack of clarity in the definition of these catastrophes. we have also seen over the last ten years that the fund could be made more efficient. because from the time the disaster occurs until the member state collects, it can take nine to twelve months, which puts the citizens of that region in a difficult situation. so we have proposed an acceleration, a simplification of the fund's procedures and advances, advance payments. we have also seen that in slow catastrophes such as drought the ten-week deadline for submitting an assessment of the damage to the commission cannot work and we have therefore asked that, in the case of this type of slow catastrophes, the use of the fund be made more flexible. in short, we have called for a reform of this regulation, but without touching on the financial aspects, either expenditure or the eligibility criteria. you will recall that in 2005 a proposal was made, which was not accepted by the council precisely because it concerned expenditure and the council did not agree with it, since it could cover other types of disasters in addition to natural disasters. in this case, that has not been the case in order for it to go ahead, for the commission, the council and parliament to give the go-ahead. the expenditure and the eligibility criteria are not touched at all. we have therefore defined and proposed for the regions criteria such as gdp, gross domestic product, with the aim of making it a threshold sufficiently adapted to the region that is going to ask for aid. we also call for simplification of all procedures. in some cases, for example, the commission has so far made a granting act and then another by which the conditions for the use of the grants were established. we ask that this be done in one act. in short, we propose that the fund, with the same resources, should be more efficient, more flexible and more transparent.

member of the commission. − as you very well know, the money that goes to kics and the eit makes up only 25% of their budget. the remaining 75% comes from other sources, either from industries – which contribute quite a lot of money – or from regional or national funds. of course, we do not exclude the possibility of those funds also coming from structural funds. what you are proposing with the regional innovation schemes is very much related to the absorption of more structural funds from the eu. i think we should make the most of it, but the advantage of the eit, as i said before, is the leverage money that is created by the very small amount of 25% of what needs to be invested for them to grow and be sustainable.
member of the commission. − as regards getting more people involved, i think the main aspect of that has to be first of all providing the incentives. so whether it involves grants or prizes or financial instruments, i think all of those have to be tailored to meet the requirements. as regards widening participation, excellence is not everywhere but it can be found anywhere. i think what we have to do is to develop that excellence, and this is why we are very happy that parliament has put such an emphasis on widening participation and on using the synergies between horizon 2020 and the cohesion funds, for example. i think that is crucial, because horizon 2020 funds on the basis of excellence, and that will not be watered down in any way; but the cohesion funds need to be used for capacity-building. we have put in place and are putting in place the elements that are required to widen participation, whether it is teaming or twinning, further advances in the whole cost programme or using the two funds for funding the same project but different aspects of it, which was not possible up to now. and of course the european research area chairs, which are also very important. we have put together a full package to widen participation, and i know that the newer member states are particularly interested in utilising those elements of horizon 2020. i do not think we should ever put a quota on what is acceptable for participation in member states, but i think we need to encourage excellence to grow when we find it.
member of the commission. − you know very well that when we are deciding on the themes for the new kics, visibility and clear rules are very important for us. this is what makes it attractive for business to participate. and that is what i have been insisting on, in the inclusion of the eit in horizon 2020, because this flexibility and these clear rules are very important for industries. that is why i believe that we cannot decide that we should have another four kics or five or six kics without also specifying the themes, because that is what makes it attractive to business – and for other partners for that matter, such as research centres and education institutions – to participate: visibility, clear rules and flexibility.
member of the commission. − teaming and twinning are very important elements of the widening participation part of the proposal. in looking at how this might operate, obviously we are very conscious of the fact that twinning aims at significantly strengthening a defined area of research in an emerging institution. when we talk about teaming, we are aiming at the creation of new centres of excellence or a significant upgrade of existing ones that are working in, and are part of, a low-performing member state or region. when you ask me when the very detailed elements of this proposal might emerge, i would expect them to emerge during the course of the trialogue discussions with parliament and the council. i think there is, particularly in parliament, huge interest in, and support for, this whole area of policy. we have had a number of discussions in the council on widening participation, and particularly those ministers from the newer member states were very anxious to be able to tie down exactly what each of these proposals meant. so it was not just talk, or a proposal that we threw out there; behind the proposal there are specific actions that need to be taken so that we can prove that, when you put policies in place, it is possible to widen participation and to get a greater family of researchers and institutions into the framework programme. that is what i think you will see during the course of the trialogue discussions.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report as it represents a boost to economic activity in europe's urban areas. the economic depression induced by the international financial crisis in europe has led to a severe deterioration of many urban areas, especially in the south of the continent. this report proposes a resolution which will help to revive both economic activity and the quality of life in the depressed areas of european cities. the report insists on developing sustainable programmes for the recovery of cities under participatory planning dynamics that allow citizens to develop the kind of city they want to live in. i therefore believe that this can be a step forward for european cities and i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposes the appropriate use of cohesion funds to build a new model of urban planning which limits their use to the creation of housing bubbles and, on the contrary, actively encourages urban planning with a significant social dimension. the report proposes actions to rehabilitate existing parts of cities, encouraging the functional conversion of disused areas, highlighting their characteristics and cultural heritage. all this must be in the service of optimum use of the cohesion funds, both quantitatively and qualitatively, in the service of common objectives in urban matters at european level. in addition, new planning dynamics involving associations and citizens are proposed with the aim of ensuring the necessary link between general policies and specific territorial areas, so that the specific characteristics, identity and history of the site where they are to be implemented are reflected in the design of the policies. in conclusion, this report proposes important aspects for urban management and encourages the implementation of urban rehabilitation programmes. in addition, it is proposed to focus on disused urban heritage and redefine it for its highest use.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which seeks to improve the functioning of the european union solidarity fund (eusf). this fund is used to provide assistance to the population affected by natural disasters occurring within the territory of the union. the report includes proposals to improve its functioning, including measures to reduce the time between a disaster and the mobilisation of the fund. the eusf was set up in 2002 to respond to the severe floods in romania that year, but has not been modified since then and there have been many different crises that the eusf has had to assist in. the report proposes only measures which can improve the operation of this financial mechanism in the care of victims and i therefore welcome it and have voted in favour.
in writing. − in favour. we are in favour of a well-functioning solidarity fund that contributes to improving sustainability and effectiveness in disaster prevention and response. we tabled a number of amendments aiming to stress the sustainability of interventions and coherence with national mechanisms. we also highlighted that speeding up procedures not only relates to european institutions (e.g., budget procedure), but also to national or regional authorities. the majority of our amendments have been carried, and we managed to improve language, e.g. when it came to advance payments, as well as the report.
in writing. − despite the operational shortcomings that have come to light over the years, the solidarity fund has proven to be one of the most successful and well-received union instruments, since it is one of the few instruments available to the union with which it can demonstrate its solidarity with and closeness to european citizens. the changes in the economic situation of the union and the majority of its member states have to be taken into account, the operability of the fund should be improved without incurring additional costs. procedures should be clearer, more precise and more transparent. i endorse the need for a clear and precise definition of the concept of disaster, setting a general criterion for assessing the severity of damage caused, and for thresholds to be established geared to the appropriate territorial level. this would help to remove doubts and negative attitudes to the european union among both member states and the public, which may otherwise believe that the union does not offer an appropriate response to their problems. the bureaucracy necessary for the fund’s mobilisation should be reduced.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposes, by way of a recommendation, to establish a regulation on the european union code of administrative procedure, which will contribute to the proper functioning of the european institutions. the report proposes a regulation setting out the basic principles of good administration, developing basic principles such as non-discrimination, impartiality, proportionality, etc. the report proposes that the commission develop a regulation on the basis of article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i think it is a good report in proposing the introduction of the principles of good administration and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. − in favour. for our group, the principle of transparency is of key importance, and we have insisted that this principle is included and emphasised: the union's administration should be open. it should document the administrative procedures and keep adequate records of incoming and outgoing mail, documents received and the decisions and measures taken. all contributions from advisory bodies and interested parties should be made available in the public domain. our group also contributed to clarifying the principle of impartiality of administrative decisions. no member of staff should take part in an administrative decision in which he or she has a financial interest. any conflict of interest should be communicated by the member of staff concerned to his or her immediate superior, who may take the decision to exclude the member of staff concerned from the procedure, having regard to the particular circumstances of the case. an interested member of the public may request that an official be excluded from taking part in any decision which will affect that person's individual interests. the request to that effect should be submitted in writing and should state the grounds on which it is based.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the european commission to respond appropriately to the risks posed by the globalisation of trade, which threatens the most vulnerable segments of society. between 2000 and 2010, there were more than 11 000 cases of business restructuring in europe, with a ratio of almost two jobs destroyed for every job created. to curb this dynamic, companies need to be more involved in offering workers alternatives to redundancy. in addition, spain has regulated in the opposite direction, with a labour reform that facilitates dismissal, turning its back on social dialogue and ignoring the search for alternatives to dismissal. for this reason, the development of a european standard to encourage greater employment protection and the implementation of measures such as the reduction of working time are all the more important. in addition, the promotion of skills management strategies and increased investment in internal retraining or training programmes offers incentives to the company to avoid redundancies. the dialogue must become more important in the light of the economic situation, so that the opportunity to implement european legislation that is fairer and more protective of workers is seized.
in writing. the recommendations voted on today are a necessary response to the risks of globalisation of trade, which threaten the most vulnerable populations, and to the increase in the number of company restructurings in europe and france. between 2000 and 2010, more than 11 000 restructuring cases were recorded by the european monitoring centre for restructuring, with a ratio of 1.8 jobs destroyed for every one job created. that ratio went up to 2.5 to 1 between 2008 and 2010! in europe, three million industrial jobs have disappeared since the start of the crisis. in france, the phenomenon is older, since between 1991 and 2010, 1.2 million jobs disappeared. to stop the bleeding, it is first necessary to involve the employees and their representatives, and as soon as possible, in order to protect jobs and activities. local and regional public authorities must also be involved, as their decisions have an impact on the business of the enterprise. the courageous employees of the fralib factory in gemenos have set up an exemplary project of cooperative society, with the support of the marseille urban community, in order to protect their tea production activity against financial speculation.

mr. president, this is the third legislative initiative on rating agencies since 2009. it is a step forward in meeting the g20 commitments in a manner consistent with the work of the international monetary fund and the financial stability board. we adopted it after six months of hard negotiations with the council, preserving the essential content, voting in the committee on economic affairs, and for that i congratulate the parliamentary negotiating team and, in particular, the rapporteur, mr domenici. the errors of the rating agencies are at the root of the crisis, its effects have been multiplied by the over-reliance on them, by the regulatory dependence, which has discouraged the good risk management. to correct this, in addition to establishing principles for market participants to have robust risk assessment systems, a transition process towards alternative standards is envisaged to be completed by 2020. democratic institutions cannot be held hostage by rating agencies. the volatility and procyclical effect of ratings on sovereign risks is evident. this legislation sets guidelines to ensure transparency and put a stop to political interference. the commission is also mandated to submit reports on the establishment of a european system for the assessment of sovereign risks and the establishment of a public sovereign risk rating agency. the package will also help prevent conflicts of interest, promote competition and strengthen the civil liability of agencies. although not the last, it is certainly an important step in its regulatory reform. answer to a blue card question. like many meps, as the european parliament has stated, we are in favour of europe having its own rating agencies. these self-rated agencies may have the legal basis of a foundation or they may be directly a public and independent agency which, by the quality of its ratings, can earn the trust of the markets and avoid the effects of the ratings we have been suffering from until now.
madam president, the excesses of a one-size-fits-all austerity policy and the lack of a comprehensive and integrated response at european level are producing very damaging effects. the development of a eurobond catalogue is not only legally possible but urgently needed to correct this situation and improve the economic governance of the euro area. in the sixth year of the crisis, more and more citizens are criticising europe for not mobilising all the means at its disposal to restore growth, create jobs and strengthen public finances in the member states in a sustainable way. if the rifts between the northern and southern states, between the central and peripheral states, widen, the cohesion needed for the european project will be jeopardized. structural mechanisms are needed to share the risks of a monetary policy more favourable to the central countries than to the peripheral ones. banking union will help us to prevent and limit the moral hazard of private debt and should be complemented by fiscal union in the public sphere; it needs to establish the conditions for euro area member states to reduce their debt, to keep it sustainable at reasonable levels and to avoid excessive costs or differentials in their financing. a european economic policy that encourages the development of the investments needed to meet our objectives must be promoted, and eurobonds can help to promote these objectives and make the euro a reliable global currency. that is why i wholeheartedly support the goulard report.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, let me thank the rapporteur, mr pallone, and the committee for this important report at a very critical juncture for the economic and monetary union. i understand that there has been a rather tense debate on this report. this reflects the difficult situation of europe in the crisis, which is analysed in the commission public finance reports of 2011 and 2012. i take due note of the fact that your motion for a resolution concludes that ensuring the sustainability of public finances is necessary. your report and resolution also stress the relevance of the efforts made by the union in recent years to reinforce its budgetary and economic governance. the commission also agrees with parliament’s view that such fiscal consolidation needs to be pursued in a country-specific and differentiated manner, aiming to preserve growth-friendly expenditure items and to respect equity among citizens in the name of social fairness. this is in line with the view expressed by the commission in our annual growth survey of last november. against the backdrop of a positive assessment of the report, i am glad to inform you that some of the relevant demands are already being fulfilled in current practice. in particular, the commission already delivers country-specific and rather detailed recommendations to member states, analyses the euro area as a whole and publishes its methodology underpinning the assessment of the structural balances of the member states. the coming months will still be difficult because the economy remains weak and our citizens continue to feel the impact of the crisis. but recent economic sentiment indicators are showing signs of stabilisation, and confidence in financial markets is considerably growing. this is reflected in the significant fall in borrowing costs for countries such as ireland, italy and spain. confidence has been boosted by determined policy action at the european level and in our member states, and also underpinned by the european central bank’s decision on ‘outright monetary transactions’. it is noteworthy that fiscal deficits have been reduced from above 6% in 2009 or 2010 to around 3% last year, and they should be coming down to a little above 2% this year. this is also to an extent the result of the work that has been done together by parliament, the commission and the council to reinforce economic governance under the six-pack. even if there is less reason for pessimism at the start of this year than there was a year ago, we cannot afford to lower our guard. instead, we must now capitalise on the improved sentiment and pursue the rebalancing and reforms of our economies with consistent determination. it is precisely for these reasons that we proposed our blueprint for a deep and genuine economic and monetary union, with a road map towards an emu that can deliver our citizens the benefits of stability, growth and jobs which the emu is supposed expected to ensure. therefore, in order to allow us to move forward on that road map, i would like to conclude by repeating myself and reiterating your call for the adoption of pending proposals such as the two-pack. let me stress that its adoption depends on the decisions of all actors involved in the process, including parliament, its political groups and each and every member of this parliament.

other aspects of competition policy, a fundamental part of the single market project. state aid can help to correct market failures and serve the public interest without harming the economy as a whole or causing market distortions by supporting undertakings that produce goods or services which would not otherwise be supplied. in difficult times, in the context of fiscal consolidation processes and a weak economy, it is more necessary than ever to ensure the efficiency of public spending. the same level of public spending can produce more and better impact with an intelligent public aid system that defends the rights of taxpayers and competitors, increases the quality of public spending and is developed in a framework of maximum legal certainty and minimum red tape to ensure its effectiveness. the commission is right to promote a review to ensure the proper application of state aid rules, focusing on those measures which may distort competition most severely, without creating unnecessary obstacles to measures which, without affecting cross-border trade or appreciably affecting competition, serve to achieve valuable objectives such as regional investment, development cases monitored for block exemption measures adopted at national level are problematic. action will therefore need to be taken in several directions, including strengthening participation and ex-ante consultation, improving coordination to ensure consistent application of the rules, improving compliance with measures taken at national level and full monitoring, including the provision of relevant information including the recovery of unlawful aid. the control of state aid is of great economic and political importance. it affects decisions taken by democratically elected authorities at in writing. - i voted in favour of this report as it includes amendments made by the legal services of parliament, the council and the commission to adapt the dangerous goods directive to comply with community law. the report presents only one amendment which is a formal adaptation of the directive without changing the substance of the directive, simply amending the extension period in several paragraphs of article 10 to extend the said period from one to two months by including the 2+2 formula in the time limits, thus allowing a reasonable time if parliament wishes to raise objections. this is a technical amendment which has been made to bring this directive into line with the law. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − in favour. the recast of the dangerous preparations directive (1999/45/ec) is proposed in order to codify amending acts and to align provisions regarding the commission’s power to adopt delegated and implementing acts to the lisbon treaty. the directive represents a bridging piece of legislation ensuring legal continuity within the legal sectoral framework, currently under fundamental reform due to the adoption of reach (regulation (ec) no 1907/2006). the dangerous preparations directive (dpd) regulates the classification, packaging and labelling of preparations, i.e. mixtures or solutions of two or more substances (chemical elements and their compounds). it remains applicable until 1 june 2015 within the transitional provisions of the clp (regulation (ec) no 1272/2008) as the eu’s new system on the classification and labelling of hazardous substances and mixtures, including the un’s globally harmonised system, in force since 20 january 2009. in addition, mixtures already placed on the market may continue to be supplied under the dpd rules until 1 june 2017. for substances, the clp rules have applied since 1 december 2010. the recast thus refers to an act that is about to be phased out.

in writing. − in favour. regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 is one of the first acts in the fisheries sector to be aligned to the new system of delegated and implementing acts. it is therefore of particular importance to find a legally-well-founded solution safeguarding parliament’s rights created by the treaty of lisbon. in the context of the alignment of regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 to the new rules of the tfeu, the commission has prepared a draft proposal classifying the powers currently conferred on the commission by that regulation into measures of a delegated nature and measures of an implementing nature. the changes proposed concern only the types of acts to be adopted and do not modify the content of the measures. the commission did not align the regulation in all its aspects to the tfeu but concentrated on the provisions in which direct reference was made to the old comitology procedure contained in council decision no 1999/468/ec, deciding in each case whether the measure should be adopted as a delegated or as an implementing act.

mr president, i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a lack of transparency is one of the conditions that has led to the crisis we are experiencing. this problem is not only reflected in the functioning of the financial system, which has been the subject of some serious scandals, but also in some supervisory bodies, such as the rating agencies. i think it is a good idea to extend to these organizations working conditions which are commonplace in companies auditing all kinds of accounts. these include preventing and limiting conflicts of interest, avoiding the dissemination of rating notes at critical moments, which may encourage speculation, and supplementing the rating results with information on the method and data used to produce the rating. but what i think is definitive is that the agencies should bear the consequences of their errors effectively in relation to third parties, including compensation for unfairly caused damage. i think that forecast is going to be what we call in english the "hand of a saint".
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents another missed opportunity to put an end once and for all to the influence these rating agencies have on the financing capacity of the member states of the european union. my position is clear on the creation of a public financial rating agency that would allow sovereign financing of the states and not a private rating system that would allow the creation of multimillion-dollar deals on sovereign debts to the detriment of the peoples of europe. at present, three rating agencies monitor the rating of these debts and allow a speculative game that only benefits the financial sector. a public agency would be a perfect solution to the problems that financial rating has created for europe's sovereign debts. this report is not intended to solve anything, and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. − while the new regulation will improve the transparency of ratings, in particular by supplementing the current rating system (e.g. aaa) with an additional system of figures requiring the inclusion of historical data to support the probability of default on debt, it is regrettable that the european parliament has not been more ambitious in its regulation. the greens put forward proposals to avoid cross-shareholding between qualified entities and agencies, but a limit of only 10% was set. the greens also wanted clearer regulation to limit the reliance of the rating agencies on the financial markets, but we did not get the necessary majority either. it is important to note that rating agencies will not be able to issue recommendations on public policies of states. the legislation also requires qualifications to take a broader view of risk, including, for example, environmental risk. parliament also called on the commission to consider the possibility of setting up a european public rating agency. this is a key factor for the greens in their attempt to put an end to the business of rating agencies.
in writing. - i regret that regulation has been so long delayed, as i have pointed out in many questions, and i would also have liked to see more detailed rules on the liability of these agencies, in line with the progress made by the case law of the court of justice in sydney and the practices of the us supervisory body, the securities and exchange commission (sec).
in writing. − with this reform of the credit rating agencies regulation, i think we are taking a step towards addressing one of the chief complains of our citizens since the crisis started. three issues are relevant in this context. firstly, with this regulation we aim to break the link between regulation and credit ratings, which has given too much power to the latter. secondly, it is good to have a clear calendar of the sovereign ratings of the agencies. thirdly, i support the idea that the commission will produce a report on a public rating agency, but i would like this to be a foundation with a public-private partnership, in order to enhance its credibility.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of this report because i believe that, although it seeks to improve the regulation of the activity of credit rating agencies, it means denying the possibility of a public rating agency and accepting private control of the sector. this report includes various technical amendments to improve control over rating agencies and to avoid speculative movements generated through their activity. all these technical provisions represent a positive step forward for the control of financial instruments which take advantage of rating changes to develop speculative movements which produce considerable profits for their holders at the expense of state financing. this technical control is ultimately the legitimization of the rating agencies and therefore, although i share the need for their regulation, i have voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report as it represents a step forward in the sustainable exploitation of cod stocks in the baltic sea. this species has gone from a situation of over-exploitation, which caused a sharp decline in its population, to an objective recovery that can allow its exploitation. as regards the technical details it develops, it provides for differentiated treatment between large and small fishermen who can now fish this species without a specific limit. the report also includes amendments limiting the delegation of powers to the commission so that it can only enjoy temporary delegations, as opposed to the indefinite ones previously provided for in the text. the measures adopted in this report are all intended to restore fishing for this species in a sustainable way, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i share the concern for the conservation of fishery resources. the report seeks to increase and establish viable technical criteria to enable the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources. articles relating to the different fishing gear permitted in european waters are amended to increase the requirements and protect juveniles of the different marine organisms which are the only guarantee of the regeneration of stocks. the report makes decision-making dependent on the scientific evaluation of marine stocks in order to have a tool to allow the modification of the gear in the light of an objective assessment of the state of the stocks. for all these reasons i considered this report important and therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the protection of our ecosystems is of the utmost priority for me. this protection of juveniles has to go. it is my belief, respecting the communities, that life in those areas is being affected and strict surveillance by the actors should be involved. the measure that we have decided to be applied should have a sound scientific base and be understood by all the stakeholders.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves a new regulation on the election of the vice-presidents of the chamber which may eventually allow minority groups to gain seats on the bureau. the voting rules for the election of the relevant important posts in parliament now require that minority groups need the support, or at least the complicity, of the majority of parliament. the report stipulates that when candidatures exceed the number of vacancies, voting will be by secret ballot, which may allow for a movement of votes towards candidates who may be considered more appropriate than those put forward by the majority groups in parliament. this report can improve the representation of minority groups on the bureau and that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, i support this report because i believe it is a decisive step towards the smart and cohesive growth advocated by strategy 2020. one of the values of the european social model has been the democratization of people's access to higher education. there are many young people with training who are a huge source of excellence, innovation and, consequently, the driving force for development and economic growth in europe. unfortunately, the crisis is closing the door to the world of work. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a good one. i would therefore like it to have a budget that is in line with its objectives and also to have its implementation not just a suggestion for the member states but an obligation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, as did the rest of my group, because it proposes the creation of an instrument to improve the situation of young europeans. the resolution proposes that the council establish a youth guarantee scheme to improve the chances of young people finding employment, recognising the very serious situation facing this segment of the population in the context of the economic crisis. the youth guarantee scheme would be financed through the european social fund to ensure an intervention strategy that would allow young people under the age of 25, or 30 if they have recently finished their studies, to receive a job offer or some form of training within 4 months. we believe that the creation of such a system is justified by the emergency situation of european youth and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. for there is an urgent need, a whole generation is being sacrificed on the altar of austerity, almost 14 million young people under 30 in europe are neither in employment nor in training. the cost of this marginalization is 150 billion euros a year for the european economy, whereas the implementation of the youth guarantee would cost only 21 billion! the youth guarantee, which the greens have been promoting for years, is a measure that is now working in denmark and austria. the french prime minister, jean-marc ayrault, committed himself at the great national conference against poverty to implement it quickly. i take note of this commitment, but i would remind you that the guarantee will only work if two conditions are met: the introduction of an income of autonomy, because too many young people are forced to work alongside their studies or training, which leads many of them to fail, and the introduction of strict rules to regulate the traineeships. the commission must act to put an end to the cynical exploitation of young workers, who are pursuing short-term contracts disguised as internships.
in writing. − spain has the highest youth unemployment rate (56.5% in september 2012 informs eurostat) of the eu. spanish governments have been unable to give a solution to this serious problem in years, that is why catalan people welcome this commission proposal with optimism and hope for a better future for our young people. although i am conscious of the different difficulties of the implementation of this measure, i will be following the application of the youth guarantee schemes in all member states, especially in spain. we will not let the spanish government play with the future of our sons and daughters anymore.
mr president, as the representative of a region, the basque country, with a high degree of industrial activity and therefore very sensitive to energy costs, i welcome with satisfaction this commitment to incorporate energy into cohesion policies. it is very timely to offer the regions the possibility of being more proactive in their energy diversification policies. unfortunately, the necessary reflection we are adopting today will not help to solve other urgent problems in the energy market which require immediate intervention. among them, the alteration of the rules of competition already produced by the legislation applying to indirect co2 emissions with a view to meeting the targets for reducing carbon emissions by 2020 would stand out. here, it is european legislation that creates a clear distortion, by considering state aid and the differences in budgetary availability between northern and southern countries. some energy-intensive sectors are beginning to feel the effects on their balance sheets and employment potential, undermining the investment and technological effort they have made in recent years to be able to take the lead in competitiveness in their sectors. i therefore call on the european parliament and the european commission to take action and find solutions to this serious energy problem.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of this report because it involves a process of energy integration in the union which includes the complete liberalisation of the sector. the focus of this report is on the use of cohesion policy to implement access to energy throughout the union and the modernisation of existing energy generation and heating systems. however, this improvement in the network is based on the complete liberalisation of the sector throughout europe and emphasising the importance of competitiveness in the sector. it is considerably vague with respect to permitted practices, allowing the exploitation of gas by hydraulic fracturing, highly damaging to the environment. energy is a vital sector for the european economy and leaving it to the private interests of certain business groups will mean the end of member states' energy policy and the submission to these private interests. that is why i voted against.
in writing. − against. the original draft report represented the particular interests of rapporteur kolarska-bobinska, in particular in its initial paragraph 12 that explicitly stated that ‘not only low-carbon, but all low-emission sources of energy, such as shale gas, ought to be accepted, including those of a transitional nature’. the explicit reference to shale gas was deleted at committee level. however, other important issues remained, making it impossible for us to vote in favour.
in writing. − the european union has been playing a leading role in the world on green energies and we have to ensure that it will continue doing it. boosting the public and private investment on green energies has to go hand in hand with scientific knowledge and economic criteria, thus making our investments economical and social truly in line with the 2020 strategy. without reasonably cheap energy our companies will not be competitive enough in the globalised world and thus will be facing unfair competition from third countries.
mr president, i want to support my group's position on this report and thank sylvie goulard for the effort she is making in coordinating this historic work. the difficulties of today will seem unbelievable tomorrow when we see how much we are better off by this firm and real step towards the real economic union we need. the union is legitimised in the eyes of its citizens when it demonstrates its capacity to improve their quality of life. today, this starts with offering solutions to the crisis, and this report gives a good measure of what we are lacking: a real monetary union, fiscal unity, discipline and loyalty between all the states and regions with their own treasuries - like the basque - to eliminate suspicions and make possible the eurobonds, which are one of the solutions against the attacks of the markets. it also stresses the need to legitimize this integration process in a democratic way and recalls that the joint responsibility we need is only possible under these conditions. i therefore support and will support all efforts in this direction.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a new missed opportunity to really tackle the crisis and is just another text along the lines of austerity. this type of economic policy is the real cause of the worsening of the effects of the financial crisis and its transfer to the real economy. the report welcomes the efforts of the member states in budgetary control and proposes debt-sharing figures, such as 'eurobills', but only accessible to non-participating states. spain will not be able to benefit from these instruments and will only be able to serve to increase the distance between northern europe and southern europe, which is suffering from the most serious financial problems. the report continues to defend competitiveness over the sovereignty of states and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the goulard report on the possibility of introducing eurobonds, in which parliament reiterates its commitment to the mutualisation of sovereign debt, pressing the commission and the council to introduce elements which will actually break the vicious circle between sovereign debt and private risk. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. ending speculation on the risk premium and interest rate of euro area public debt is crucial to getting out of the crisis. job creation, social justice and poverty eradication are not dependent on risk premium or agency rating, which are made on orthodox economic axioms. if we want a different kind of public policy, we need to limit the power of agencies, big financial lobbies, in determining european economic policy.
in writing. − i have supported this very good report of mrs goulard as i am of the opinion that it is time to put on the political agenda the issuance of some kind of common debt. the four steps that are envisaged in this report are quite sensible, particularly the issuance of eurobills and putting in place an european redemption fund that ties common issuance of debt to tight fiscal discipline. i hope that the commission is able to react in the coming months to this report with a new legislative proposal.
the next item is the debate on the statement by the vice-president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in syria [2013/2511 (rsp) ]. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president and distinguished members of the european parliament, permit me to update you, on behalf of high representative/vice-president catherine ashton, on the eu’s assessment of the situation in syria. i am sure that all of us here would agree that the political solution to the heart-wrenching and almost two-year long conflict in syria is not yet in sight. the political process that the eu and the international community have been supporting with true resolve has, unfortunately, not moved far enough as yet. conversely – and there are also no signs that the assad regime has moved in its own intransigence – we all witnessed the defiance of president assad in his unacceptable speech, as recognised by many of our supporters and joint special representative brahimi. from our side, the eu’s official statements remain unambiguous: there is no future for assad in the political future of syria. the eu has incessantly worked with all partners on the bilateral, multilateral and interinstitutional levels to address the whole array of pressing issues. political efforts continue, and there is no need to recall all of the daily diplomacy that operates in brussels as well as in european and world capitals. from our side, we can count the most recent statement of the high representative on assad’s speech, the european council and fac conclusions of december that covered very broad areas of our approach to the syrian tragedy. we must also mention the extension of the sanctions regime, official recognition of the syrian coalition of revolutionary and opposition forces as legitimate representatives of the syrian people, or support to the third committee, as well unhrc resolutions. and we will keep on examining if further sanctions can be adopted in order to put pressure on the regime. the eu commends and continues to support the mission of mr brahimi. his perseverance in reaching a workable solution over the last months has earned him much deserved respect. we do hope that within the international community we are nearing a compromise on how to best assist syria’s future. here we will be watching very closely a report from mr brahimi that he will present to the un security council on 29 january. he could not attend the foreign affairs council in january, but we have invited him to the fac in february. at the same time, the eu has managed to reinforce actions addressing the challenges faced at present by the syrian population. they range from the increasing flow of hundreds of thousands of refugees into the syrian neighbourhood countries during an extraordinarily harsh winter and continuing massive internal displacement of millions of syrians to possible chemical incident scenarios and the consolidation of the opposition. the european council tasked the foreign affairs council to work on all options to support and help the opposition and to enable greater support for the protection of civilians. this issue will be tackled at the next foreign affairs council on 31 january. although financial assistance is only part of the solution, it does help in easing some of these challenges. since the last debate here in the european parliament, the eu has almost doubled all types of assistance in and outside syria. today, over eur 500 million (of which over eur 350 million is in humanitarian aid) go to long-term actions on supporting refugees, syrian youth and the general population particularly affected by the unrest, including skills, education and mentoring for refugees. the eu is also funding activities, such as the regional protection programme, aimed at building up the resilience of displaced syrian people as well as enhancing the capacity of communities which host them in neighbouring countries. more, of course, is certainly needed, and improved channels of delivery will have to be devised, given harsher weather conditions descending on refugees and internally-displaced syrians. i would like to particularly commend the work done in this field by commissioner georgieva and her staff. our efforts also try to prepare for the day after and the transition, which will include financial assistance to support political transition, institutional and economic recovery as well as support to the population and post-conflict accountability. the eu is also preparing preventive measures in case of a potential chemical weapon incident. at the moment the focus is more on the trans-border element of this threat, on which we cooperate closely with syria’s neighbours such as jordan and turkey. in all of our financial interventions, the eu uses a four-pronged approach. it includes ongoing support to the multilateral institutions such as the un and ingos and civil society organisations, alongside just-being-rolled-out support of local syrian ngos and civilian structures together with structured support for the opposition. as you know, the eu co-chairs the un humanitarian forum and chairs the donor coordination work within the friends of syria working group on economic recovery. we are working with our partners to improve channels of our delivery, planning and gap analysis. the eu will also participate in the donor conference initiated by the un secretary-general ban ki-moon and hosted by the kuwaiti emir on 30 january. while on one side we work towards a political solution, on the other we do not lose sight of the human dimension of the syrian tragedy that has unfolded in the past two years. it has resulted in over 60 000 dead, 2.5 million internally displaced syrians and 500 000 refugees; numbers which, unfortunately, are rising as we speak. as commissioner georgieva will tell you later, we are working tirelessly every day to alleviate the suffering of the syrian people. but we all agree that such a tragedy cannot go on without more action and initiatives. i know that some of you are of the opinion that today, more direct military assistance to the opposition should be envisaged. but such an option is still very divisive and runs the risk of hardening the conflict. this is why, in spite of all the difficulties and the doubts on the shortcomings, we must remain determined to keep the course, by supporting mr brahimi’s efforts, assisting the opposition and relentlessly calling for the syrian leadership to face up to reality in the country and at last put an end to all violence.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, madam minister, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the truth is that the horror being experienced in syria has exceeded all limits. yesterday, 90 students taking their exams at the university of aleppo added to the unbearable figure of 60 000 people referred to by the presidency, and i would like to take this opportunity to express my best wishes to them for their semester. she herself has reminded us of the facts of this tragedy: five hundred thousand refugees in neighbouring countries, two million and a half thousand internally displaced persons in syria and absolutely intolerable damage to infrastructure and housing. we were told that bashar al-assad would fall sooner or later, that it was a matter of time. that fall hasn't happened yet. and we were also told that, with russia's involvement, russia would eventually give up its positions in the security council. the truth is that russia's position has been a complete chimera and it must answer to the international community for the attitude it is maintaining in the face of this situation. the special envoy of the un secretary-general and the arab league met last friday in geneva with the deputy secretaries of the united states and russia. 'by the way, mr president, i have not seen any reference to this and i do not know whether there were representatives of the european union; they have certainly not appeared in the reports or in the media.' this week mr brahimi is in egypt and he has said that the situation is not only bad, very bad, but that it is likely to get worse and that if this conflict were to continue for another year it would result in 100,000 more deaths than the 60,000 that have already occurred. and he has said that either the legitimate demands of the syrian people are met or the situation in syria is going to turn into a hell as if they are not already living in hell. and in the face of this situation, the international community is acting as if it's doing something, following a really tragic script. that is, as long as the conflict does not go beyond the syrian national sphere - and there are obviously risks of it being projected onto the whole region - and as long as chemical weapons are not used - and again we must applaud the courage and determination of france, whose president has made very forceful statements in this regard - time is still being gained to see whether assad finally succeeds in crushing the opponents, which also does not seem likely, or to see whether the opposition coordinates, organizes and, indeed, the fall of the regime actually occurs. in view of this situation, mr president, the international community must take a decision. we had a very interesting debate yesterday on mali, a conflict which has, indeed, very significant negative potentials, and the international community has been able to take decisions. in this house, on all the occasions when we have discussed this matter, we have spoken of the french initiative for a humanitarian corridor and we have spoken of the possibility of establishing a no-fly zone, which naturally requires a certain unanimity in the united nations security council. but what is clear is that progress must be made in this situation. and it is also clear, mr president, that this conflict has a humanitarian dimension. and i would particularly like to thank mrs georgieva for her efforts in this regard. but let's not kid ourselves. the citizens of the european union are not only looking to the european union to respond to the serious humanitarian crisis that this conflict is producing. what they are hoping for is that we will be able to stop this bloodbath, that we will be able to arbitrate measures that can really end this shameful situation and that we will be able to rise to the occasion, which demands that in these conditions and at this moment the international community in general, and the european union in particular, be able to put an end to the terrible suffering, mr president, that the syrian people are suffering.
member of the commission. − mr president, let me start with where the humanitarian crisis in syria is heading: unfortunately, from bad to worse, and with the worst still to come. we have seen in the last weeks a very significant deterioration in conditions in syria, because of the combined impact of three factors. first, intensified fighting; second, economic conditions are now catastrophic; and third, the winter this year is, unfortunately, fierce and is affecting people dramatically. regarding the fighting: not only has it intensified, but more often than not, atrocities are being carried out. while the assad regime carries the vast majority of the blame, atrocities are also carried out by the other side, and that makes conditions for the delivery of humanitarian aid particularly difficult. second, what is now hitting people as well are factors like increase of fuel and food prices, and lack of food. we are now faced with starvation in the places with the most severe fighting like aleppo, idlib, hama and homs. in these conditions, we are doing all we can to get help to people, and i want to particularly address the comments that have been made by ms flautre on how exactly european assistance works in syria. from the very early days of the crisis we have engaged in three ways as the leading funder, as the one donor that has a presence on the ground, and also with very active humanitarian advocacy through the syrian humanitarian forum that has met seven times, by time and again pursuing – including with the opposition – our fight for respect for international humanitarian law, so that people at least do not die because of ignorance of the existence of this law. because of our engagement, we have moved access to affected syrian populations quite dramatically forward. in the beginning, assad would allow only the icrc inside syria. our relentless advocacy led to eight international ngos, seven of which are european, now operating inside syria and also to over 90 civil society organisations, mostly community organisations, to be allowed to be the delivery mechanism for humanitarian aid in addition to the syrian red crescent. true, left to assad, he would have liked the syrian red crescent to be the only vehicle, but we have moved way beyond this point and today one out of every three syrians gets help because of what we do, what we fund (the numbers have been spelled out), but also what we do to provide more space for humanitarian workers. we are engaging with the opposition. we have had a series of meetings with the aid arm of the opposition based in cairo, and i can assure you that we are pursuing every possible channel to get help to people inside as well as to the refugees, whose numbers are growing. i have visited the region twice. it is heartbreaking to see what is happening. i recall talking to a young girl from syria, now a refugee in jordan, who has not been to school for two years, and i am thinking of the lives that have been shattered, not only the people who died but those whose future is being buried by this conflict. the education system in syria is gone. over 700 schools are now home to internally-displaced people. the health system of syria is gone. not only do the wounded not get help, but immunisation and vaccination has practically stopped. so yes, we are facing a grave humanitarian crisis, and it is absolutely paramount that we work hard. for the only way for this crisis to end is, unfortunately, not in the hands of humanitarians, it is in the hands of politicians. some have spoken here for in favour of a military option. we have been in the libya crisis, and i can tell you that syria is not libya. syria is much better militarily. when i talk to people in the region, they tell me that, if there was military action, they fear that would lead to the unleashing of chemical weapons, with much graver humanitarian consequences than we currently have. so a military solution is not going to deliver results of a kind that would make things better. it is the political solution that we all have to raise our voices to urge for. i want to finish by saying that we have also been in the lead to make sure that there will be a very high level of attention paid to the humanitarian crisis. the secretary-general will chair a meeting that the emir of kuwait will host on 30 january. we, the eu, have been a strong voice for this meeting to take place, because the needs require funding of a magnitude that is not yet there, with the exception of us. for the honour of our member states: 23 out of 27 have contributed generously to help the syrian people. we have called on our civil protection mechanism twice. eight of our member states have delivered in-kind assistance to turkey and jordan, and i know that if we called on them again, they would be there. but we need everybody to step up to the plate because, unfortunately, the political solution that is the only way forward is not yet in sight, and i fear that means terrible suffering for millions of syrian people and a terrible risk of a spillover impact for the whole neighbourhood. i want to assure this house that the humanitarian team of the commission has been engaged. people are risking their lives. i have a staff member that has been shot at. of the humanitarian community, 15 people have died and many more have been wounded. we are persevering, we are carrying the commitment of europe towards the suffering of innocent people with our greatest possible commitment.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i would like to firstly thank all members for the very constructive interventions. i think that we all share a genuine concern and a deep sense of urgency in trying to address this horrendous situation which i think has been very well outlined by the commissioner. it will require the determination and the cooperation of all of the institutions of the european union and indeed of all of the international community to find ultimately a political solution, as the commissioner has said. in my remarks, i wish to respond to some of the points raised in the questions asked and i apologise if i miss anybody or any point which has been raised. i want to begin by agreeing with the condemnation of the atrocity in the university in aleppo yesterday. i am sure that everybody in this house shares in that condemnation. i also agree with mr salafranca about the potential catastrophe, loss of life and deepening humanitarian crisis if this conflict continues indefinitely into the future and that is why we must redouble our efforts. specifically in response to the question about the talks in geneva and the tripartite meeting which took place: the eu was not there. this was the second meeting between mr brahimi, the us and russia and it was mr brahimi’s plan to keep that particular forum, that particular dialogue between the three; and we understand that. however, we are in constant contact and communication of course with him and his team. we are constantly updated and informed as to the progress that he is making and the discussions and dialogue which he has. it is of course the commitment of the eu to be fully engaged in every possible form where there is an opportunity to contribute. in answer to ms de keyser, the eu is participating in all efforts relating to accountability both in geneva and in new york and that will continue to be the case. a number of points were raised by ms schaake and ms flautre. we are all aware of the shortcomings of our combined efforts, whether on the diplomatic or humanitarian front. it is not a perfect process, that is for sure, but the situation i think cannot just be simplified as sometimes it is easy to do. we need to look into all the possible options, all aspects and all opportunities for cooperation with ngos, as commissioner georgieva has pointed out, and the different civilian organisations to see how we can help them, how we can best support them, how we can ensure that humanitarian aid meets the target which have been set out by members and indeed by the commissioner, which is civilians who are suffering for a variety of reasons not least the deteriorating weather conditions. we are acting with each of them in a very concrete way, in a very coordinated way. we are doing everything that we can to support them on the ground. that commitment, that determination and in practice those steps are being taken by the eu and will continue to be. in summary, i would like to say that the cooperation between the european parliament and the institutions is extremely important in order to carry forward the day to day work on the humanitarian front and indeed on the political front. we have to provide every possible opportunity to provide support, to help the opposition and to enable better protection for civilians; and that is, i think, an immediate and very pressing priority. we will be focusing on finding better ways to make our efforts more effective. there will be an opportunity to review the sanctions and the very steps that have been taken at the next foreign affairs council. intensive regional cooperation efforts are also underway to ensure that the spill-over effects from the syrian conflict is contained. this was mentioned by a number of members but i will not name everybody. we will do everything we can to contain that and to ensure that there is no further destabilisation of what is, i think we can all acknowledge, an extremely volatile region.

the next item is the joint debate on - the report by mr mario mauro, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an association and cooperation agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of iraq, of the other part (10209/2012 - c7-0189/2012 - 2010/0310 (nle)) (a7-0411/2012), and - the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. the declaration will be presented by mrs creighton, president-in-office of the council, in the absence of mrs ashton, and mr mauro will be replaced by mr salafranca sánchez-neyra in presenting the recommendation.

council of ministers which will deal with this important subject tomorrow. i would like to pass on to you, mr president, the reflections which i would like to share with the rest of the house on behalf of the rapporteur for this report, mr mauro. firstly, this agreement represents the first contractual relationship between the european union and iraq, not only in the commercial field but also in many other fields, and its purpose is to consolidate relations between the two countries. the agreement devotes a major chapter to cooperation activities in the fields of health, education, the fight against poverty, the promotion of transparency and effective governance. as regards trade aspects, this agreement, which is not a preferential agreement, incorporates the basic principles of the world trade organisation, of which iraq is not a member, and some of the clauses have a strong connotation relating to important political issues: the fight against weapons of mass destruction, the fight against terrorism and drug trafficking, the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms, especially of ethnic and religious minorities, which are the most exposed to risks in this region. this resolution, mr president, pays particular attention to human rights and the participation of women in post-conflict reconstruction processes and at the highest levels of political and economic life, and calls on the iraqi authorities to take the necessary steps to develop a civil society which can play an important role in the political process. it also called for measures to stimulate the emergence of an independent, pluralistic and professional media sector and advocated that the european union should support iraq's national reconciliation on the basis of a political dialogue that excludes no one. it called on the iraqi government to respond to the concerns about respect for human rights, which have been expressed continuously through measures to support the work of the high commissioner for human rights and giving priority to the fight against impunity and to the reform of the law and the judicial system. the fact that a resolution on the future of iraq and its relations with the european union has been added to the draft recommendation on the agreement is due to the fact that iraq is now at a critical stage. this phase, which has been marked by the withdrawal of american troops, began some years ago and is precisely at the moment of the country's democratic transition towards the creation of a coalition government which takes account of the agreement reached between the various political forces in iraq. in this context, the european union cannot fail to play its part and to provide the necessary support to the iraqi authorities in order to contribute to the reconstruction and development of the country, to national security and stability, to overcoming the humanitarian emergency and to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that it is important for the european union to make a strategic commitment to the future of iraq. this association and cooperation agreement is a very important signal in this direction, but nevertheless this road is long and i am convinced that the european union must live up to its ambitions and, of course, this resolution is clearly intended to serve to support that purpose.
