in writing. − in favour. articles 1 and 2 outline the scope and subject matter of the directive. here, an effort has been made to ensure that the aim of complete coverage for consumer disputes is achieved, while offering consumers a high-quality, transparent, effective and fair redress mechanism. both existing and newly-established dispute resolution mechanisms that comply with the minimum quality standards established by this directive will be called ‘adr entities’ and will subsequently be provided with a european quality label that will boost consumers’ confidence and trust. the possibility of traders submitting disputes against consumers has been excluded, as traders already have sufficient means to resolve these claims without being included in the scope of adr.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it provides new elements for the development of association agreements which are not merely economic agreements. among the new elements mentioned are cooperation in strengthening civil society and its responsibility in all areas, the inclusion of the overseas countries and territories (octs) in the european union's horizontal and environmental programmes, the inclusion of the objective of improving labour and trade union rights, and the recognition of public investment as the only way to improve living conditions in both the octs and europe, etc. in short, the report allows the development of economic, social and cultural rights through the implementation of these association agreements with the octs. these are agreements based on international solidarity between peoples and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in favour. as my colleague, mr bicep, has already said, in the tense context of the 2014-2020 budget negotiations, the process of revising this association decision must not be affected by national frictions. today the european parliament has shown its progressive face by welcoming the commission's proposal and going further, in particular by focusing on sustainable management of natural resources, the promotion of renewable energy, investment in employment and a relentless fight against tax havens. the absolute priority of this new association must be the ecological transition, in the name of a social and solidarity-based economy for territories which often suffer from a high economic dependence on their neighbouring states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to ban all radioactive substances from water intended for human consumption. the report amends the previous directive on prohibited radioactive substances. it is a report designed to fill a gap in the legislation. the substances which were not included were radon gas and tritium gas. these substances were not present in the legislation and the commission put forward a proposal to parliament in which missing points have been supplemented, such as the establishment of minimum acceptable doses for adult population rather than for critical population such as children or the elderly. the report includes detailed regulation and offers full protection for european citizens against such substances. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the rivasi report provides for greater prevention measures to prevent our waters from being contaminated with radioactive particles. the first step to achieve this is to change the legal basis of this report in the treaties. the second step, a very important advance, is to establish more stringent controls on the parameters of the studies on radioactivity in water. the aim must therefore be to protect the population by constant monitoring, by means of studies and repeated supervision of the dangers of water contaminated with radioactive substances. however, the european commission needs to go further and force member states to fully implement the water for human consumption directive and also extend preventive measures. i shall vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. radioactive contamination of drinking water can occur due to human activities (accidental releases of radioactivity or improper disposal practices) or naturally. so far, radioactive contamination of drinking water has not been adequately monitored or remedied. the quality of drinking water is currently regulated under the council’s drinking water directive 98/83/ec (dwd), including the monitoring of radionuclides. however, the dwd requirements for monitoring the frequency of the radioactive substance tritium and the total indicative dose (effective dose for one year of ingestion resulting from all radionuclides detected in drinking water) are still not implemented (even though member states have had to comply with the dwd since the end of 2013).
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a further step in the economic sacrifice of the member states in the name of austerity. this report covers the implementation of the two-pack to develop the tools for monitoring the national budgets of the member states. the report is based on the principle that austerity policy should be imposed on all countries, but with special emphasis on those countries which are experiencing budgetary difficulties. the report aims to extend the monitoring and control of government deficits to countries outside the euro area and argues that the countries involved should take account of the commission's recommendations. the report therefore turns the tables on the loss of sovereignty by the states to the financial sector. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. - i abstained from voting. the most relevant aspect of this report to me - and indeed the one that has prevented me from voting against it - is the introduction of the need for public debt audits in those countries which are subject to macroeconomic programmes. in the case of spain, however, i think that its delicate situation must also be taken into account.
in writing. − both documents in the two-pack proposal represent a step forward for monetary union. in particular, this regulation leaves the commission the possibility of enhanced surveillance of a member state experiencing serious financing difficulties. on the other hand, for the countries receiving certain types of precautionary financial assistance, this surveillance will be automatically applied and a list of precautionary assistance instruments will be established. these measures will contribute to prevent some of the ongoing situations in the eu zone; therefore i fully support the agreement.
madam president, the basque country, the nation i am here representing, is almost a state for tax purposes. we have our own treasury and we answer for our public accounts and our deficit. in the last 30 years, after the franco dictatorship, we recovered our estates. we have made a tremendous effort to put economic policies in place which have given rise to a development model which is totally different from the one which has failed in spain. we've boosted the productive tissue. in euskadi, neither construction nor speculation is the basis of our growth. european tests say that our financial system is sound and solvent. we agree with the principle of financial supervision, but if the luxembourg court of justice believes that our economic concert is an autonomous treasury, we want direct european supervision of our accounts. and we want tax harmonization, so that we are not penalized for applying the same tax measures that some member states adopt without reproach. the effort of our citizens to prosper, to do so seriously and by fighting with work the scourge that was for years the intolerable violence of eta deserves this consideration.
in writing. - i voted against this report because austerity has proved to be no way out of the economic crisis europe is going through. putting the reduction of sovereign debt at the centre of member states' economic policy can only hold back the economic growth potential of countries in budgetary difficulties. this report implements the measures adopted in recent years on the control of the member states' budgets. the report argues that austerity in public accounts leads directly to economic growth when the reality in many member states is proving, day after day, just the opposite. to introduce a legislative amendment which goes against the reality that is intended to be legislated can only be called madness. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted against it. it was a good opportunity to at least allow the governments of some countries to implement countercyclical policies. they haven't. in addition, governments and the commission have greatly watered down the possibility of mutualising the debt.
in writing. − both documents in the two-pack proposal represent a step forward for monetary union. among other measures, this report promotes monitoring of the common budgetary rules by independent institutions. although euro-area member states have to submit their draft budgetary plan for the following year, they will remain fully sovereign in voting on their budgets. an opinion will be given by the commission, with the possibility of being penalised with a 0.3 % gdp fine if the member state does not follow the indications or does not comply with the objectives. therefore, this regulation complements the preventive arm of the stability and growth pack, by ensuring that eu policy recommendations are integrated appropriately into national budgetary preparations and increasing peer pressure in the euro area. for all the reasons above, i fully support the agreement.

in writing. - the social problems of our societies have been accentuated by the current financial crisis. it is therefore necessary to encourage investments which give priority to the achievement of social objectives in the interests of financial return. in recent years, we have seen the emergence of a social investment market that helps to address the social consequences of the crisis by providing finance for social enterprises. in practice, most smes have social objectives and obtain a large part of their funding through donations or funds from the public sector. their activities depend on stable sources of funding which are adapted to their needs. evidence shows that regulatory requirements at european and national level do not guarantee the raising of social entrepreneurship funds. i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal to establish a common regulatory framework on the use of the designation of a european social entrepreneurship fund.

in writing. − the world conference on women in 1995 had as one of its main demands the removal of obstacles to the active participation of women in all spheres of public and private life through full and equal participation in economic, social, cultural and political life. it is enough to mark international women's day and the data show how much this issue and many others are still valid and therefore i supported the report on 'eliminating gender stereotypes in the eu'. mandatory quotas are needed to increase the number of women in legislative and business leadership positions . it is also necessary to support the creation of a fund to promote equal measures for women's equality and, above all, to combat violence against women. the work/life balance remains a major problem for many women in the eu. the labour market participation rate for mothers is 12% lower than for women without children, while the rate for fathers is 8.7% higher than for men without children. it is also essential to reduce the wage gap. it is therefore imperative that the european parliament should approve any measure which can contribute, such as this report, to achieving real equality for women.

in writing. − in favour. the adopted envi report practically overwrites the draft report by oreste rossi (efd, it), turning a plea for subsidiarity and regionalisation into a welcoming of the commission communication. the report notes that much of the unnecessary administrative costs linked to environmental legislation are due to inadequate or inefficient public and private administrative practices in various member states and in their regional or local authorities. it emphasises the importance of timely and correct implementation (transposition) of eu law by the member states and regional and local authorities, also with a view to ensuring a level playing field. the report regrets that the procedure for a directive on public access to justice in environmental matters has been halted at first reading and calls on the co-legislators to reconsider their positions with a view to breaking the deadlock. it also notes the frequent concerns of petitioners in several areas of environmental policy, such as landfill and waste disposal, wildlife habitats and air and water quality, and applauds their efforts to bring authority to account. underlining the crucial importance of effective inspections, the report urges the member states to step up their inspection capacities, calls for common minimum criteria for inspections and urges the commission to set up an environmental law inspection unit.
member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, i would like to apologize for the delay. the flight from brussels was delayed by over four hours. i'm happy to be with you. i would first like to thank you for your involvement since the beginning of the process of reform of the common agricultural policy. i would like to thank in particular the rapporteurs, mr capoulas santos, mr dantin, mr la via, and all the fictitious rapporteurs who have been involved in the proposals for regulations under discussion today. this step of determining your negotiating mandate is crucial to be able to actively enter the second phase of negotiation of an agreement between the european parliament, the council and the commission. this is not the end of the road, it is only the beginning of the political negotiation phase towards an agreement on a reformed, ambitious and pragmatic common agricultural policy which i hope we will be able to reach together by next june. there are still some points which will have to be clarified between us, the commission, parliament and the council, at the trilogues which i hope will follow very soon. however, i think we agree on the basic principles, which allows us to look forward to the next phase of the negotiations between the three institutions under good conditions. the issue of fairness and distribution of support to farmers will be one of the key topics of the final discussion phase. many of you have already been very active in supporting the capping of direct aid or the rebalancing of support between member states. the notions of active farmers, degressivity of aid and internal convergence of aid to farmers are essential to better target public expenditure. that is why i support the idea of an absolute minimum objective of internal convergence, as has been done for external convergence. aid convergence must not remain a concept but must become a tangible reality by 2019, with concrete ambition. this development must be accompanied by a complementary tool to meet agricultural realities and societal expectations. i'll give you three examples. the establishment of young farmers is a european challenge and therefore requires a european approach and not a national option. the commission has proposed a compulsory measure for all member states on this issue, since we need a european approach and not an optional one at the choice of the member states. small and medium-sized farms are part of our food model and economic fabric. a simplified scheme for very small farms is important, both for the administrative simplification for the benefit of the beneficiaries and the administrations, but also for clear support for this category of farms. i am also in favour of the idea of a premium for the first hectares, which is also going in the same direction. we must also provide the means to maintain agriculture throughout our territories in the less-favoured areas. of course, all this must be done in the context of the most impeccable management possible in terms of the quality of public expenditure. in recent months we have worked together a great deal on these issues. i particularly support the idea of a rapid suspension of reimbursements to member states when serious management and control problems are detected and not dealt with properly. greening is a means of enhancing the production of public goods. it also reflects the economic dimension of soil fertility and biodiversity. it is also a tool to combat climate change. this development of the common agricultural policy is therefore necessary both for the proper management of natural resources and for farmers and their economic competitiveness in the medium and long term, since this competitiveness is also linked to soil fertility and water quality. we must not give in to the temptation of so-called greenwashing or approximate measures which would have a questionable effect, would be very complex and would result in unacceptable error rates, also in the quality control of public expenditure. however, i agree with the principle of equivalence between certain agri-environmental practices and the three proposed greening measures under three conditions: if the alternative measures are equally effective and more relevant locally, if the system remains simple to apply and simple to control and if all farmers or, in any case, all agricultural areas in the european union are involved. in order to use taxpayers' money effectively, it seems to me important that greening measures should be the basis for the second pillar agri-environmental measures and that 7% of the ecological focus areas should also act as stabilizers of agricultural ecosystems, which is synonymous with productivity and long-term competitiveness. i would add that, in order to affect all farmers, greening must include a credible system of penalties that goes beyond the 30% loss. this is the system of penalties applied to all other measures financed under the first pillar. in parallel, the position of agriculture in the economy and the territories must also be strengthened, first of all at the structural level. we have proposed measures to encourage producer organisations, inter-branch organisations and the short-term marketing system to improve the competitiveness of the sectors and the added value for farmers. in this respect, moreover, the competition rules need to be clarified. we know that not everything is possible or desirable in this area, but i would like to mention one particular issue on which we will have to continue to work, namely: what measures must be taken to ensure that the peak of the crisis is managed more and more effectively, or even avoided, in the common interest of limiting the negative economic impact on the agricultural sector and making better use of the public budget? in addition, we must keep a reserve for adverse economic situations. private storage and public intervention measures must be supplemented by the crisis reserve and emergency measures. in a crisis we must be more reactive in the immediate and not debate the most relevant legal basis, as is too often the case today in crisis situations. that is why we need reactive measures, so that we can react quickly. it is also appropriate to make available to member states and farmers, under the second pillar, an income stabilisation tool. the end of sugar quotas also fits into this context. the sugar quotas we have at present do not meet the current economic challenges. the same applies to the wine sector. the high level group on plantation rights has outlined the future paths around a concept of authorization of plantation rights. we therefore remain within a framework of monitoring what is happening in this sector, but we also need to move towards a system more adapted to the current situation. the aim is to pave the way for a new distribution of roles between public authorities and private actors in the management of markets, without going back to administrative management, but by adopting flexible, efficient and pragmatic market regulation, in line with the reality of today's markets. finally, i would like to return to the question of the transparency of financial support provided through the common agricultural policy. this transparency is the basis of trust for taxpayers. we must inform the citizens about the use of community money if we want the common agricultural policy to be a genuine, strong and sustainable partnership between europe, the european taxpayer and agriculture. i thank you for the work already done. i shall be attentive to the discussions we will have today, with the aim of moving in a balanced way in three directions: supporting competitive agricultural production, sustainable agricultural production and agricultural production for the employment and development of our territories. i very much hope that the debate we have today will lead to a vote on a negotiating mandate for parliament so that we can start negotiations between the council, parliament and the commission as soon as possible, stressing once again that what you will vote on tomorrow is only the beginning of the negotiating process. we will probably have the opportunity to continue the dialogue by june, i hope, just as i hope to obtain a political agreement on this reform.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the cap is not only a good thing for the environment but also a good thing for the environment. the proposal made by the european commission did not take into account the diversity of european agriculture or the need to establish flexible instruments to adapt to the different realities that exist in the european union. i think that the committee on agriculture has done a good job, with commitments which were fundamental, such as the flexibility of greening. it is essential that our producers can comply with these measures; there is no greater danger to the environment than an abandoned rural environment. coupled payments are also important to ensure support for sectors in crisis. it is necessary to delimit the number of hectares for cases such as spain, where we have a problem with this reform that is being proposed. it is essential to maintain sugar quotas until 2020 and vine planting rights until 2030, to reintroduce the milk quota, to strengthen producer organisations and to be able to harmonise competition rules. we have in our hands the future of farming and livestock farming in the european union. let us remember that this is a mandate, that there is a long way to go to negotiate with the council and that we are playing with the future of millions of people living in our rural environment. i would like to thank the rapporteurs for their work and the contribution of all those who have made it possible in the committee on agriculture.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we are faced with one of the hallmarks of europe, one of the basic pillars of the european construction. it is therefore regrettable that the whole common agricultural policy should come to the house in such an open way. we have only to look at the number of amendments we are going to have to vote on tomorrow to conclude that the terms of this reform should have been reviewed by the committee responsible. i understand that mature matters should be brought to the plenary, if necessary with a few fringes, but not with all or almost all the material completely raw. from my position as a non-attached member, i would have liked the political groups to have reached more consistent agreements. what a shame. it is a pity that this will weigh on the relevance of the whole reform, and a pity that parliament has missed this first opportunity, this first opportunity, to make a structural reform.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteurs and the alternate rapporteurs on the intensive work they have done and on the agreements reached in the committee on agriculture. for my country, spain, the initial proposals of the college of commissioners penalized the most competitive sectors and those professionals, such as farmers, who have to bear the most production costs. my colleagues from southern europe and i have been very keen to explain the serious problems of implementation of the community's proposal in mediterranean sectors such as olive oil and landless livestock farming, and i am pleased to say that we have been heard. i shall now be following very closely the discussions in the tripartite dialogue on a subject which has not yet been discussed: the future of the wine sector. we have not had the opportunity in the committee on agriculture to discuss the ideas which have begun to emerge from the european commission to replace the present system of vine planting rights. this sector is currently one of the few in the process of growth; it would be unfortunate if, at a time like the present, we decided to destroy a production management system which is bearing fruit. parliament must advocate the maintenance, beyond 2018, of an effective vineyard management system such as the present one, otherwise we would be throwing away the efforts made in recent years by european producers to improve the quality of their wines and to penetrate new markets in third countries.
mr president, mr commissioner, the commitments of the committee on agriculture have taken account of many of the demands of the spanish agricultural sector, and that is a matter of satisfaction, as is the fact that the initial proposal of the european commission, which was certainly negative, has been softened. but that is not enough: we need - and i am asking for it at the moment - the support of the house for the amendment we have tabled which allows the area eligible for aid to be limited. if this does not happen, the eligible area in spain could increase by 90% from 22 to 38 million hectares, leading to traumatic adjustments in key sectors. we are also committed to maintaining the milk quota system until 2020 on a smooth path towards liberalization and, of course, we strongly support the cultivation of tobacco, which is very important for regions such as extremadura or the canary islands. and speaking of the canary islands, i cannot help but remind the commissioner, whose sensibilities i am aware of, that the commitment to the outermost regions must be a permanent commitment, as are their circumstances, and that any change in their status must always be decided by consensus and moderation.
we are faced with a historic opportunity to adopt an ambitious cap that supports agricultural and livestock activities. agriculture, in addition to producing food, has a social, environmental and territorial function. in galicia we have 70,000 hectares of permanent pasture linked to the land-based production system. this reform must maintain the public intervention systems and, in the event of the end of quotas, achieve a milk fund to compensate the sector if they finally disappear. we want to adopt a fair cap that pays for the work and guarantees the production costs of farmers. we want to approve the best possible redistribution of direct aid from the cap, which cannot be separated from agricultural activity and must be directed at all farmers in the sector, with the amount linked to employment, the territory and the value of income. this parliament must support a fair, green and local cap linked to the territory. the countryside needs a future opportunity.

the next item is the debate on the report by sharon bowles, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european system of national and regional accounts in the european union (com (2010) 0774 c7-0010/2011 2010/0374 (cod)) (a7-0076/2012).
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i support the work of the rapporteur, sharon bowles, as well as that of the alternative rapporteurs, particularly that of edward scicluna, whom i am replacing today and whom i congratulate on his election to the national parliament of malta. statistics are essential for the proper functioning of democracy and the economy. they contribute to improving public debate, the conditions under which economic operators operate and economic governance. we need quality statistics, which provide independent, reliable, comparable and timely data, which are obtained by sound methods and transmitted according to a precise timetable. the european system of national and regional accounts was established in 1970 and is now governed by a 1996 regulation. it has been established in line with the system of national accounts developed by the united nations. this initiative adapts the system to the 2009 revision of the international system of national accounts by the united nations statistical commission. the new system should support the strengthening of european governance and the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. the amendments seek to provide more complete data while safeguarding confidentiality where appropriate. they stress the need for more methodological work on environmental externalities and social inequalities, as well as on research and development. they also promote regional accounts with a common nomenclature for cohesion policies, the analysis of economic interdependencies and compliance with the budgetary framework directive, address the treatment of contingent liabilities and insist on coordination of pension sustainability. the s&d group therefore welcomes the agreement reached at first reading and expects the commission to develop this regulation and to submit the reports required by it.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, this report is important because it is one of the few in which the commission has considered the importance of the regional level in the european union. i think that the commission should be more involved in regional statistics, in order to have a clearer picture of what happens in member states. in spain, for example, there is no transparency law. citizens cannot know the territorial distribution of public expenditure by the spanish central government. there is also no territorial information about tax collection, which remains centralised. this lack of transparency of the spanish state is one of the main reasons now fuelling pro-sovereignty feelings in catalonia. this is why i, in particular, welcome the annex to this regulation. the annex reflects that there should be an analysis of the inter-dependence of regions and member states. that is why the liberal group will support this report. we wish to thank the rapporteur, sharon bowles, and all the meps, for their good work.
member of the commission. − mr president, maybe just a few explanations, because ms bowles mentioned contingent liabilities, on which parliament was especially active. we are achieving very good progress on the six pack, covering contingent liabilities. the eurostat task force report on contingent liabilities was presented to the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ), which gave the report its strong support. the collection of this data – on public private partnerships, debts of public corporations and government guarantees – will be institutionalised while excessive deficit questionnaires with annual, monthly and quarterly data will be available in 2014. data on pensions will be available in accordance with the provisions of the draft esa regulation – with this being optional for 2012 and compulsory starting from 2015 – on a three-year basis and, finally, the commission is ready to present a report to the econ committee, upon request. it was also said that this is maybe a dull file. i was myself for many years a member of the governing board of the statistical office of slovenia – by the way, my phd was based on social national accounts – and i have probably heard esa 95 mentioned as many times as anybody here. i can only say that no important and substantial decisions are possible without hard statistical work and long methodological discussions, and i have learnt that the esa is a kind of statistical bible. so in moving from esa 95 to esa 2010 we are taking an extremely important decision. we are bringing stability to the statistical system on the one hand but, on the other hand, we are bringing in new elements through new knowledge and, of course, also new times. so it might sound dull, but without toil and hard work there is no attraction, no importance and there are no fair decisions. i wish to thank parliament again and very much look forward, from the commission’s side, to continuing this work together with parliament in the future.

the next item is the report by mrs åsa westlund, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the protection of public health against endocrine disruptors (2012/2066 (ini)) (a7-0027/2013).
mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the rapporteurs for this splendid report, which is balanced, although it was really difficult to get it. this is a very important report because these are substances which can affect health, and that is the most important thing and deserves the greatest legislative and scientific rigor at the same time. however, i have to say that i do not entirely agree with paragraph 25, because in this paragraph it is stated that it is proven that endocrine disruptors are substances that do not have a threshold. however, and probably after this commitment was made, the conclusions of the commission's expert advisory group, coordinated by the joint research centre, were presented on 19 february. they clearly underline that, according to most scientists, a threshold can be set for most endocrine disruptors. i therefore believe, commissioner, that we in this parliament should not anticipate or prejudge debates taking place at scientific level, nor do i think it right to contradict the conclusions of a scientific committee by a vote in parliament. we should leave the scientists to their work and concentrate on laying down the broad lines for the community framework. and that said, once we have the efsa reports and the joint research centre reports, we must be ruthless and absolutely rigorous with substances that can affect health and the environment. we must have zero tolerance for health issues. if a substance has to be banned altogether, it is banned; if there are thresholds, they have to be corrected and there has to be good risk management appropriate to the protection of human health.
mr president, the report we are discussing today has an important impact both from an economic and a social point of view, since immigration is one of the great challenges facing the european union, and i want to congratulate mrs hirsch, who has done a good job. it is necessary to devise a strategy for community immigration and for extra-community immigration. although it may seem paradoxical at a time when many member states are facing high unemployment, it is expected that in the next ten years there will be a shortage of skilled labour, particularly in the information technology sector. the aim should therefore be to achieve a qualitative immigration oriented towards the needs of the labour market. if we are to be competitive, we must design and coordinate an immigration policy that facilitates the mobility of workers. it is essential to reduce administrative burdens and to unify the validation of qualifications. we must make it easier to find work anywhere in europe. it is not logical, for example, that a young spanish graduate should find it easier to find work in germany than in other member states. immigrants must be integrated and for this they must have decent work and help to learn the language and customs of the host country; their families must also be supported. the question of circular migration must be examined in depth, with good cooperation with the countries of origin. the coordination of social security systems will also facilitate the mobility of workers. the history of our continent has taught us that humanist values, based on respect, equality and justice, are the right way forward. let's not leave this behind and make immigration an opportunity for all.

the council, that our thoughts and prayers are with vice-president papastamkos and his family this afternoon. since we last discussed egypt many challenges have emerged for the government and for the people. there is clearly a serious political divide in the country between the government and the main opposition – the national salvation front. we have seen demonstrations and violent clashes across the country. we urge calm. we urge restraint. we urge dialogue. the referendum and adoption of the constitution have not led to a great sense of direction, with a low turnout of 33 %. and, as many of you will be aware, the country is facing huge economic challenges with a 12 to 13 % budget deficit. the imf has already identified a usd 14 billion funding gap. this is the issue, more than any other, that is immediate and needs our engagement, notwithstanding – as i have already indicated – the political challenges that are faced by the country. more than ever, europe as a neighbour and a partner has to engage and support egypt’s democratic transition. special representative bernardino leon has spent a month of shuttle diplomacy to cairo to meet with the government, the presidency and the whole political opposition, on my behalf, in order to build confidence and to look for common ground on those political and economic issues. together with other members of the international community we will continue to push for the finalisation of the imf arrangement which will allow the european union to mobilise our macro-financial assistance of eur 500 million. in parallel, we will also have to discuss the means of how best we mobilise our existing financial assistance in a timely fashion, and i would ask for the support of this house and commitment for this undertaking. democracy-building is not an easy process. there are no ‘quick fixes’. the building of deep and sustainable democracy is a long process. it requires hard work, commitment, as well as patience – patience domestically and internationally. the fact that we do have an opposition that is operating and working is in itself part of that democratic achievement. that egypt had peaceful and fair presidential elections is another, and so is the formal invitation to the european union to observe the upcoming parliamentary elections, which as honourable members know were due to start on 22 april. president morsi accepted the administrative court ruling to refer the electoral law to the supreme constitutional court. i believe that was a wise decision. this will likely postpone the elections, which gives more time, of course, to reach agreement on the outstanding issues that still exist. in this very tense political context, elections need to be held in conformity with the constitution and in a peaceful, inclusive and transparent manner. we know that going to the polls to vote is very important, but it is only one component of building deep democracy. another is the importance of working with all sides to build bridges, to promote reconciliation, to respect and safeguard the fundamental human rights of all citizens, whether they are ‘winners’ or ‘losers’ of the election. we see that egyptians are openly debating human rights issues in public, in political circles, in the media, and at the shura council. i welcome that debate. we share many concerns and we want to see real progress in these areas. our special representative for human rights, stavros lambrinidis, was in egypt in mid-february and met with institutional as well as civil society interlocutors. he conveyed the message of particular concerns we have on police abuse, on torture and impunity, freedom of expression and belief, women’s rights, the working conditions for ngos, and the promotion of economic and social rights. we have stressed the importance of ensuring a favourable environment for civil society and encouraged the adoption of a new ngo law that ensures ngo transparency while respecting the independence of civil society from government control, that eliminates burdensome registration procedures, and does not subject ngo activities to prior government approval on the basis of their alleged ‘usefulness to society’, and that does not limit or demonise ngo funding. i am extremely pleased that the egyptian authorities have shown willingness to engage and have requested through our special representative, to whom i pay real tribute for the work he has done on this, eu assistance and expertise on the ngo law. however, the situation of women in egypt is of great concern, in particular in terms of violence and other forms of harassment. we are funding a eur 4 million project – with un women – on women’s empowerment. last weekend, helga schmid, our political director, met with the women with whom we have been engaging over the last two years. we are concerned about the stories that they gave us of the harassment they are facing. we are continuing to support the national council for women, currently in the process of drafting a national strategy for combating violence against women as a basis for a comprehensive law. last week, another important event took place in the relationship between the european union and egypt, which was the resumption of the formal dialogue under the eu-egypt association agreement that had been postponed since the uprising in 2011. following the commitment of president morsi during his visit to brussels in september last year to relaunch the process and following the task force meeting in november, an association committee at senior officials’ level was held in cairo on 28 february. we raised our concerns on human rights, on the need to build a political consensus and the establishment of a better business environment. egypt focused on asset recovery and the eu financial package. i have to say to honourable members that we are all aware of the consequences of an economic collapse, which could be devastating in egypt. we have to approach this problem in a very constructive and timely manner. we recognise that we have to show what we call ‘strategic patience’ with the political developments in that country, but not remain silent on issues of fundamental freedoms and human rights. at the same time we need to move quickly to try and help meet the socio-economic expectations – both the goals of the revolution and the aspirations of the egyptian people. more globally, we of course need to support egypt’s efforts as a regional power, be it in involvement in the league of arab states, its attempts to bring together those who have been engaged in supporting and searching for a political solution in the syria crisis, the brokering of the gaza ceasefire or the continued efforts on palestinian reconciliation. this is a very difficult time for egypt. as i have indicated, there are real challenges that need to be faced. i believe the european union has an incredibly important role to play in that. we are determined to play it, to be a friend and partner, but also to be a critical friend in times such now, which are extremely difficult for the people of egypt.

mr president, commissioner, very strict measures have been taken to combat doping, which has been a cancer in recent years, and now the same must be done with match-fixing, a scourge that affects all levels of sport: athletes, coaches, referees and officials. the report, which was adopted by a large majority in parliament last year, already suggested some measures: to recognise intellectual property rights of organisers of sporting events so that they can oppose betting they do not consider appropriate; to urge member states to criminalise all forms of corruption in sport; to cooperate with third countries in the fight against match-fixing and corruption in sport; to ask europol to work with joint investigation teams and to cooperate with eurojust on corruption in sport; to ask sport governing bodies to link data from the transfer matching system with the data from other anti-corruption systems to establish more effective control. but above all, good governance is essential - it has been found that match-fixing occurs to a large extent when athletes do not receive the remuneration they deserve - and education and the collaboration and involvement of sports associations are also essential to inform their peers of the seriousness of match-fixing. i welcome, madam commissioner, the commission's initiative to adopt a recommendation on good betting practice in 2014.

in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because of the uncertainty currently affecting the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, which will lay the foundations for the 2014 budgetary guidelines. the vote on the mfp in parliament postponed the procedure for its approval, since the council's proposal was rejected, which means the automatic increase in the 2013 budgetary thresholds plus an increase due to inflation estimated at 2%. the report proposes a number of points of interest on the need for realistic funds to meet the objectives set and to equip the institutions of the european union with the capacity to meet their policy objectives. however, in this context of uncertainty in the mfp negotiation, any modification of the mfps cannot have a considerable effect. that is why i did not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the 2013 budget negotiations have demonstrated once more that the system of financing the eu budget – with national contributions amounting to more than 75 % of eu revenue – is in contradiction with the letter and the spirit of the treaty, and is putting the eu budget in a position of total dependency on national treasuries, which can be particularly detrimental at a time of national budgetary constraints. the structure of union revenue must be reformed to include the introduction of new and genuine own resources, like the financial transaction tax and the new eu vat.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it introduces a distribution of seats in the european parliament which seriously undermines the representation of small countries. the distribution of seats in the european parliament for the next term should include the members for the new member state, croatia. with the decision not to increase the number of members it was decided to allocate these seats by subtracting them from the existing delegations. in the distribution of members of parliament, the representation of the smaller countries of the union has been considerably eroded, while the representation of the larger countries has been maintained. in this way the representation of countries such as portugal, ireland, greece, etc. has been eroded. this reform of the distribution to be implemented will give less say to countries that are suffering from the financial decisions of the european institutions. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − in favour. when the next parliamentary term starts in 2014, the current derogation from article 14(2) of the treaty on european union (teu) will expire and the european parliament will be composed of 751 members (750, plus the president). the current number of seats is 754: 736 for members elected in accordance with the nice treaty, which was in force at the time of the 2009 elections, plus 18 for members appointed under the lisbon treaty through an amendment to article 2 of protocol no 36 on transitional provisions, which established a temporary derogation from article 14(2) teu (which specifies that no member state may be allocated more than 96 seats) to allow the maintenance until 2014 of the 99 seats assigned to germany under the nice treaty. when its accession treaty enters into force, croatia will be assigned 12 seats in parliament (it currently has 12 observers) under article 19(1) of the act of accession, which also amends article 2 of protocol no 36, resulting in a temporary increase in the total number of seats to 766. as a result, the total number of seats will need to be reduced by 15 in order to bring it into line with the number laid down by the treaty provisions (751).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution as it represents a timely rejection of the draft regulation presented by the commission. this project is not compatible with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council, which currently regulates the definition, designation, presentation, labelling and protection of geographical indications for spirit drinks. the new proposed regulation amends annexes 2 and 3 to the current regulation, which lists the spirit drinks listed in europe. these indications imply the recognition of traditional productions associated with different regions of the continent and change the content in artificial alcohols, as the commission proposal seeks, reduces the quality of these indications and makes the quality of these products decrease. to protect the producers of these spirits i have voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted against this decision because it represents a missed opportunity to transform the common agricultural policy into a useful tool for improving the situation of the majority of european farmers and the environmental services they provide. the commission's proposal was a reform to guarantee payments to landholders for the mere fact of owning land, not for cultivating it, with a fixed ceiling of €300,000. despite having proposed numerous amendments to reduce these limits to a third of that amount, and despite the fact that these payments are linked to the fact that it takes place on eligible land, among other things, the amendments have not been adopted; only amendments that made the document even worse have been adopted. this reform of direct payments is supposed to guarantee the incomes of landowners and continue the neglect of small farmers throughout europe. this decision on direct payments has meant the loss of an opportunity to develop a farmers' cap and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. − against. meps have today voted for the cap to plough ahead unsustainably, with an outcome that is even worse for the environment than, and just as unfair as, the current model. meps have utterly failed to seize an historic opportunity to overhaul eu agricultural policy and make the cap fit for the 21st century. the fact that this is the first time the ep has had a say on the cap as a co-decider makes today’s outcome even more regrettable. while meps voted in favour of capping direct payments to farmers under the cap, the level set – eur 300 000 – is ridiculous and far too high to make a difference. huge farming businesses which do not need the funding will continue to get big pay-cheques, whilst depriving other areas of the cap from funding, notably for schemes that could be used to promote more sustainable farming.
in writing. - the region i represent, catalonia, does not have a large agricultural area to exploit the economies of scale of agricultural crops. livestock account for 60% of the final agricultural production in catalonia. the cap reform proposal does not take sufficient account of cattle and sheep farming without a territorial basis, as in the case of catalonia. it is necessary to take account of the different agricultural specificities of the different regions of the eu when proposing such a reform. i have therefore called for the possibility of distributing agricultural aid according to the needs of each region, as has been finally agreed. the application of a single tariff does not reflect the diversity of european production. i also welcome the flexibility of the definition of active farmer, the increase in aid to young farmers and the fact that a ceiling of eur 300 000 has been set for the aid each farm receives per year. however, it is necessary to continue to call for regionalised programming in those member states, such as spain, where their regions have regionalised responsibilities in the field of agriculture and rural development.
in writing. - i voted against this decision because it legitimises and maintains the current market structures for the next period of the cap. the channels for marketing agricultural products are the main problem faced by farmers in order to achieve sufficient profit margins to maintain their activity. while they are forced to sell at below cost prices due to excess demand in season, the agri-food processing and distribution sector sells at prices several times higher than the farmer's. this unfair situation in agricultural markets must be firmly regulated, but the amendments put forward in parliament's committee on agriculture have not been accepted and the resulting text does not solve the problems of the agricultural value chain. that is why i voted against.
in writing. − against. despite some positive outcomes in the agri committee, such as the definition of advanced systems and methods of sustainable production, improvement of children’s eating habits through fruit and vegetable and school milk schemes, and precautionary measures improving bee health, the text is pretty bad overall and dominated by the interests of big agro-industrial concerns.

in writing. - i voted against this decision because it represents a failure for the implementation of the future rural development policy of the cap. this is a report that deals with the many aspects of this policy, from environmental aspects to programmes for young farmers, but most of these programmes have been designed to have little or no effect on the european countryside. although there are points which could be of interest to farmers, the simplification of procedures for this type of rural development programme fails. it is committed to the introduction of the private sector in risk prevention funds, leaving it to private business instead of proposing a public agency that assumes the risks of agricultural activity. i have therefore voted against this decision.

in writing. - i voted against this decision because it is an example of the inability of the european institutions to bring agricultural policy closer to the farmer. this report was intended to simplify the procedures and the administrative burden that farmers have to bear in order to access european aid programmes, but this intention announced by the commission has been reduced to a timid reform. the procedures will remain the same and this is an administrative barrier which operates in favour of large farms and agricultural enterprises which, by having legal advice teams, can overcome these administrative barriers. this clear orientation of a cap towards business often leaves farmers outside the programmes which are intended for them, because they cannot supplement the complex procedures. that is why i voted against this decision.

in writing. - i voted against this report because it keeps nuclear energy within the energy strategy for 2050. the energy strategy contains very ambitious targets for emissions reduction by 2050, with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80%-95% from 1990 levels. such long-term strategies are of no political use but should serve as a guide for future developments in the sector. from this point of view, the targets seem ambitious, but the report argues that nuclear energy should be one of the main sectors responsible for this decline in emissions. the report proposes to replace conventional energy production with nuclear, increasing the risk to the population. that is why i voted against this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it improves the conditions for safety tests to be carried out on european nuclear power stations. our group has been firmly opposed to the use of this type of energy for years, but this report improves the safety conditions to which the plants currently in operation must respond. the result of these stress tests should be used to force the plants to implement improved safety measures, increasing the cost of production of this type of energy to show the national energy systems the true economic cost of its use. if the safety measures required by the stress test results are implemented, nuclear power plants will be less profitable and less attractive to private investment. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution, although i did not propose the closure of any power stations.
in writing. - i am voting against this report because it does not provide sufficient guarantees in the area of stress testing of nuclear power stations in the european union. we need much broader legislation which sets much more restrictive conditions when defining the safety conditions of a nuclear power station. nuclear energy, the source of unfortunate disasters such as the one that occurred in fukushima, must be the subject of a social debate on the energy model we aspire to as a society. in the meantime, we must ensure that the use we make of it is absolutely safe for the citizens. i therefore reject this resolution, which is insufficient to achieve the objective of the european legislators: to ensure that the stress tests carried out on eu nuclear power stations are strict and complete.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a step forward in the effective protection of the population sensitive to substances which are potentially dangerous to health. because of scientific advances in recent years, the importance of proper hormone production and its relationship to the proper functioning of the body is beginning to be known. there are numerous diseases that are related to the malfunctioning of the body's hormone production. these new developments have highlighted the importance of much more comprehensive regulation of the presence of chemicals that may alter the production of these substances. i believe that increased control of the maximum levels of these synthetic hormone-distorting chemicals in certain consumer products is essential to improving the health of european citizens. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. for we can't afford to wait any longer to act. the risk of disease from endocrine disruptors is vastly underestimated, and we continue to be exposed to these substances every day, through our food or through direct contact, in town and in the countryside. a clear and broad definition of these hazardous substances is therefore urgently needed to reduce the risk of exposure and to protect the most at-risk populations such as pregnant women, foetuses and children. indeed, pregnant women may unknowingly be harming the health of their unborn children. the public authorities must therefore inform the public through very clear national information campaigns: beware of pvc floor coverings, varnishes on certain furniture, tin cans containing bisphenol a, or cosmetic products that may also contain these endocrine disruptors. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the term 'commercial'.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in the legal situation of immigrants in the various member states of the european union. the report partly sets out the many administrative problems faced by immigrants in claiming the same social rights as other inhabitants of the member states. the report, while not mentioning border control and the unfair treatment of immigrants, does suggest improvements to equal access to the same rights as european citizens. the introduction of legislation on the inclusion of immigrants in social security systems, access to certain social rights, etc., means fighting against the conditions of marginalization and institutional racism suffered by the immigrant population on many occasions in the member states. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the demographic situation in the european union is such that the working age population will decline by 14 million over the next decade. this requires us to take social and economic measures to enable the integration of new immigrants that europe will need when growth and employment levels are restored. however, while coordination of our social security systems may be necessary, our migration and asylum policies remain subject to imperatives linked to each national situation, in particular the labour market situation. european coordination in the field of immigration is to be considered, but in no case harmonization. i do not support the report by our colleague, mrs nadja hirsch, because it does not make that distinction.
in writing. for i welcome the adoption of this report which supports the granting of the right to vote to foreigners, particularly at local level, the opening up of legal migration channels, the creation of a rapid and effective european mechanism for the recognition of diplomas and qualifications, the development of reciprocity in social security and the facilitation of access to the labour market for foreign students. this report demonstrates the aberration of the security approach currently being developed by the member states and agrees with the observation already made by the united nations and the council of europe, which is supported by many reports. the contribution of migration is essential to the development, including economic development, of our societies. the challenge for the union is to increase its attractiveness and to facilitate the reception of migrants. this requires an ambitious, open and respectful approach to migrants' rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a total ban on asbestos still existing in europe and proposes actions to remove all asbestos still existing. asbestos is an extremely toxic substance which has been used for years in europe as a building material because of its low cost and its saving advantages. for years this material was used until its terrible health consequences were discovered and it was banned. however, many buildings still have this material, exposing the workers who occupy them to significant health risks. the report goes into more detail on the need to act on the places where this material is found, with a view to cleaning all european buildings of this dangerous material before the 2023 deadline. this ban comes from a union campaign for the protection of workers' health. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. this resolution basically calls on the eu to develop, implement and support a model for asbestos screening and registration in accordance with article 11of directive 2009/148/ec and to request owners of public or commercial buildings to: a. screen buildings for the presence of asbestos-containing materials; b. prepare plans to manage the risks they present; c. ensure that such information is available to workers who may disturb such materials; d. in the case of member states who already implement compulsory screening schemes, to increase the efficiency of such schemes.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it seeks to extend and improve the functioning of european mutual societies, it means breaking down the barriers of protection in the member states. mutual societies are non-profit-making cooperative societies, usually operating in the fields of employment, insurance or health insurance. the form of these types of societies is interesting, but it's no guarantee that they won't end up with a capitalist functioning. the report includes interesting points to improve the status of these types of companies and make them equal throughout the european union, but also proposes the elimination of trade barriers to the activity of these companies between member states, which is a step forward in the development and implementation of the single market. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. in this resolution we basically, in the light of the outcome of the recent study on the situation of mutual societies in the union, and bearing in mind the clear preference expressed on several occasions by parliament for a statute for a european mutual society, request the commission swiftly to submit, following the detailed recommendations set out in the annex hereto, on the basis of article 352 or, possibly, article 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, one or more proposals allowing mutual societies to act on a european and cross-border scale.

in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this resolution because it would have led to a diversion of attention from the problems of sport in the various member states of the union. the european parliament is taking a stand on match-fixing at a time when regional governments in spain are taking over the debts of some of the leading football clubs. it is certainly a major problem in the operation of sport in europe, which reduces its quality in order to maintain the profits linked to the big companies that sports clubs have become. party buying can be a practice that, due to its widespread use, has become a major source of illegal business. but there are many more problems linked to sport, with the amount of money it generates on the continent, which should have been included in this resolution. that is why i did not vote in favour.
in writing. − in favour. among other things, the text calls on all the main stakeholders individually to take responsibility and to develop a comprehensive approach by complementing one another’s efforts to combat match-fixing in sport. it also asks the commission to develop a coordinated approach to the fight against match-fixing and organised crime by coordinating the efforts of the main stakeholders, such as sports organisations, national police and judicial authorities and gambling operators, in this area and by providing a platform for discussion and for the exchange of information and best practice. thirdly, it calls on sports organisations to adopt a zero-tolerance policy on corruption (both internally and in relation to external contractors) in order to prevent their members from yielding to external pressure. fourthly, it urges sports organisations to establish a code of conduct for all staff and officials (players, coaches, referees, medical and technical staff and club and association leaders) which sets out the dangers of match-fixing, includes a clear prohibition on manipulating matches for betting or other purposes, stipulates the associated sanctions and includes a ban on gambling on own matches and an obligation to report any approaches concerning, or awareness of, match-fixing, coupled with an adequate whistleblower protection mechanism.
in writing. - it is understandable that the public authorities should deal with issues such as violence in sport or the use of substances not allowed by sportsmen, but it is surprising that they should also intervene in match-fixing, since maintaining fair play should be an inexcusable guideline in the behaviour of any sportsman who, where appropriate, could be monitored by the corresponding federations or associations, but not by the public authorities directly.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank mr gallagher for raising this issue. it is a really important issue. we have already discussed, in this house, the consequences of overfishing by iceland and the faroe islands on fish stocks and the preservation of these species. i share concerns over the impact of these actions on our fishermen, and especially the impact of these actions on our local fisheries and local communities. small-scale vessels and small fishermen have no alternatives, so i agree that for them this is a very difficult situation. we are following the situation very carefully. we are trying, through many channels, to put pressure on the icelandic and faroese governments to change their policy. we hope that, at the end of the day – although it will take a lot of time – we will be able to come back to negotiations with all coastal governments and reach real agreement on this topic. although for the moment this is not the case, we will have to see what we are going to do. to cut a long story short, the option of trade sanctions is, of course, on the table. however, it is important that we carefully consider two very important factors. firstly, we have to consider carefully what the legal conditions are that we have to meet. secondly, we have to think carefully about the timing of our actions. regarding mackerel, we are now discussing the possible options with the member states. next week i will meet the norwegian minister in brussels, and i hope that we can come to a common decision. we would like to have a common decision with the norwegian government on this. however, i should say that the commission has already looked into the procedural aspects with the aim of accelerating the decision-making process if and when we go forward. so, if we decide to go forward, we have already made all the preparations for accelerating the procedure. i would like to assure members that we will keep everyone interested in this issue informed, starting from next week, when we finalise the discussions with the norwegian government. regarding atlanto-scandian herring, the landscape here is rather clearer – unfortunately, i would say. the commission regrets the announcement made on 26 march 2013 by the faroe islands that they intend unilaterally to more than triple their quota.
madam president, what is at stake is compliance with international standards. the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the agreement on straddling fish stocks and highly migratory fish stocks clearly establish the need for very close cooperation between all coastal and fishing member states. this is what the european union, norway, the faroe islands and iceland have been doing with regard to mackerel in the north-east atlantic, and what has happened since 2010 - as mr gallagher has clearly explained - is that the faroe islands have increased their catches fivefold since 2006 and iceland has increased its catches by 23. overall, the sustainability of these resources is being undermined without regard to existing fishing patterns, the rights and interests of other countries and the european union. this is causing great concern within the sector and action is needed, firstly to restore a culture of compliance and the existence of rules and, secondly, because otherwise the allocation of internal quotas, the management measures being taken by the member states and even the credibility of the control measures being carried out will be called into question. so we have to reset the playing field, we have to react. i clearly support the commissioner in her desire to find solutions. i think it is very reasonable that it should try to do so through dialogue, but i think it should also take into account the need to take action in the event of failure and clearly set a time frame for this.
mr president, i would also like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr karas, and the parliament's negotiating team on having managed to tackle these issues, which are the failures of the banking system that have led to a public, costly and unprecedented crisis. it was necessary to address unsustainable credit growth and institutions with insufficient capital quality and quantity, to provide protection against risks arising from complex and liquid activities as well as off-balance sheet exposures, to strengthen governance and to create an appropriate incentive system. this initiative is a milestone in delivering on the g20 commitments to a stronger financial system that supports growth and meets the needs of families and citizens, and updates the basel iii review. for the first time, there is a regulation for the uniform application of rules in the european union and also a directive to improve governance and supervision. the agreement, in my view, has three very positive aspects: it affects the 8 000 banking institutions - with differentiated treatment - , it supports the real economy and, moreover, it seeks consistent implementation at international level. i think it supports a change of culture by limiting the ratio between fixed and variable remuneration, it supports transparency by setting accounting standards country by country and at the same time it introduces flexibility and proportionality by favouring a treatment of systemic risks and credit to small businesses. regulatory reform must continue.
