in writing. − abstention. today the european parliament gave its binding consent for easier eu visa rules for ukrainian citizens. i have my concerns. since 2011, the ukrainian parliament has been examining two draft laws making it illegal to say homosexuality is normal, or supporting lgbt people in any way. they are now close to being adopted, and the european parliament expressed concern about these draft laws on several occasions. ahead of today’s vote, human rights organisations including human rights watch and ilga-europe had called on the european parliament to send the agreement back to committee, postponing the vote. the alliance of liberals and democrats for europe made this request, but failed to gather a majority. i wish this vote had been postponed in order to send a strong political signal to ukraine. we cannot deepen our relationship with a country that enacts witch-hunting laws against its minorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which amends an existing agreement with moldova of 2008, because it provides for improvements for moldovan citizens in facilitating visas for short stays (90 days) in each 180-day period. this improvement will reduce the time and costs associated with travel within the schengen area.
in writing. − in favour. the visa facilitation agreement between the european community and the republic of moldova has been in force since 1 january 2008. this agreement has been extremely successful. despite these successes, an evaluation of the functioning of the agreement highlighted some additional amendments that should be made to correct any misrepresentations or differences in interpretations of the text. it represents an encouraging step forward and will promote the people-to-people contacts, the economic development, the cultural and scientific dialogue, stability, security and well-being of the citizens. the visa liberalisation process is also an opportunity for moldova to implement the reforms needed in the area of freedom, security and justice. there are still some significant problems in moldova, in particular ones related to the rule of law. nevertheless, ordinary people should not suffer: the freer travel is, the better chances for improvements we have.
in writing. - i abstained in this report on the impact of the crisis on human rights. the report notes that even if the current crisis situation worldwide were to improve, by 2020 there would still be more than 71 million people in the world in extreme poverty due to the crisis. the report also refers to the exponential increase in unemployment since the beginning of the crisis, which seriously affects the rights of workers, the right to health, education and food. the developed countries are also warned about the failure to meet the millennium development goals, specifically the failure to meet the 0.7% of gdp that has to go to the least developed countries. in short, the report describes well the serious world situation resulting from the crisis, but in my view it lacks proposals to deal with it, nor does it point to the political leaders responsible for the situation. i therefore could not vote in favour and abstained.
in writing. − in favour. human rights include the right to food, water, education, adequate housing, land, decent work, health and social security. all these are topics affected by the crisis. the resolution condemns the fact that these rights have been under attack in a number of countries since the crisis began, recognises that worsening poverty is the main factor preventing people from asserting these rights, and calls for the eu to invest more effort and money in achieving the millennium development goals, given the evidence that the world is falling far short of the goals set for 2015.
in writing. − in favour. the sógor report – despite attempts by the rapporteur to reverse it – supports the commission proposal to determine the population of a country based on the principle of ‘usual residence’ – and use this also when it comes to the question of qualified majority voting in the council (after a transition period of twelve months a person, living in another country, is considered usual resident of that country for statistical purposes). the commission proposal in general, including this part, has been supported by our group in the opinion-giving afco committee and therefore also in empl, and finally in plenary.
in writing. - the report sets out the measures for the environmentally responsible management of ship dismantling provided for by the hong kong convention. the report also proposes that these measures should be applied to ships from non-eu member states anchored in member states, in order to enforce the same rules as those for ships flying the flag of an eu state. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − in favour. while the ep has voted to put an end to european ships being recklessly scrapped in developing countries in hazardous conditions, this is jeopardised by the failure to adopt a financial mechanism to support this. it is very frustrating that a narrow majority succumbed to the highly misleading lobbying by the maritime sector, seeking to shirk its responsibilities, and voted down the proposed financial mechanism that would have made safe ship recycling competitive. currently, most eu ships are sent to south-east asia at the end of their lives, where they are beached, with their hazardous materials leaking into the environment and causing unacceptable conditions for human health and the environment. this is an opprobrious practise, which circumvents eu rules under which the export of hazardous waste to non-oecd countries is outlawed.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of this report because i believe that accession to the european union or non-accession is a matter of the sovereignty of a country, in this case croatia. but the enlargement process involves negotiations on the fulfilment of neoliberal criteria which will have a negative impact on the population of croatia. among these criteria are privatisation and liberalisation of public services, the stability of the banking sector and budgetary consolidation, which, as has been demonstrated in the eu member countries, have been the causes of the crisis and the suffering of the working classes. in particular, there is no reference in this report to the high unemployment rate of around 19% or to how accession would help to solve this problem. however, the report expresses concern about the law on strategic investments, as it is not in line with european standards, urging the government to reform the law in order to better protect property rights. i therefore abstained.
in writing. − in favour. we tabled the following 12 amendments at committee level: (6) croatia is not on track, but only largely on track to meet outstanding requirements; (10) need to involve parliament and civil society in monitoring exercise; (18) public administration needs to be professional, accountable, independent and impartial; (22) not ‘with satisfaction’ regarding the fight against corruption, but ‘generally satisfied’ and need to further step up fight against corruption; (32) lgbt rights, socially but also health system, pride; (33) croatian administration not fully prepared for eu funds, need to strengthen capacities; (39) need transparency regarding environmental assessments of large scale investments projects; give priority to environment in spatial planning; (40) concerns about proposed law on strategic investments and european social and environmental standards; (41) appeal to eu ms not to restrict free movement of persons after accession/transitional measures; (43) war crimes: need to swiftly address com recommendations; concerns about law on invalidation; (56) bilateral disputes, enlargement process and arbitration mechanism; (61) com needs to evaluate and assess involvement and role of civil society in enlargement process. four of our 12 amendments were rejected at committee level. these were amendments 6, 32, 33 and 43.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution because as long as turkey maintains its military occupation of northern cyprus with over 40 000 troops deployed, it will never be able to become part of the eu. turkey, however much it wants to appear and present itself as a peace actor in the region, maintains an illegal occupation of about 35% of the cypriot territory which exposes it in that role it wants to appear. turkey maintains a policy of permanent cultural invasion, moving thousands of turkish families to northern cyprus to become a minority and ultimately to eliminate the turkish cypriot cultural identity.
in writing. − in favour. renewed mutual engagement in the context of the negotiation process is needed in order to maintain a constructive relationship. the text stresses the importance of creating the conditions for a constructive dialogue and the foundations of a common understanding. it also notes that this should be based on common values of democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights. the ep commends the commission and turkey for the implementation of the positive agenda, which proves how, in a context of mutual engagement and clear objectives, turkey and the eu could advance their dialogue, achieve common understanding, and produce positive change and necessary reforms.

in writing. - in 1999, under the pretext of avoiding a humanitarian catastrophe in kosovo, nato attacked yugoslavia, causing thousands of civilian casualties and destroying factories and infrastructure. the result of that war was the destruction of yugoslavia's economic structure and kosovo becoming a nato protectorate, despite un resolution 1244 which considers kosovo part of serbia. after 14 years of the attack and 5 years of kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence, reality has shown that the artificial creation of a pseudo-state has been anything but sovereign. this resolution we voted for approves the end of kosovo's supervised independence, which constitutes recognition of its independence, and in turn reaffirms the mandate of eulex to renew and intensify efforts to improve the rule of law in kosovo and to monitor, guide and advise. i have therefore voted against the resolution.

in writing. - none of the votes of the spanish socialist delegation can be interpreted as a recognition of kosovo, in the absence of an agreement between the parties or a new security council resolution. we are firmly committed to the european perspective of the western balkans, which we consider to be key to stability, peace and the reform process in the region. we are defending a constructive position which is not only the most consistent with the international community's commitment to multiethnic states in the western balkans and with international law, but which, far from being an obstacle, has proved to be key to stimulating serbia's european commitment, stability in the region and progress in the belgrade-pristina dialogue, which must continue. we therefore regret that, for another year, the recognition of kosovo is again contaminating a resolution which would be more effective if it focused on the problems of the people and on what the commission communication has pointed out in relation to the economic situation, corruption, organised crime, integration or displaced persons.
in writing. − in favour. it is especially important that the text welcomes the outcome of the european commission’s feasibility study concluding that stabilisation and association agreement can be concluded between the eu and kosovo in a situation where eu member states maintain different views on status, and provided that kosovo fulfils a number of basic conditions; and that encourages nevertheless the remaining five eu member states to proceed with recognition of kosovo and invites them to do their outmost to facilitate economic, social and political relations between their citizens and kosovo citizens.
in writing. - this resolution expresses the parliament, the council and the commission's full agreement with the process of economic governance and the european semester and their willingness to continue to impose the same neoliberal economic dictates on the member states. i am not against the principle of harmonizing indicators at community level, but i am against continuing to impose the principles of control of public expenditure, privatization and liberalization, which are what these indicators are going to measure. that is why i abstained from voting on this resolution.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, thank you very much for holding this debate. we have indeed noticed with concern a more restrictive approach on human rights, notably concerning freedom of expression and the media. the european union values the increasingly positive relationship that we have with vietnam. a close relationship has developed to the point of allowing for an open and frank discussion, also on issues of disagreement. we must of course take into account the very long journey that vietnam has travelled in the last few years. there has been progress in many areas. vietnam was one of the poorest countries in the world at the end of the eighties and within a quarter of a century vietnam has lifted millions of people out of poverty and made progress, as i said. however, there are other areas – those mentioned in your resolution for instance – where we do have concerns, and we regularly raise those issues with vietnam at all levels. following the sentencing of bloggers last september, high representative catherine ashton expressed her serious concerns, calling on vietnam to respect its international obligations and to release the convicted bloggers immediately. the eu head of delegation in hanoi reiterated the eu’s concerns on 11 january and again in march at the occasion of an eu démarche on the death penalty. presidents barroso and van rompuy raised human rights concerns when meeting the general-secretary of the communist party of vietnam in january. the eu-vietnam partnership and cooperation agreement gives a valuable opportunity to deepen cooperation on human rights. on this basis we agreed to establish an enhanced human rights dialogue. the dialogue is our primary tool to address issues of concern and there might be a first meeting in vietnam already before the summer. furthermore, our delegation in hanoi, in coordination with member states, attends trials of human rights defenders, visits prison facilities and interacts with local human rights activists. also, as some of you said, vietnam’s membership of the human rights council of the united nations could be an important opportunity to further highlight the situation of human rights in vietnam. our objective is to achieve tangible results in the dialogue with vietnam. i have confidence that the different instruments that we have and other activities will help strengthen human rights in vietnam as a fundamental element of our partnership.

member of the commission. − mr president, i want to start by vehemently condemning the horrible bomb attacks in boston this monday. i express my solidarity with the victims, their families, the american people and the authorities. as we have discussed today, the hunger strike started in guantánamo more than two months ago. last week, the us military said that 43 of the 166 guantánamo prisoners have refused food. defence lawyers estimate that 100 to 130 inmates have joined the strike. we can discuss the exact figures, but it is of course a very serious situation. and behind these figures, there is a collective act of despair, with some prisoners detained for up to 11 years still facing indefinite detention without charge, without trial. according to the department of defence, 11 guantánamo prisoners have lost so much weight that the us authorities have decided to force-feed them through tubes inserted into their noses. this of course raises complex legal and ethical questions related to the practice. while the principle of the autonomy of the patients and the right to consent to medical treatments has to be respected, the necessity of force-feeding and its legality with regard to international law should be assessed on a case-by-case basis, and obviously the european union does not have detailed information on the individual cases. however, i can give reassurance that we are following this with great attention, as the recent remarks made publicly by the president of the international committee of the red cross have raised many concerns. other reports and allegations regarding the conditions of detention in guantánamo, as well as the rising tensions within the facility, are also matters of concern to us. beyond these questions, i am convinced that the best humane response to this dramatic situation is to reactivate the political process leading to the complete closure of the guantánamo detention facility. respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law lie at the heart of the eu’s approach to countering terrorism. the fight against terrorism cannot be used to justify practices such as unlawful arrest, arbitrary detention and ill-treatment of detainees. as you know, all of the eu institutions – the council, the commission and the parliament – have taken a very firm stand on this issue, calling consistently for the closure of guantánamo. we repeat that call today. while stressing that the primary responsibility rests with the united states, the eu responded – as a friend and a partner – to the administration’s requests for assistance. in june 2009, the eu, its member states and the usa adopted a common framework within which a number of eu member states accepted over 20 ex-detainees for resettlement. since then, the us congress has adopted controversial provisions within the national defense authorization acts for 2012 and 2013. they provide for the indefinite detention without trial of certain categories of suspected terrorists and dramatically limit the ability of the administration to use federal money to transfer guantánamo detainees. on several occasions, including at ministerial level, the eu has shared our concerns with the us administration about the compatibility of these provisions with international law, and the possible undesirable consequences for transatlantic cooperation on fighting terrorism. we are the usa’s closest friend and ally. we shall remain committed to supporting efforts to fight terrorism, as well as the efforts of the us administration towards the complete closure of the guantánamo detention facility.

on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur because i think he has produced a balanced report in terms of the context in which it was produced and its objectives. in the end, the aim of this report - and i think the commissioner has put it very well - is to discuss in a broad way the major problems and the major limitations of the development of renewable energies at the moment, especially in those dimensions which are more pan-european. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would like to say - and we must not forget the purpose of this report - that we are talking about one of the aspects that must be considered in an energy policy. so until the commission proposes a direction, a direction, for what it proposes to be climate change policy and energy policy from the year 2020, that is, the road to the year 2030, it does not really make much sense for us to set specifically new targets, higher targets than there are right now. because we have to look at the whole of the interaction between the different dimensions that are affecting energy policy and climate change policy and, among other things, the issues that have to do with the development, for example, of the emissions market, for which we are also waiting for a proposal for revised structural measures from the commission.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report with my group in this house because it lays the foundations for cooperation with the democratic socialist republic of sri lanka in the field of aviation. this report seeks to implement a judgment of the court of justice of the european union which declared a clause giving member states the power to refuse, revoke or suspend an airline's licence to operate in a member state contrary to eu law. the report therefore seeks to revoke one of the 'horizontal agreements' so that the powers of refusal, revocation or suspension of permits in this area fall to the european union and not to the member states. as the report is only intended to speed up and eliminate the problems arising from the bilateral agreements to establish a joint negotiation in the field of air transport with sri lanka, i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and sri lanka. the establishment of a strong legal basis between sri lanka and the european union and the prohibition of anti-competitive practices were key elements of this recommendation and of the agreement signed by the european commission, which is why i voted in favour of the recommendation put forward by petri sarvamaa.
in writing. − in favour. traditionally, international aviation relations between member states and third countries are governed by bilateral air service agreements. these agreements include a ‘designation clause’, which allows a third country to reject, withdraw or suspend the permissions or authorisations of an air carrier that has been designated by a member state but that is not substantially owned or effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. sri lanka has signed 15 bilateral agreements, the relevant provisions of which must be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the union. more specifically, article 2 of the agreement governs designation, authorisation and revocation of authorisation and clearly states that in exercising its rights, sri lanka shall not discriminate between air carriers of member states on the grounds of nationality. article 4 resolves potential conflicts with the competition rules of the union. the agreement was signed on 27 september 2012. in its decision of 26 november 2012, the council requested that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement, in accordance with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the development of the single european area to be a step forward for the union. the report seeks to promote cooperation between member states in the field of air navigation with a view to creating the future single area. this impetus is reflected in the establishment of cooperation modalities and mechanisms and in the special role given to eurocontrol as the eu's 'technical and operational arm' in this field. the development towards the single european area will make it possible to reduce red tape between the countries of the union and to facilitate and promote the activity of the air navigation sector. it is for all these reasons, which will benefit the sector, that i have decided to vote in favour, together with my group in this parliament.
in writing. − in favour. eurocontrol is an intergovernmental organisation with 39 contracting parties from all over europe, including all the member states except estonia. it plays a pivotal role in air traffic management (atm) in europe. in line with the single european sky (ses) legislation, the commission designated eurocontrol as the performance review body of the ses in 2010 and as the network manager for the atm network functions in 2011. the aim of the agreement is to strengthen and consolidate cooperation between the eu and eurocontrol in order to enable the latter to support the eu in the implementation of the ses and related eu policies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it includes an improvement in information archives and provides greater access to the historical archives of the various european institutions. the report seeks to replace the traditional practice of granting access to archives through the conditions laid down in a specific contract between the commission and the european university institute in florence. the proposal for this report replaces this contract with a council regulation regulating the term and thus improving the transparency of the historical archives of these institutions. it is the improvement of transparency in the european institutions that i have voted for this report.
in writing. as a historian, i can only welcome such a vote. i have given my agreement to the transfer of the archives of the various european institutions to the european institute in florence (ief) to enable them to be consulted by the greatest number of people and by researchers interested in the functioning of the european institutions and in the history of european integration.
in writing. − in favour. the historical archives of the eu institutions represent an important source of information on the history and legacy of the european union. therefore it is essential to provide access to the archives for public consultation and for the preservation of information about the eu institutions, and to support research about the history of european integration. the proposal for a council regulation which is currently being examined under the consent procedure by the european parliament (rule 81(1) of its rules of procedure) provides a more solid legal and financial framework for the cooperation between the eu and the eui. at the same time it also enhances the role of the eui, which is intended to manage the historical archives of the eu institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because there are timing problems in some member states, as the first council proposal set the period for holding the elections between 5 and 8 june 2014, which coincides with pentecost in some member states. in order to encourage participation in the holding of this electoral process, the council made another proposal with two options in may, of which this report includes the second, according to which the next elections to the european parliament would be held between 25 and 28 may 2014. such dates are the best option within the council's proposal as they would not entail an increase in the financial cost and would allow a sufficient period of time for the formation of parliament's political groups before the first plenary session to be held in july 2014. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. this report was drawn up in response to a request for consultation from the council on a draft decision seeking to modify the period during which the forthcoming european elections would ordinarily have been held. under article 11(2) of the act concerning the election of the members of the european parliament by direct universal suffrage (the ‘electoral act’), this period would have been thursday, 5 to sunday, 8 june 2014, by analogy with the dates on which the first elections by direct universal suffrage were held (thursday, 9 to sunday, 12 june 1979). in paragraph 5 of its resolution of 22 november 2012 (1), the european parliament asked the council to ‘consult parliament on holding the elections on either 15-18 may or 22-25 may 2014’. given that, in most member states, the dates on which the elections would ordinarily have been held would have coincided with the whitsun bank holiday weekend, the council took the view that it would be preferable to bring them forward and proposed that the electoral period should run between thursday, 22 and sunday, 25 may 2014.
in writing. − in favour. on the basis of the considerations established in the report, and pursuant to article 6(3) of the rules of procedure, after considering the reasons for and against defending the member’s immunity, the committee on legal affairs recommended that the european parliament should not defend the parliamentary immunity of gabriele albertini.
in writing. − in favour. at the sitting of 14 january 2013 the president announced, under rule 6(2) of the rules of procedure, that he had received a request from the greek authorities to waive the parliamentary immunity of spyros danellis. the president referred the request to the committee on legal affairs under rule 6(2). mr danellis is accused of dereliction of duty for having, allegedly, in his former position as mayor of hersonissos, omitted to take steps to close an establishment operating in his municipality despite the existence of a decision by the sanitary authorities which required such steps to be taken. on the basis of the considerations made in the report, after considering the reasons for and against waiving the member’s immunity, it is recommended that the european parliament should waive the parliamentary immunity of spyros danellis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the application of the rules laid down in directive 2004/25/ec on public procurement also concerns business law, labour law, corporate governance, etc. the directive establishes community rules on public procurement, emphasising the need for public procurement procedures to be transparent and to allow equal treatment in order to avoid fraudulent practices. the directive calls for the standardisation of award procedures in all member states to ensure equal access for all economic operators in the eu. but the directive must cover all economic operators and not just at the time when this type of public procurement has fallen the most; it makes no sense to change these rules until the volume of activity in this sector returns to normal. the report also calls on the commission to take account of the representatives of workers in the sector. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − in favour. after decades of failed attempts, the directive was finally adopted by the european parliament at the end of 2003 in second reading and published in the official journal in april 2004. member states were given until may 2006 to transpose the provisions of the directive into their national laws. it is an unfortunate coincidence that the transposition date of the directive coincides with the start of the crisis. in the light of these findings the ep believes that the application of the directive cannot be properly assessed only on the basis of limited data being available. the ep therefore suggests that more relevant data is needed in order to establish not only the need for changes to the directive but also the precise harmonisation steps to be taken next.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the requirements for european funds must be reformulated to allow for the financing of new productive initiatives in areas undergoing industrial conversion. the report argues that regional and structural funds are needed in old industrial areas in the midst of industrial conversion and that cohesion policy funds can finance industrial regeneration policies. in view of the extreme emergency generated by the growth of unemployment in many european countries, it is essential to allow the financial instruments to be used to generate jobs in the areas of the union most in need. the report includes some points on public-private partnerships which i do not share, but the extreme need for the areas under conversion is the fundamental reason for voting in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the report underlines that regions are different even if they share similar characteristics such as an old industrial base, and that there is no blueprint for a regional development / conversion strategy. it points out common features of old industrialised regions and identifies opportunities for solutions, in particular the different policy instruments offered by cohesion policy to tackle the challenges of old industrialised areas. the report highlights that the sustainable regeneration of old industrialised regions is very costly and therefore european funding needs to play an important role in possible future attempts to reconvert old industrialised regions. it shall also bring a contribution to – and shape – the decision-making process in support of future integrated territorial investment and policy delivery for the 2014-2020 period.
in writing. - i voted against this report because once again there is an attempt to endanger marine ecosystems just to guarantee maximum profits for oil companies. the report follows the commission's initiative to harmonise safety standards for these types of farms following, amongst others, the bp oil spill in the gulf of mexico in 2010. it initially included a number of points of interest, but the amendments adopted have left on wet paper what could have been a justified tool for control and accountability in the sector. the report adopted reduces the european maritime safety agency's capacity to intervene, the moratorium on oil exploration in the arctic is lifted, the financial obligations of oil companies are not clearly laid down, etc. for all these reasons, and particularly because it allows fishing in the waters of the balearic islands and the canary islands, i voted against this report with my group in this parliament.
in writing. − against. fundamentally, this legislation fails to achieve what it set out to achieve, and for many member states with existing operations it is business as usual. this may not provide sufficient protection against a deepwater horizon type incident in union waters. although it is generally felt that some legislation on offshore extraction is better than no eu legislation, greens had proposed two key amendments that were rejected during the vote. one: reintroduction of envi’s recital for a moratorium on the arctic, and two: a proposal of a moratorium on sensitive touristic and coastal areas (e.g. the canary islands). we lost both.
in writing. - i voted against amendment no 3 because the text is drafted in a very general way: it includes all tourist areas. the safety of these activities is of particular concern to the mep, who recently asked the european commission about the compliance of the mediterranean sea authorisations with the agreements signed through the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea (oj l 4, 9.1.2013, p. 13) and with the provisions contained in directive 2008/56/ec, which establishes the framework for community action on marine environment policy.
mr president, i have supported this report on renewable energy because it contains important suggestions for improving our current regulation. the commission must take account of the contributions and commitments made by the member states in terms of figures and deadlines and improve the monitoring of the policies they apply. it is essential to set new targets with percentages and deadlines, and to provide legal certainty and stability to a sector which innovates, invests and is a clear source of skilled employment. regulatory arbitrariness and retroactivity in spain, for example, have caused real damage to companies and entrepreneurs who have the potential and can bring changes to the spanish development model, the real basis of the country's employment and economic problems. the decarbonisation targets are now being met, but this approach jeopardises future possibilities. finally, i believe that a stronger commitment must be made to decentralized generation with renewable energy, self-consumption and storage, which are very important in promoting a fundamental change in the electricity sector. ensure supply, promote more responsible efficiency and consumption cultures and make their effects on co2 emissions more visible.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a new missed opportunity to bring about a real change in the energy policy of the member states. the report, although it contains a number of measures of interest which could lead to an improvement in the energy system, does not set specific objectives which would oblige the member states to implement a genuine energy conversion strategy. despite all its support for renewable energy, the report continues to consider biofuels as a renewable energy source, without taking into account the very serious food and environmental consequences of their mass cultivation. the european union needs a real binding and clear strategy for member states to exclude biofuels. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. − against. while today's vote sends a mixed message on eu renewable energy policy, meps have given strong backing to national support schemes for renewables and called for a binding 2030 eu target. they have sent a message to the commission and eu governments to act in order to capitalise on the economic and employment-creating potential of renewables. however, given the moves by energy commissioner oettinger to undermine renewables and prevent the commission from pushing for an ambitious target, we regret the failure by a majority of meps to explicitly vote for a nominal target of 40-45 % by 2030. this is an unfortunate dilution of the political signal that parliament is sending on renewables.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because it contains positive elements on the need to preserve and develop national systems of support for renewable energy, as well as mentioning the environmental, economic and diversification or decentralisation of energy production benefits of this industry. i regret, however, that the binding targets for the post-2020 timeframe have been rejected.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains important aspects for the judicial protection of gender equality in the balkan candidate countries for accession to the european union, it only considers legal aspects and not economic aspects, which are at the root of the problem. the report obliges the candidate countries to develop an institutional system to defend women's rights, but does not consider the impact of the economic opening of the common market on equality in these countries. economic equality is a key element of an effective gender policy and the policy of privatisation and liberalisation that comes with membership of the union has a major negative impact on economic inequality. that is why i abstained from voting on this report.
in writing. − in favour. in this report, the choice has been made to specifically address implementation mechanisms in accession countries instead of listing the problems concerning women’s rights and gender equality in general. the goal is to make concrete calls on countries to adapt their laws, policies, budgets and/or institutional frameworks, so that it is clear what is wanted from them to implement gender equality. therefore, issues like the shortcomings in health care systems for women and the lack of education aimed at eliminating gender stereotypes have been left outside of the scope of this draft report, as they are not addressed by specific implementation mechanisms established by authorities. violence against women is included for some countries, since in that area the governments may be called upon to provide a hotline, shelters, police protection and proper judicial handling of cases.
in writing. - as regards §5 (nominal vote 1): for women's participation in working life to be effective, it is not the 'disputed' quotas that are important but sustained and effective support for conciliation measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it can be a tool for promoting effective respect for freedom of expression and freedom of the press in the member states. this report contains a number of points of fundamental importance for the exercise of press freedom, from the obligation of pluralism to the prohibition of censorship. this report will also provide a new means of defending the profession of journalist in the european union. in spain we can see how these fundamental freedoms are being violated every day, with journalists being assaulted and detained by the police, journalists being fired for ideological reasons, etc. the spanish government will find in this report many difficulties in continuing to exert political pressure on the media sector. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - freedom of the press is one of the pillars of european democracy and contributes significantly to the configuration of the fourth estate. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the european institutions to protect the freedom of information of our citizens. the report proposes the establishment of a common regulatory framework for the media in the european union, stressing the importance of media pluralism and safeguarding their editorial independence. in addition, it is particularly important that member states protect cultural and language communities by allowing and encouraging access to media in these languages, as the report concludes.
in writing. − in favour. this ini, entitled ‘eu charter: standard settings for media freedom across the eu’, was decided in libe after the ep resolution on the media situation in hungary, where general outcry dictated the issue be addressed. libe organised a relevant hearing before adopting the report in committee. as problems with media freedom and pluralism exist in several member states, our group’s amendments included ‘naming and shaming’ countries on the basis of osce reporting and were consistent with our position of speaking out on specific issues in specific countries. the country-specific mentions did not pass in committee. however, the libe report underlines the importance and urgency of annually monitoring media freedom and pluralism in all member states and reporting on a yearly basis on the matter, in liaison with all stakeholders, both institutional and other. the ep believes that the commission, the fundamental rights agency and/or the eui centre for media pluralism and media freedom must carry out this task and publish an annual report with the results of the monitoring, which should be presented to parliament and the council and proposals made for any actions arising from conclusions in the report.
in writing. − the independence of journalists is crucial to ensuring free and ethical journalism. for this reason, i voted in favour of protecting journalists from both the internal pressures of the publishers and the external pressures of political and economic lobbyists. we must prevent other agents from being able to influence the content of the news. it is necessary to establish an annual monitoring system at european level on changes in national rules governing the media in order to avoid situations where journalistic independence may be endangered, such as that resulting from the hungarian media law of 2011. in this report we also denounce the effects of the crisis on the working conditions of journalists and call for their immediate improvement. quality and journalistic independence are at stake.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it is a new attack on the welfare state and the rights of european pensioners. the report introduces the principle of pension sustainability by introducing market economy criteria into the regulation of public pensions. the report also encourages member states to ban compulsory retirement so that workers can 'choose' to continue working. with the very serious unemployment among young people in the southern european countries, raising the retirement age is a real social crime that does not follow any social reasoning. the report also argues for the need to consolidate public budgets and even supports the implementation of individual pension schemes, thereby extending austerity to pension schemes. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. − abstention. the adoption of paragraph 58 – ‘regrets that third pillar systems are most often cost-intensive, more risky and less transparent than first-pillar system; calls for stability, reliability and sustainability for the third pillar’ – made us vote as we did.
in writing. − the current economic crisis has highlighted the vulnerability of public and private pension systems. we have voted today to adopt new measures to ensure the continuity of public pensions. it is necessary to ensure a decent standard of living for all citizens throughout their old age. among other proposals, i have advocated the creation of a combined pension system with a universal public pension, supplementary pensions established by collective agreement and individual savings schemes. in order to cope with the decline in the working population, which is causing a decline in the systems that support current pensions, it is important to extend the years of contribution of workers, as well as to strengthen reactivation policies that generate more contributors, training policies that generate higher quality jobs, and control policies to eradicate undeclared work. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report with the aim of finding new solutions to guarantee the quality of life of our citizens.

madam president, the establishment of economic and monetary union was not accompanied by a process of financial union, the gap between the overall functioning of financial markets and national control of financial institutions was not closed. supervisory powers and the essential aspects of deposit guarantee and resolution schemes have remained in the hands of the member states. this has weakened european financial stability, distorted the internal market and made it difficult to pass on the common monetary policy to households and businesses. the establishment of a european supervisory system, with european authorities coordinating national supervisors, and the forthcoming adoption of initiatives to establish common rules for bank resolution and progress on the harmonisation of deposit guarantees are going in the right direction, will improve the financial system and the smooth functioning of an internal market based on common rules, a single rule book. however, overcoming the crisis and perfecting economic and monetary union itself require going further. the breakdown of the link between private and sovereign debt, the normalisation of credit and the correct transmission of monetary policy in the euro area call for a banking union. the fiscal compact for debt sustainability and public finances should be complemented by a financial union for the flow of credit and the solvency of private entities. the commission's initiative to present two different legislative proposals, conferring powers on the european central bank and aligning its operation with that of the european banking authority, has always been seen as an inseparable package that had to be adopted with parliament's backing. parliament, aware of the priority and urgency of this initiative, has accelerated its processing and has done its best to secure a compromise, first within itself and then with the other institutions in the legislative procedure. as regards the reform of the european banking authority, consistency with the internal market has been ensured, the integration of the new mechanism into the european system of financial supervision has been ensured and, at the same time, the powers of the european banking authority have been increased. it has been agreed to draw up a supervisory manual, to establish stress tests and to establish rules which increase confidence among participating and non-participating countries in the single supervisory mechanism. the final result is reflected in this sitting: the negotiation has been concluded, a compromise has been reached which we can conclude with a final vote once the council confirms that it is in a position to do so. parliament is currently negotiating an interinstitutional agreement with the european central bank to ensure that it is subject to full parliamentary scrutiny and control in its new supervisory responsibilities. we will not accept a democratic deficit of transparency, accountability and parliamentary control in the single supervisory mechanism. when full judicial powers are assumed, full democratic responsibility must also be assumed.
mr president, we urgently need to implement the banking union, or at least its first pillar. i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteurs, mrs thyssen and mr giegold, on the great work they have done and also to thank the work done both by commissioner barnier and by the irish presidency, represented here by their minister creighton. we have set high expectations about the importance of banking union and it is therefore important to live up to those expectations and give massive support tomorrow to the amendments to the reports by mrs thyssen and mr giegold. this support is essential to ensure that the first pillar of the banking union, the single supervisor, is ready as soon as possible. the minister was talking about sending a message to the markets. i couldn't agree with her more. but it is also important to send a message to the citizens, and to see that their political representatives are looking for solutions to the crisis and looking for solutions to future crises. it is important to have the single supervisor ready to begin to defragment the financial markets and to ensure that credit reaches our small and mediumsized enterprises, and also to ensure that smes are financed on the basis of their economic situation and not on the basis of their geographical location. but it's also important to allow for the direct recapitalization of our banking system, and to get to break the vicious circle between sovereign debt and bank debt. in short, to show the citizens that we are working to solve their problems. and finally, i would like to say to mr barnier that we are looking forward to your new proposals on banking union.
mr president, mr commissioner, the experience of recent years has shown that banking union is a necessity and not an option, because national supervisors have proved to be insufficient, ineffective and, in some cases, blatantly negligent in assuming their supervisory functions. we need a single supervisory mechanism within the european central bank. in the electoral programme we adopted for the last european elections we already advocated the creation of this european monitoring service and the progressive communityization of fiscal and social policy, another subject on which we have made progress this morning in order to deepen the single market and to respect the principle of solidarity. we also believe that the european banking authority needs to be further strengthened to avoid, as the report says, a split between euro-zone and non-euro-zone countries in the rules applicable to the financial sector. it must therefore have the material and human resources to meet the difficulties and complexity of the task and must have real autonomy. we hope that no member state will ever again go from boasting of the strongest financial system in europe to presenting a map of craters in which, as far as we know, greedy scoundrels reigned supreme. the commission has therefore our full support in taking the appropriate measures and putting this mechanism into operation as soon as possible.
