mr president, in a month's time, at the diplomatic conference of the world intellectual property organization in marrakech, we will have a historic opportunity to redress a great injustice: the lack of access to culture for people with some visual impairment. according to the european union of the blind, which includes the spanish once, the european union's very restrictive and complex negotiating proposals have made it difficult to reach a comprehensive agreement on the treaty. according to the representatives of the european blind, the european positions have been and are serious political barriers to reaching an effective and agile final agreement in favour of blind people. i hope that the commission and the council will reconsider their much-criticised negotiating behaviour in the run-up to the forthcoming diplomatic conference.
mr president, let us say it loud and clear: the current copyright laws are responsible for the fact that millions of people with visual impairments and other reading difficulties are hungry for books. only 5% of published books are accessible in the formats appropriate for these people. this is in rich countries, because in poor countries it's less than 1%. the wipo treaty could remove these barriers posed by copyright laws. this is not a treaty, let us remember, to increase copyright protection for those who already have many other legal ways to defend their rights. however, the commission and the council insist on an inexistent and unfair balance between the visually impaired and the reading disabled on the one hand and the copyright holders on the other. based on this misperception, they have drawn up a long list in favour of industry which will, de facto, render the treaty unworkable and inoperative, as well as very expensive for millions of people, especially in poor countries. some publishing groups have also been lobbying the european parliament against the treaty for some time, betraying its commitment to blind people's organisations. the european commission also ignores the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, arguing that voluntary measures are more effective than mandatory ones. i therefore join the organizations calling on the commission and the council to stop obstructing the drafting of an effective treaty and to stop seeking an impossible and unfair balance between industry and one of the most marginalized groups in the world. in particular, we call for the withdrawal of recitals d and e on commercial availability for the implementation of the treaty, for the international distribution of personalised books to be allowed, for the use of technological measures to block the treaty to be prohibited and for the deletion of recital j on voluntary measures.
the author. - mr president, let us remember that the stockholm programme was adopted in december 2009 and it is now - through the legislature, when we have already passed the equator of this mandate - to assess the degree of compliance. we have put forward an oral question with which we intend to answer two fundamental questions. first, what have been the results of the programme to date? and secondly, what are the main elements that could inspire the programme that succeeds the stockholm five year programme 2009-2014? it is about ensuring an area of freedom, justice and security - that is true - but it is also about assessing what the consequences have been so far. we have seen progress in the area of the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons; we have seen a protracted but still unfinished negotiation - far from being completed - for the ratification of the european convention on human rights, which affects citizenship and fundamental rights; we have seen the copenhagen dilemma, the requirements of democracy, respect for the rule of law and the separation of powers in accession to the union, being raised in the most graphic manner, but, starting with accession to the union, a relaxation of controls with regard to the guarantee of democratic pluralism, respect for fundamental rights, transparency in access to documents. we are currently debating an ambitious data protection package with two parts - a regulation and a directive - which is also far from being finalized. we have seen challenges to the free movement of persons, including setbacks by some union governments, who are trying to rebuild the borders between member states, where citizens regarded free movement as one of the greatest achievements of the area of freedom, justice and security, including the construction of europe throughout its history. we also see how the advances in security - better protecting european citizens - pose unresolved challenges and we have seen how a crisis has emerged with great force, with great virulence, not only financial and economic but also political, of legitimacy and of leadership in the european union, with a crescendo of populisms that pose crude challenges to the values and founding principles of the european union. the question therefore is, with regard to the future of the stockholm programme, what can we do to inspire a five-year programme to succeed the stockholm programme, in the same way as there was a hague programme and before that a tampere programme? what programme will there be after stockholm to ensure that the european parliament plays a decisive role, as the treaty of lisbon requires? three years after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and three years after the adoption of the stockholm programme, it is therefore essential to provide a response that provides greater security for the fundamental rights of citizens. we see how - even today - the european union agency for fundamental rights excludes the evaluation of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. that is the subject of this debate. we want to know the commission's opinion so that we can answer the three questions put in the oral question. the credibility of the european project is at stake, the confidence of the electors and citizens in this european project, and we believe that we are close to the last opportunity to give them an answer on the subject of citizenship rights, which is the reason for europe. if we don't do it now, it may be too late when we try it in the next legislature.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i am very grateful to parliament for the opportunity to assess the implementation of the stockholm programme. your question is very wide in scope and, given the short amount of time available, i will only be able to give a limited response at this stage. nevertheless i hope that it will become clear that we have made, and continue to make, significant progress in this whole area. the jha council last december carried out a mid-term review of the stockholm programme. ministers’ discussions were based on an overview of progress drawn up by the cyprus presidency. this overview consisted of an assessment of progress in all areas covered by the stockholm programme – asylum and migration, civil and criminal justice, internal security, civil protection and external relations in the jha field. the council debate served as a response to the european council’s request, when it adopted the stockholm programme, for a mid-term review. the cyprus presidency subsequently informed the president of the european council in writing of the outcome of the council debate. it was noted in particular, and i quote, that ‘the debate in the council showed, in general, satisfaction with the progress made to date as well as confirmation of the need to take forward work on those elements of the stockholm programme which remain outstanding in order to continue to secure for our citizens an area of freedom, security and justice. the usefulness of a programme such as the stockholm programme was also underlined by a number of delegations as a guideline for defining legislative and operational priorities.’ the council debate also enabled ministers to reiterate their commitment to maintaining the right balance between security concerns and the protection of individual rights. i cannot provide an exhaustive list of the substantial number of measures which have been agreed since 2010, but i would like to highlight a few in particular. in the area of asylum and immigration, a comprehensive set of measures relating to the common european asylum system is being finalised and the european asylum support office has become operational. a joint eu resettlement programme was agreed and regional protection programmes further developed, and a directive on a single permit for third-country nationals to reside and work in member states was adopted. in terms of specific operational measures, the visa information system (or vis) was launched, the it agency became operational and sis ii went live last april. in the area of justice, the directive establishing minimum standards on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime was adopted and a regulation on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters was agreed. as far as internal security measures are concerned, a number of important directives were adopted. these include measures to ensure better protection against large-scale cyber attacks, strengthened measures for preventing on-line child sexual abuse in order to facilitate the prosecution of perpetrators and improve the protection of child victims, and a directive on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings. in general, the council takes the view that a particular focus should now be given to implementing legislation which has already been adopted and to ensuring that measures already agreed are made fully operational. as far as the institutional arrangements are concerned, the council considers that the application of the ordinary legislative procedure functions well, strengthening the commitment of both our institutions to cooperate in ensuring that the area of freedom, security and justice is completed and made fully operational. the instruments established under the lisbon treaty have already proved to be useful. a standing committee in the council ensures effective operational cooperation on internal security and other measures such as the solidarity clause, which will doubtless help to further strengthen cooperation in future. the establishment of the european external action service continues to contribute to ensuring good coordination where there is an external dimension to jha policies. overall i think we can look with some degree of satisfaction at what has been achieved under the stockholm programme. that, of course, should never lead us into complacency. this does not apply just to the council but also to parliament. i think both our institutions need to demonstrate in practice our commitment to making rapid progress on implementing the remainder of the stockholm programme and in fulfilling our shared objective of creating a more secure, open and fairer europe.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the speakers for this question, which asks the commission not only to list the results achieved during the stockholm programme but also to list the obstacles which the commission considers have been encountered in implementing this programme. i also note what mr berlinguer said. all right, there's this list, this list, but how much publicity has there been, how well has this program been implemented? the country i know, malta, joined the schengen system in 2007, and sometimes i think that today it is actually possible to drive a car from malta to stockholm without being stopped once. this is a great achievement of the european union, namely that these borders which in the past have created so many wars, such as the border between poland and germany or the border between gorizia and nova gorica, are today only lines on a map. this is not an abstract thing, this is a concrete thing. this is just one example, and it does not mean that there are no obstacles. one of the obstacles is the one mentioned by mr aguilar, namely the growth of nationalist populism in the worst sense of the term, that is to say, the introduction of obstacles to the free movement of persons under one pretext or another. this has been promoted with the idea that there is an attempt to demolish what has been built up with so much patience, with so many sacrifices, because for me the schengen system represents a milestone. we must be proud of this and must therefore always be vigilant and not introduce obstacles to the implementation of what i consider to be a legacy for future generations. i would like to thank the three members who asked this oral question on the implementation of the stockholm programme. three years ago the lisbon treaty and the charter of fundamental rights put european citizens at the centre of european integration. putting the citizen at the heart of the european union was a quantum leap, and the commission that took up its office in february 2010 put the necessary steps in motion to take such a leap. vice-president reding, who incidentally sends her sincere apologies because for personal reasons she could not be present here with us today, and my fellow commissioner malmström, had the opportunity to exchange views with the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) on the mid-term review of the stockholm programme last december. let me highlight some of the achievements. in the field of justice we have had major advances in the area of civil justice, taking steps to stimulate the single market. we call this the so-called justice for growth, which in simple terms means taking concrete action which helps to put europe back on the right track. for example, we have removed the costly and bureaucratic exequatur procedure in the brussels i regulation. judgments for one member state will automatically be recognised in another member state. we are also working on the insolvency package, which updates the current rules on cross-border insolvencies. we want viable business to get a second chance, also with a view to saving jobs. the data protection reform package which is on the table will reduce administrative burdens for businesses and ensure a high level of personal data protection, but we have also made concerted progress in the criminal justice field. we are particularly proud of the advances made in the field of victims' rights: the victims' rights directive, combined with the european protection order (criminal directive) and the european protection order (civil regulation), have improved the standing of victims of crime throughout the criminal procedure. we have also made considerable progress on strengthening procedural rights. the adoption and publication of the directive on the right to interpretation and translation, as well as the directive on the right to information, increases the support for persons in criminal proceedings across the union. i must say that this is a concrete achievement which is felt by the ordinary citizen, and i would like to thank parliament and the council for their joint efforts to conclude, very soon, the negotiations on the directive on access to a lawyer. fellow parliamentarians know that this is regulated in different ways, not only legally but also in its implementation in the member states. in the field of criminal law the commission has proposed minimum rules and minimum sanctions to protect the financial interests of the european union and the euro against counterfeiting. the aim is simple: to use criminal law to strengthen protection for common eu goods. we call on parliament to work on these proposals as a matter of priority. citizens' rights are an essential element of the european integration process. in this context, on 8 may 2013 we presented the eu citizenship report, the annual report on the eu charter of fundamental rights and the annual report on equality between women and men. the approach is to focus on the effective implementation of fundamental rights. in fact, the commission has even gone beyond the stockholm programme, which by its nature provides strategic guidelines. but that shouldn't be seen as a rigid corset. for example, in march 2013 the commission presented the eu justice scoreboard, which seeks to assist member states in the development of more effective justice. it provides objective, reliable and comparable data on the efficiency, quality and independence of the justice systems in all member states. some call it name and shame; i prefer to call it name and praise. it is an evolving tool and will gradually expand the indicators and the areas covered. in the field of home affairs, we can be proud of what we are close to achieving on asylum. at the next plenary, parliament is likely to vote on a common area of protection from oppression, violence, torture and fear of persecution, with common rules and common outcomes, where member states cooperate in a display of european solidarity. the visa information system and the second generation schengen information system have gone live and are now tools enabling the correct functioning of the border-free movement that europeans enjoy and, i hope, will continue to enjoy throughout most of our continent. we have a framework in place for local schengen cooperation and have put forward proposals for better governance of the schengen area and improved surveillance of our borders. we may now be close to an agreement on both of these. the frontex agency has a new mandate for more effective operation, with stronger guarantees on fundamental rights, and we have proposed a new mandate for europol, bringing it into the post-lisbon treaty era. we have adopted an internal security strategy and are regularly reporting on its implementation. we have concluded agreements on terrorist finance tracking with the united states and on pnr with the united states and australia. we have new directives in place against child sexual exploitation and trafficking in human beings. we have brought eu law into line with the un firearms protocol. we have put forward legislation on explosive precursors and a new eu policy and reporting mechanism against corruption. in line with our global approach on migration and mobility we have launched wide-ranging discussions with many of our neighbouring countries and have made good progress on visa facilitation, liberalisation and readmission. we have put forward proposals on third-country students and researchers as well as intra-corporate transferees and seasonal workers, while also developing a new agenda for integration of third-country nationals and furthering the debate on family reunification. there are still important tasks to achieve. we are, for example, working intensively on a proposal for a european public prosecutors office, which would be responsible for combating crimes affecting the financial interests of the union, and other issues such as anti-corruption policies or security in cyber space remain high on the agenda. justice and home affairs cover sensitive policy areas that were traditionally seen as solely a matter of national competence. the eu decision-making process is still adapting to the new legislative and institutional framework established by the lisbon treaty. we have made a lot of legislative proposals, but i would like to stress once again the importance of the effective enforcement of the legislation that we have put in place. one particular need which was acutely revealed in the last few months concerns the rule of law, and i will conclude with this comment. as president barroso said in his state of the union speech last september, we need a better-developed set of instruments - not just the two extremes between the soft power of political persuasion and the nuclear option of article 7 of the treaty. we need something in between. the commission hopes it can count on the support of parliament for creating a new mechanism enabling the european union to take effective action.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, the legitimacy of political systems, or political projects, is based on the results they provide to improve the daily lives and expectations of citizens, and also on the values to which those citizens subscribe, values which mark the identity of that political union. we know that the european union is not delivering good results for its citizens in terms of growth, in terms of employment, in terms of public policies. what about the values? because the european union is a political project based on freedom, based on solidarity, based on respect for the rights of those citizens, and the fundamental value is the sense of belonging, the knowledge of being part of a common territorial and political project. it will soon be three years since the adoption of the stockholm programme of action, and much progress has been made. both the commissioner and the council minister have referred to this. but i would like to point out three areas where there are problems: the first of these, free movement. the commissioner pointed out that from malta to stockholm, one could cross the continent without encountering any barrier to freedom of movement. but that is possible because very recently he has not crossed europe to go from germany to denmark, because there he would have had a brake, or because he is not an eastern european citizen going to the united kingdom, because there too he would have had a brake on freedom of movement. we know that there is a conflict between this parliament and the council on schengen, and we know that there are bad omens about the freedom established in schengen. the second, transparency. we have the issue of access to documents pending, and an oral question has been tabled in this very house on the blockage that is taking place. thirdly, the protection of citizens' rights. the commission has concluded negotiations with the council of europe on the convention. i would encourage the council, once we have the opinion of the court of justice of the european union, to conclude this process and better protect the rights of citizens.
mr president, in the absence of a review of the stockholm programme and its action plan, i would like to highlight only three issues, objectives not yet achieved, which affect the fight against terrorism and serious crime. firstly, i refer to the failure to implement article 75 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union as regards the freezing of assets and the use of internal terrorist lists in the european union, which has not been revised since 2009. secondly, the absence of legislative initiatives on the european system for monitoring the financing of terrorism. thirdly, and this is a very regrettable and recent development, the interruption of the first reading of the european pnr. i am pessimistic about the european public prosecutor's office, but the most serious thing, mr president, is the lack of interinstitutional agreement. what do i mean? i am referring to the lack of agreement on the use of delegated or implementing acts in the legislative procedure. there is no interinstitutional agreement, and this short-circuits and blocks the legislative task. i refer specifically to two dossiers in my possession: one on the revision of regulation no 539 and the other on the fight against the counterfeiting of the euro. but you only have to look at the schengen evaluation process to understand how important what i am saying is. either there is an urgent interinstitutional agreement or we will not be able to carry out effectively the legislative task entrusted to us - with value in terms of codecision - by the treaty of lisbon.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the protection of the rights of women is not restricted to the protection of the rights of men and women in the context of the fight against unemployment. the journey has been a pleasant and rewarding one, but there have also been significant obstacles along the way, which we have managed to overcome until we have reached our goal, which is to allow any victim of crime to obtain the recognition and the maximum possible protection within the territory of the european union. this regulation is part of the legislative package strengthening the rights of victims in the european union and complements the european protection order directive which ensures mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters. the combined application of the two instruments, criminal and civil, will allow persons who have obtained a protection order to move freely and safely throughout the european territory, including the united kingdom and ireland, which have also expressly requested to be included in this regulation. pursuant to article 3 of the treaty on european union, which will strengthen and develop the area of freedom, security and justice of the union, in accordance with the principle of mutual recognition, protection measures in civil matters adopted by a member state are to be recognised as civil measures in another member state. we've tried to simplify these protection orders as much as possible. a standardised, multilingual certificate has been drawn up to this end, containing most of the civil measures that could be agreed to protect the lives and physical and moral integrity of victims. if the protected person is not physically present in the home member state, he/she has the possibility to request the certificate online, by fax or by any other technical method. it is also intended that the protected person should not have to bear the financial costs associated with the recognition of the protection measure in another member state. this is an administrative procedure which is easily obtainable by victims and also protects them when travelling and being transferred to other countries. the recognition of the measure and the application for the certificate do not require the presence of a legal representative or a lawyer, which - as you will understand - greatly reduces costs and thus makes life easier for our citizens. we have found it easier and more appropriate to create a european union-wide database of protection measures and certificates issued. this will ensure that national authorities have secure and rapid access to the required information and secure and rapid cross-border protection. in this way, a victim of a terrorist offence who has obtained a restraining order from the offender, for example in a civil action, and who moves to travel or live in sweden, can apply through this certificate for the enforcement of the agreed civil action before the swedish authorities, in accordance with this regulation. for example, a portuguese victim of gender-based violence who has been declared as such by a portuguese court and who has also been granted a series of protection measures, such as a restraining order against the offender or a ban on communication between the offender and the victim, may move to a territory, say, romanian, where the authorities of this country will immediately enforce the measures agreed by the portuguese judicial body, through the multilingual standardised certificate that the victim can request from romania by any electronic means and by registering the victim in the european register of victims without any need for legal assistance. the rapporteur and i want to see these measures of recognition spread as widely as possible throughout the union, and we call on all member states to work together to achieve this. we also propose that these protection measures be made available on the e-justice portal, which is installed in all eu countries. i do not want to conclude, with the commissioner present, without thanking, of course, the cooperation, very good cooperation, which we have obtained both from the directorate-general for justice of the european commission and from the cypriot and irish presidencies. i would also like to make a special mention of my colleagues in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and the committee on women's rights and gender equality and, above all, antonia parmanova, an efficient and hardworking member of parliament from bulgaria, who, together with this spanish member, i believe we have been able to make life a little easier for our citizens. i hope that at this moment this kind of recognition, these kinds of measures and our attempt to bring the citizens much closer to the european union will be recognised by them.

on behalf of the verts/ale group. – madam president, allow me first of all to congratulate our colleagues lópez-istúriz white and parvanova for having led that important debate. it has been said, and i fully agree, that this is not a minor issue, especially for those women who suffer gender-based violence. according to the council of europe around 20% to 25% of european women experience physical acts of violence at least once during their adult life. 12 to 15% find themselves in a relationship of domestic abuse and more than 10% suffer sexual violence. according to eurostat, the rate of unreported crime is 60%, and according to the european women’s lobby, violence against women affects approximately 45% of all women across europe; an estimated one-fifth of women in the european union suffer from violence. seven women die every day from violence of this kind. the annual cost of this kind of violence in the european union could be as high as eur 16 billion. this is not, i repeat, a minor issue. this regulation is thus intended to apply to protection measures ordered with a view to protecting the person when there are serious grounds for considering that that person’s life, physical or psychological integrity, personal liberty, security or sexual integrity is at risk: for example, in order to prevent any form of gender-based violence or violence in close relationships such as physical violence, harassment, sexual aggression, stalking, intimidation or other forms of indirect coercion. the aim of the regulation is to establish an efficient recognition mechanism to ensure that all protection measures taken in civil matters in the member state concerned can circulate freely throughout the european union. this is important because it affects all kinds of victims, and it also includes any obligations or prohibitions imposed on the person causing the risk, such as a prohibition or regulation on entering the place where the protected person resides, works or visits, or stays regularly. that is why i would like to offer my congratulations on the job done, and i fully expect that the member states will recognise that this important measure should be implemented as soon as possible.

mr president, commissioner, when we built the euro area we knew that it suffered from certain imperfections due to the fact that we shared a single monetary policy and not a fiscal union and, even less, a political union. this triggered a lack of coordination already highlighted in the kok report of 2005. the 2008 crisis has exacerbated these imperfections, but, let us be positive, it has also given us the opportunity not only to overcome them, but to improve the whole architecture of the euro and of the european union. with the design of the euro area we are skipping the traditional philosophy of the european union since its inception: to move forward step by step, to move forward in stages, to deliver what is agreed. now that we know what our shortcomings have been, we are returning to this philosophy, whereby one of the great challenges is to create a true economic union. the banking union is one of the priority areas in which we must make progress within the economic union, as we saw yesterday in this house, but it is only one step, which shows the solidarity that is so important. solidarity is not yet automatically established, but it is constantly being called for in european law. my colleague and friend mr gauzès put it very well when he called for the social dimension. the proof of this is the decisive and agile action needed in the times of distrust we are living in. the ex ante coordination of economic reforms and the convergence and competitiveness instrument are key to automating the solidarity needed by countries that share the same currency but which at times still seem to lack a common horizon. in this respect, it is important that ex ante coordination applies to the euro member states, but without diminishing their responsibility to pursue reform processes. the convergence and competitiveness instrument should be combined with a financial incentive mechanism with budgetary capacity to avoid the previous failures. the two instruments are a further but necessary step towards the much needed economic union and, in short, political union. that's why this resolution is so important.
mr president, the performance of the european economy since the establishment of economic and monetary union has been unsatisfactory. member states have not delivered on the commitments of the stability and growth pact, the union has not achieved the objectives of the lisbon strategy, and europe is the area of the world that is responding the worst to the challenges of the crisis. the policies of indiscriminate adjustment have led to job losses, economic contraction, higher total indebtedness and have opened cracks within the union. the economic and monetary union must evolve by integrating responsibility and solidarity, discipline and encouragement. the proposals to move towards ex ante economic coordination are in the right direction, but they must be part of a common economic policy framework. it is also necessary to make way for a policy of investment incentives in this common economic policy framework, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, to improve competitiveness. but to improve competitiveness in a multi-factor way, european cooperation must be based on a social pact, on fiscal resources beyond those provided for in the multiannual financial perspective and under democratic control. and, in addition, to restore growth, credit initiatives will be needed to improve the sustainability of public finances and to revive growth.

madam president, commissioner, economic and monetary union must strengthen the european social model, which is the hallmark of our union. it is a way of doing, of working, of progressing, which is a reference in the world. europe means development, but with values, and it is a project for the people. so the principle of social cohesion, together with sustainability and knowledge, forms the tripod on which strategy 2020 sits to re-launch us as a global power. economic and monetary union is one more instrument to maintain this position, a tool to counter with guarantees social dumping and the lurking of financial speculation. in the face of the image of europe imposing austerity and cuts, we need to rediscover the europe which has meant for the 27 member states an objective improvement in the living conditions and the list of rights of their citizens. mr commissioner, an economic and monetary union will only succeed if it is built on a human scale, on the basis of solidarity, trust, employment, recognition and respect for all those who aspire to form it, with shared standards and instruments that provide the strength of unity in the face of the global challenge and the opportunities of diversity to share and exploit all available knowledge. let us return to the foundations of our strength and, commissioner, as you have heard today, put in place the most effective tools to ensure that we do not forget the people who are having such a hard time in this situation in europe.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i was asked by president barroso and commissioner andor to take this policy debate. i agreed to change my agenda and reschedule meetings in brussels which were intended for preparing the package of country-specific recommendations for next week, because i place such a strong emphasis and importance on the social and employment agenda of the european union and on the social dimension of the economic and monetary union. let me comment on a few issues that have been raised by several speakers, starting with ms cornelissen, who referred to the scoreboard and how to strengthen the social dimension in economic governance. in my view, there is scope for better catering for the social dimension of the emu in the existing instruments of economic governance. for instance, a scoreboard of employment and social indicators built around existing instruments would help in detecting situations of social distress or social imbalances to which you and many others referred, and would trigger early corrective action through employment and economic policies. this enhanced surveillance would help first to provide greater visibility to the social policy dimension when taking macro-economic decisions at the level of europe and the member states. second, it would also strengthen the monitoring of employment and social policies in order to identify and enable the alleviation of major difficulties in good time. i believe we have much to learn from each other in the member states within the european union. benchmarking of best practice already takes place in the employment and social coordination mechanisms. this could be further developed to support the ex ante coordination of major economic reforms. the social dimension of the emu could also be reflected in the competitiveness and convergence instrument, as long as it involved forms of financial support for such measures as help facilitate the implementation of difficult reforms. for instance, a member state which commits to implementing a difficult pension reform could in principle receive support for a lifelong learning programme to improve the employability of older workers. many of you referred to the role of the social partners. it goes without saying that the social dimension of the emu is also about reinforcing the role of social partners. in the short term, suitable involvement and participation of social partners in policy debates and policy-making processes could already help increase ownership and enhance the effectiveness of policies and their coordination at euro area level. the involvement and consultation of social partners at national level is, of course, essential and should be further developed, and that is the responsibility of the member states. i said in my opening remarks that we need to do whatever it takes to combat the unemployment crisis, especially youth unemployment, and for that we need, in the immediate short term, concrete action and policy initiatives, especially in fighting youth unemployment. here we have the initiative of the youth guarantee scheme, which is based on good experience and good results in, for instance, the nordic countries. it gives the young person a guaranteed chance to get either a job or a place in education or on a training course and thus improves his or her employability and helps him or her when returning to the labour market once the economic situation improves. this is, to my mind, a kind of best practice that can be utilised in europe as a whole, and we need to really focus on the youth guarantee scheme and move it forward. i also want to point out that for the next multiannual financial framework the commission has proposed that at least 25% of cohesion policy funding be allocated to the european social fund (esf) and that the budget of the esf will increase by 10%, which is eur 84 billion. the task of the european social fund is to increase employment opportunities, promote education and lifelong learning, enhance social inclusion and contribute to combating poverty. moreover it has been proposed that at least 20% of total esf resources in each member state be allocated to the objective of promoting social inclusion and combating poverty. arvoisa puhemies, lopuksi pari sanaa suomeksi, koska jäsen jaakonsaari nosti esiin hyvin tärkeän kysymyksen. hän korosti, että meidän ei pitäisi asettaa vastakkain talous- ja rahaliiton taloudellista ja sosiaalista ulottuvuutta. olen samaa mieltä, asia on juuri näin. euroopan yhteiskunnallinen ja taloudellinen malli perustuu siihen, että me kykenemme saamaan taloutemme toimimaan tehokkaasti ja luomaan työpaikkoja ja samaan aikaan me pidämme huolta heikommassa asemassa olevista ja tarjoamme heille yhdenvertaiset mahdollisuudet menestyä yhteiskunnassa ja työelämässä. meidän on nyt työskenneltävä näiden molempien ulottuvuuksien puolesta ja tältä kannalta tämä talous- ja rahaliiton sosiaalinen ulottuvuus on hyvin tärkeä ja keskeinen. komissio tulee pian tekemään tästä konkreettisia ehdotuksia.
madam president, i would remind the house that in april my political group asked that neither the debate nor the vote on the resolution on guantanamo should be taken up at that plenary session, given its proximity to the terrorist attack in boston. mr swoboda proposed that we continue the debate and that the vote be held at this part-session. since that debate has already taken place, madam president, under rule 122 of the rules of procedure, i ask that that commitment be honoured and that the debate not be held again, because it already took place at the april partsession, and that parliament therefore vote tomorrow on the resolution on guantánamo alone.
we support these two reports, madam president, because we share their general principles, particularly in the fight against tax fraud and evasion, in shifting taxation to more growth-friendly areas and in providing fiscal incentives for the selfemployed and small and mediumsized enterprises, especially with a view to encouraging innovation and research and development activities. we also found that they intelligently combine the global and the local in a field where the european level is essential and where proximity is also useful in order to improve control and boost the real economy. we therefore support the need to combine our efforts to combat unfair tax competition and tax havens at global level. but at the same time we welcome the explicit mention of the role that the principles of subsidiarity and multi-level governance should play in the implementation of sound european taxation. we believe that this mention is an express endorsement of institutions such as the basque concert or the navarre convention, which have proved effective in channelling potential towards economic and social growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to promote and strengthen the fight against tax havens from the community level in order to boost public revenue in the member states. it is not the first time that the european parliament has spoken out against the fiscal gap in this respect, but the other european institutions and the member states have made no progress in this area. this type of report is never put into practice because the governments of the member states, the commission and the council prefer to push through austerity policies in order to privatise strategic public sectors, leaving public services and fundamental rights of european citizens in the hands of capital in order to create new investment sectors for companies and banks. i voted in favour of this report, although i know that it will not be implemented because it contains measures against tax evasion which the iu maintains in all its fields.
in writing. − in favour. among other things, this report calls for member states to implement the commission’s two recommendations, for the eu to lead internationally, for tax treaties between member states and developing countries to be based on common standards with a view to avoiding base erosion for those countries, for a halving of the tax gap by 2020, and for tax administrations to be strengthened. the report welcomes the us foreign account tax compliance act (fatca) while calling for the data protection rights of eu citizens to be respected. it also calls for the generalisation, extension and internationalisation of automatic information exchange; the introduction of a mandatory common consolidated corporate tax base; revision in 2013 of two key directives that facilitate corporate tax dodging; cross-sector country-by-country reporting; an obligation to create public registries of the beneficial ownership of companies, trusts and foundations (codifying offshore leaks); substantive requirements for notification and publication of tailored tax rulings; broad tax haven identification criteria, with a corresponding eu blacklist to be published by the end of 2014; the adoption of comprehensive measures against vat fraud, in particular carousel fraud; and assistance to developing countries. however, some provisions are still missing or are weaker than we had wanted: for example, the black list in 2014, and the reference to ‘several’ criteria for the classification of a jurisdiction as a tax haven, where one should have been sufficient.
in writing. - tax havens are the black holes of globalisation. tax fraud and tax evasion cost the european union €1 trillion in lost tax revenue each year. this bleeding causes an unfair distribution of the tax burden and distorts markets and fair competition. it provides cover for the black economy and other illicit activities, affects financial stability and weakens tax systems. its effects are particularly pernicious in these times of crisis by diminishing social protection capacity, holding back growth and sustainable employment and undermining fiscal consolidation efforts. it is important that the european council at its next meeting should promote decisive action in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. my amendments, which are included in the resolution we adopted this morning, call for the automatic exchange of information between administrations, the introduction of european taxes for companies operating across borders and the non-recognition within the eu of companies set up in non-cooperative jurisdictions. i am in favour of companies that evade or have committed tax fraud not being able to participate in public tenders, and i support the whole of the resolution that has been adopted.
in writing. - tax fraud and evasion at eu level amount to €1 trillion each year. in addition to having a negative impact on member states' budgets, it gives a competitive advantage to tax evaders while reducing taxpayers' confidence. although the fight against tax fraud is a matter for the member states, i believe that a coordinated framework at eu level is needed to adapt to globalised markets and the interconnected economy. in this respect, i support all the measures proposed in this report, in particular the reduction of fraud by half by 2020, the promotion of transparency and the exchange of information in tax matters.
in writing. - i voted against this report because, although it contains certain points of interest relating to the fight against tax fraud, it introduces neoliberal governance principles in the coordination of the member states' tax policies. the report makes some points on the fight against tax evasion which could be shared, but it then introduces all the concepts of economic governance which are the product of the neoliberal ideology which has led us to the crisis we are suffering today. the report reaffirms the need to clean up public finances without even mentioning the plundering of public funds that the rescue of the financial sector has entailed, ignoring the real cause of the increase in public debt: the rescues of the banks. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour. the recent debt crisis has raised several new problems in the european union, which require the proper adjustment of tax policies in the short, medium and long term. some of the countries have already made these adjustments, while others are still ahead of them. it should be emphasised that tax policy remains a competence of national sovereignty and that the different tax systems of the member states have therefore to be respected, whilst the barriers of the internal market and the uncertainties and misunderstandings originating from the legal gaps should be suppressed as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is intended to speed up the political procedures so that the government of the czech republic can implement protocol no 30 to the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. normally, the acceptance of such a protocol by the czech republic would have to be implemented in the treaties of the european union through the conclusion of a convention, which would imply a significant economic, temporal and political cost for an amendment affecting only one member state. the amendment favours the application of the fundamental rights of the european union in the czech republic and therefore improves the defence of these rights in that member state. this justifies the speeding up of the complex and slow political procedure. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union was drafted by a convention held from 17 december 1999 to 2 october 2000, bringing together representatives of parliament, the member states, national parliaments and the commission. the charter was proclaimed on 7 december 2000 and its text was adapted at strasbourg on 12 december 2007. a second convention was held from 22 february 2002 to 18 july 2003 to draft the treaty establishing a constitution for europe, most of the substance of which was incorporated into the lisbon treaty, which entered into force on 1 december 2009. both conventions were convened to address major issues concerning the constitutional order of the union, including the adoption of a binding text setting out the fundamental rights and principles recognised by the union. in the light of the above, it is not necessary to call a convention in order to examine the proposal that protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and to the united kingdom be extended to the czech republic, as the effect of that proposal, if any, would be limited. thus, the ep approves the european council’s proposal not to convene a convention.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it respects the institutional process for the czech government to be able to apply protocol no 30 to the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the acceptance of that protocol by the czech republic should be implemented in the treaties of the european union through the consultation of the european parliament. the report supports the implementation of protocol no 30, which will improve the protection of eu fundamental rights in the czech republic. this justifies support for the procedure for the application of the protocol in that country. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. protocol no 30 does not exempt the uk and poland from the binding provisions of the charter. it is not an ‘opt-out’. it does not amend the charter. at face value, the protocol would seem not to alter the legal position which would prevail if it were not to exist. yet the very existence of the protocol has given rise to legal uncertainty and political confusion. in that respect, it affects adversely all member states and not just the uk, poland or, prospectively, the czech republic. what is perfectly clear, moreover, is that were protocol no 30 ever to be interpreted as having the effect of limiting the scope or force of the charter’s provisions, the result would be to lower the protection of fundamental rights afforded to people in poland and the uk, and would therefore undermine the efforts of the eu to reach and maintain a uniformly high level of protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in the crossborder protection of victims of crime. the report seeks to develop a european protection order for victims so that all member states of the european union will recognise a protection order issued in any of the countries of the union. the european protection order aims to improve the situation of legally protected persons when they move to another eu country, especially those who have been victims of gender-based violence. in this case the report extends protection to civil matters relating to matrimonial property and other types of conflicts which may arise with national legislation where a european protection order exists. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. i fully support the overall concept of the regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures, but consider it imperative to further address the issue of victims of gender-based violence. to this end, i back the report’s approach of making a reference to provisions in the proposal for a directive on victims’ rights. in order to better provide for the needs of victims of gender-based violence, officials likely to come into contact with cases where a person’s physical, psychological and sexual integrity is considered to be at risk – particularly cases of violence against women – should be appropriately trained. the work of civil society, particularly ngos, women’s associations and other voluntary organisations providing specialist support is recognised by the rapporteurs, and member states are encouraged to support the work of, and collaborate with, such organisations in providing support to victims of violence, and particularly female victims.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves an improvement in the existing rules on customs controls in trade relations between the european union and canada. the report specifically addresses improving the safety and information of the methods of operation of supply chains to ensure safety conditions and information exchange in the trade of potentially dangerous substances. this report is only intended to improve these safety conditions to avoid potential risks that may occur in the supply chain, through the exchange of information. the report improves the regulation on the control of potentially dangerous materials. i think that this point needs to be included in international trade agreements. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the customs relations between the eu and canada are based on the agreement on customs cooperation and mutual assistance in customs matters that has been in force since 1998. the new agreement extends cooperation to matters related to supply chain security, while building on horizontal provisions and principles of the 1998 agreement; so it is in practice a broadening of the current cooperation and contractual relationship. the framework established by the new agreement does not go beyond cooperation in the areas of information and data exchange, cargo inspections, the elaboration of minimum common standards as main areas. the agreement only sets the basis for working and cooperating towards establishing mutual recognition in some control areas, without however providing the legal basis for mutual recognition arrangements to be set up within the framework thereof.
in writing. − the system of banking authorities and the prudential supervision of credit institutions needs to be revised to take account of the changing economic and financial environment and the need to provide liquidity to the european banking system, with particular reference to the situation of certain member states whose finances are in critical condition. i believe that the banks must be given back their role of supporting policies for the development of the territory and, therefore, of facilitating investment. this can be achieved by implementing a sustainable system of checks and balances which combines the urgent need for a sound banking system with the equally urgent need to relax the constraints of a european economic policy which has been too rigid and which has also affected the work of credit institutions.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a new attack on the economic sovereignty of the member states of the european union. the report sets out rules to improve the functioning of financial sector control, seeking to avoid bailouts by the public sector and the banks themselves guaranteeing the sector's deposits, and introduces good initiatives in matters of prudential supervision of the sector, but is based on the transfer of sovereignty to the european banking authority which will be the one to set the criteria and objectives. this is an institution which, in the name of market neutrality, will impose on the member states the conditions laid down by financial capital. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the banking sector is not left to the mercy of the banks. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour of the amended proposal, and in favour of postponing the vote on the legislative resolution, as suggested by the rapporteur, mr giegold. on the content, i have followed the line of the rapporteur. instead of sticking to the narrow ‘strictly ssm-related’ changes proposed by the council, we insisted that, in addition to the ecb being treated as other supervisors in the eba, there were a number of points concerning boosting the effectiveness of the eba as the ‘guardian of the single rule book’ for banking supervision that could not await the review scheduled to start in 2013. in particular we tabled amendments addressed at: improving the information gathering powers of the eba in the light of the poor experience of stress testing; ensuring that there are regular annual stress tests of banks under the eba’s overall control; requiring the eba to produce a handbook of best practice supervision to supplement the ‘what?’ of the ‘rulebook’ with a ‘how?’; requiring the eba to promote a diverse banking sector; and ensuring that an appropriate balance is achieved in the voting mechanisms on different decisions, between the ‘home’ country supervisors of a bank and the ‘host’ supervisors of its subsidiaries and branches as well as between the supervisors in the ssm and those outside.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis, as we know, has brought the banking system of some member states to a standstill and at the same time tested its resilience in others. we have repeatedly proposed as an institution a change in the powers of the european central bank, convinced that at this historic moment we need a european credit institution that is strengthened and effective in its action to support the credit institutions of the individual states. in this sense, the lowering of the interest rate threshold was certainly a first step forward. to stimulate growth and development, however, this is not enough: the ecb must guarantee european stability and strength while at the same time ensuring that the public accounts and the accounts of the main national credit institutions are kept.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a new attack on the economic sovereignty of the member states of the european union. the report calls for the transfer of specific powers in banking supervision to the european central bank. for years the national banks had the task of supervising and controlling the national financial sectors and, in almost criminal practices, they have evaded their responsibilities by allowing all kinds of evil practices in those sectors. in the case of spain, the illegal marketing of products, the use of abusive clauses and all kinds of excesses by the banking sector have been carried out with the connivance of the banco de españa, which has completely ignored its functions. the improvement of prudential control in the sector is achieved by bringing the responsible to justice and to prison, not by transferring powers to the ecb. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour of the amended proposal, and of postponing the final vote on the legislative resolution. and this despite the fact that some good verts/ale amendments were rejected, such as: giving opt-in countries the right to control decisions in the ecb through a binding mediation procedure in the eba; integrating the ecb’s fees into the european budget, thereby enhancing ep control; ending the possibility of the ecb to adopt ‘regulations’ (the final compromise was to limit these regulations to ‘only where those union acts do not deal with certain aspects necessary for the proper exercise of the ecb’s tasks or do not deal with them in sufficient detail’ – which is more constrained that in the com proposal); and considering another legal base or treaty change to render the common supervisor even more attractive for opt-in countries and solve conflicts of interests as well as the exclusion of insurance. (the final compromise requires a review that must consider ‘developing further the ssm on the basis of any provision in the existing treaties or the treaty changes potentially required in order to make the ssm work more efficiently’ – which is, of course, much weaker).
in writing. - this report, which is one of the two legislative drafts establishing the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) for banks, headed by the european central bank (ecb), is a very important step towards the 'banking union'. in particular, the proposal provides for the ecb to be given responsibilities for the preventive supervision of euro area credit institutions. the bank shall also have exclusive competence to monitor and detect risks to the viability of banks and may require action in this regard. although i support all the measures proposed in the report, the final vote has not been taken, pending the views of certain national parliaments and the conclusion of some interinstitutional negotiations between the european parliament and the ecb.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a substantial improvement in the safety and compulsory information required of the various pyrotechnic products used in europe. there are cultural practices in the use of this type of material, such as the fallas de valencia, which are not affected by the fact that this is a report that has no prohibitionist intention but seeks to regulate the obligations of information, control and authorization. improved legislation in this area, setting similar standards in all member states to ensure the safe handling of these products, is a step forward in ensuring safety without limiting free use. there are many cultural events in spain which use a wide variety of such products and this report guarantees reasonable safety standards without prohibiting such practices. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. this report makes modifications to a proposal of the european commission recasting directive 2007/23/ec on the placing on the market of pyrotechnic articles. it was presented in november 2011 in the framework of the implementation of the new legislative framework (nlf) adopted in 2008 as ‘the goods package’ covering the complementary instruments, decision 768/2008 on a common framework for the marketing of products, and repealing council decision 93/465/eec, and regulation 765/2008 setting out the requirements for accreditation and market surveillance relating to the marketing of products and repealing regulation (eec) no 339/93. the present proposal is part of a package, aligning nine product directives to the nlf.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a good source of information on the way in which the member states of the union regulate audiovisual media services. the report critically analyses how the aforementioned regulation is being implemented and includes a serious warning about the countries monitored. the study acknowledges the technical advances which the development of the sector at european level has brought in recent years with the development of numerous channels, but does not leave aside the question of content. the study acknowledges shortcomings in the control of serious offences that may affect the protection of children, the promotion of alcoholic beverages, the promotion of hatred, etc. this report is a good tool to show the reality of the sector in the union. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the implementation of the audiovisual media services directive because i believe above all that the eu must have a legislative framework that guarantees all citizens of europe access to information and to a plurality of opinions. these are essential elements for our european democracy. i fully agree with the idea that european regulations on this subject should be standardised, especially when it comes to standardising upwards, always with a view to strengthening the freedom of information of citizens.
in writing. − in favour. the main aim of the report is to evaluate the effectiveness of directive 2010/13/eu on audiovisual media services and the progress made in its transposition. the directive is the cornerstone of media regulation in the european union. under article 33, the commission is required to submit a report to the european parliament on the application of the directive in the member states every three years. publication of the commission’s first report was significantly delayed owing, inter alia, to the fact that some member states had not fully transposed the directive within the indicated deadline.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, this is a crisis that has brought unspeakable suffering to the people of syria and has already gone beyond syria’s borders, dramatically destabilising the whole region. the european union has consistently supported the vision of a political settlement outlined in the geneva communiqué. high representative and vice-president ashton has officially expressed her full support for the joint call made by united states secretary of state, john kerry, and russian foreign minister lavrov to convene an international peace conference on syria as soon as possible as a follow-up to the geneva conference of june 2012. keeping the political track alive is paramount for the european union. next week’s foreign affairs council discussion will take stock of where we stand, while also tackling the politically sensitive issue of adapting the european union sanctions regime. the european union should continue its engagement with the national coalition for syrian revolutionary and opposition forces while remaining open to cooperation with other moderate groups. the european union urges all parties to the conflict to fully respect international humanitarian and human rights law and condemns terrorist attacks of any nature, including any assaults that may endanger the civilian population. the number of people in need of assistance in syria – we are talking about 4.25 million internally displaced people – and the number of refugees – some 1.5 million – arriving in the neighbouring countries continues to grow at an exponential pace. the unhcr estimates that, by the end of 2013, the number of syrian refugees will have reached 3.5 million, with 1 million refugees in each of lebanon, jordan and turkey and a further 500 000 in iraq. were this to be the case, it would mean that, by the end of this year, syrian refugees would account for 25% of the lebanese population and 16% of the jordanian population. the sharp increase in the number of refugees has increased the humanitarian needs at an alarming rate, outpacing current relief efforts and assistance. the economic costs of hosting syrian refugees were estimated in 2013 at usd 700 million for lebanon and usd 851 million for jordan, respectively 1.6% and 2.9% of the gdp of countries which are already heavily indebted. the cost to turkey so far has been about eur 600 million and is expected to reach eur 1 billion by the end of the year. to respond to this challenge, the united nations is expected to issue a revised appeal for at least usd 3 billion in june 2013, their largest appeal ever for a single crisis. to address these exploding needs, the european union has repeatedly increased its funding to become the first donor, with eur 860 million of assistance pledged, of which most has already been disbursed. standing tall, the european union has repeatedly called on all donors to deliver on existing pledges and to increase their contributions. we are improving coordination among donors and welcome the assistance coordination unit’s efforts as regards using all channels to provide assistance everywhere in syria. we will work to strengthen this syrian-led effort and will work tirelessly to improve access for our aid. we are also working intensively to mobilise significant additional funds this year with a view to addressing the plight of the refugees and stabilising syria’s neighbouring countries. this will require a long-term commitment and a regional approach. to better coordinate our efforts, the commission and the european external action service, together with the member states, are working on a comprehensive response to the crisis, which will also include dealing with the threats stemming from the potential use of chemical weapons, the presence of european fighters in the country and the provision of international protection to syrians in the european union.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, although the humanitarian situation, as the commissioner has just explained to us, is terrible, with over 100 000 dead, six million internal and external refugees, my group would have preferred that this debate had taken place in the wake of the latest events: the statements by the president of france and the minister of defence of that country, before yesterday in the committee on foreign affairs; the opposition conference which took place yesterday in madrid; the press conference to be held tomorrow in jordan by the united states secretary of state; the arab league meeting; the next opposition meeting in istanbul; the expiry of the embargo on 31st of this month; and, of course, mr president, the geneva conference, following the announced meeting between the united states secretary of state and the russian foreign minister. but here the question is what the position of the parties will be. president. - the next item is the report (a4-0173/97) by mr pimenta, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, security and defence policy, on the situation in the middle east. and one wonders what the position will be of other actors, such as israel, iran, turkey, qatar, or saudi arabia, who have conflicting interests. in the meantime, the humanitarian situation is worsening, atrocities are taking place in this country and i think, commissioner, that, beyond humanitarian aid, we should ask ourselves what we can do. there is a clear difference between russia's position and that of the rest of the western world on the future of assad, but beyond that difference there is a convergence in the international community to avoid chaos in syria - even though we are already very close to a situation of chaos - and a radical islamist regime. let us take advantage of this convergence to seek concrete short-term solutions to put an end to this massacre and these atrocities. and it seems, commissioner, that, except in the field of humanitarian aid, where the european union is doing so, given its possibilities, frankly, the european union is being left out of the political solution.
mr president, the situation in syria is deteriorating dramatically, to the consternation of a europe plunged into the worst crisis in its history, which unfortunately also limits our capacity to respond. i had the honour of chairing a delegation from the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to jordan to assess the situation of refugees, particularly in zaatari camp, where there are about 100,000 people, mostly women and children, and which has been described, indeed, as one of the largest cities in jordan at the moment. this situation raises a lot of capacity problems for jordan, which is showing generosity, but needs financial support. for many of us, the european union must increase it in a way that is both expected and, in the view of many, unstoppable. the resolution we are debating today also raises the need to keep the borders open to syrian and palestinian refugees. but above all, it calls for cooperation in fair burden-sharing, cooperation with the neighbouring arab countries and, of course, emphasis on maintaining law and order and respect for human rights and security in the refugee camp, so that intolerable human rights violations do not occur. finally, we also call on the member states to take on the refugee influx and reception programme that will have to be addressed if we are to live up to the impressive human and humanitarian drama that the syrian crisis is posing for the european union.
madam president, in the face of this humanitarian tragedy, i express my solidarity with the displaced and refugees from syria, with the women and girls sold for 2 500 euros to old saudis, with the children, with the elderly. i have proposed, and i am proposing here, madam, that we do what we did with the libyan displaced. then we went to the shousha camps. today i propose that the libe committee, which is responsible for this matter, should go to the fields of jordan, lebanon and turkey. they have to feel us. we must show the unequivocal solidarity of the european parliament and the european union, and we must explain what is happening to parliament, to the community institutions and to the world, firsthand. and, madam president, we must open our doors to this tragedy. we must open the door to resettlement and settlement for refugees, for the libyan vulnerable, especially children and women.
