in writing. − in favour. in the 2014 european elections 12 eu member states will each lose one seat and none will gain any. these reductions are needed in order to comply with the 751-seat limit set by the lisbon treaty and to make room for croatia’s meps. the draft european council decision, approved by parliament by 574 votes to 71, with 39 abstentions, leaves unchanged the redistribution of seats between member states proposed by meps on 13 march 2013. after parliament’s consent, the text still needs to be formally adopted by all eu heads of state and government at the 27-28 june summit. the proposed solution means that 12 member states – austria, belgium, bulgaria, croatia, czech republic, greece, hungary, ireland, latvia, lithuania, portugal and romania – will each lose one seat at the next european elections. the remaining three seats have to come from germany, whose share must go down from 99 seats to 96, the maximum allowed by the lisbon treaty (see table below). this solution should avoid a ‘traumatic reallocation of seats, with heavy losses for medium and small member states and huge increases for big ones’. it is also the ‘least imperfect of the possible solutions’, said lead meps rafał trzaskowski (epp, pl) and roberto gualtieri (s&d, it).

mr president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that our first duty as members of this parliament is to deplore the violence and the loss of human life and, secondly, to express our unwavering commitment to freedom of expression, freedom of assembly, freedom of conscience and respect for the rights of minorities. but given these premises, i believe that the european union must act responsibly, not by encouraging radicalisation or polarization, but by presenting solutions based on dialogue, mutual understanding and respect. i think we should not overlook the importance of these events in turkey and i think the debate on this occasion is not whether we have reacted well or badly and not whether we have reacted early or late. i think that commissioner füle and the high representative have reacted well and i think that the important thing is to take into account that we cannot afford a destabilisation of turkey. turkey is a positive and active partner of the european union, which has introduced many reforms; it is a loyal ally of the west in the atlantic alliance, where it took risks in the invasion of kuwait; it is a strategic country in the black sea oil passage; and it is a country which plays an important role in the 'arab spring' conflict and has taken in more than 400 000 syrian refugees. we cannot therefore allow ourselves, mrs ashton, to be incited by the european union to destabilise the situation in turkey. i simply want to say that this conflict must be handled with a sense of responsibility, with prudence and, of course, also, as many members have said, in accordance with the democratic principles and values which we defend in our political project.
mr president, i think we should always start by expressing solidarity with those who have been reprisals and condolences to the families of the victims in these situations where intolerable violence is taking place. but the best way to show respect for the people who have taken to the streets and squares of turkey in recent weeks is probably to try to interpret what their message is, what comes out of taksim in its pluralism, in its interclass, intergenerational character. however, it seems to me that it is relatively simple to interpret that this is not the "arab spring", or "occupy wall street", or the "madrid indignados", or the violence in the suburbs of britain or france of a few years ago. it is a specific message, a very specific turkish message, from people who say very simple things and, of course, things that are difficult to achieve: that they want justice in their country to be independent, that they want the press in their country to be plural and free, that they think that in their country minorities must be recognized and protected, that they think that in their country a bipolarisation must be avoided, a confrontation for reasons of nationalist or religious authoritarianisms, which are worth as much. that is, a message that aspires to a mature and solid democracy. and this message of warning is addressed to the powers that be, to the government, to erdogan; it is also addressed, as ria oomen-ruijten said, to the opposition, which must make itself credible; and it is addressed to europe, which must act with maturity so as not to react in a contradictory way to those who want us to help them achieve their objectives without interference.
mr president, turkey is a great country, a candidate for membership of the european union, a regional power, a member of nato, europe's main trading partner, and i agree with mrs ashton that it is not the time for us to distance ourselves from turkey, but the brutal repression of citizens who protest and the reprisals against the media are not compatible with the european union. how many years have we been negotiating with turkey without opening the chapters that would have solved the problems for which citizens are now protesting - freedom of expression, freedom of assembly, in short, civil rights? these human rights chapters are, by the way, the first to be opened in any enlargement negotiations and the last to be closed. it has been so in all the other enlargements and it is not so in the case of turkey. only 13 of the 35 chapters have been opened and only one, politically irrelevant, on science and research, has been closed. only three chapters on competition, social policy and public procurement are open, and none on democratic reform and human rights. there are 18 chapters blocked by the european union and i think, mrs ashton, that you should, instead of travelling to turkey, travel to european capitals to bring the member states into line with what the european union wants, which is to consolidate the european perspective of a truly democratic turkey.

the next item is the debate on the report by elmar brok and roberto gualtieri, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on the recommendation to the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and vice-president of the commission, the council and the commission on the 2013 review of the organisation and functioning of the eeas (2012/2253 (ini)) (a7-0147/2013).
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, this recommendation taking the opportunity to congratulate the rapporteurs, elmar brok and roberto gualtieri fits in with the purpose and aim of the 2010 council decision to contribute to improving, by its revision, this decision adopted by the council of ministers. i think that a very clear first finding is that the service is fully operational and is working and i think that the merit of the high representative and her collaborators, very particularly mr vimont, must be recognised. that said, i insist that we have to frame the logic of the european external action service's activity in a legal framework, which is the council decision, which established a staff and material resources and an ambition. so the service was meant to be what it is and we can't expect miracles. i would like to make a comparison, and that is that the personal and financial resources available to the european external action service for the whole of the european union are very similar to those of a member state like denmark. the office can clearly be improved by improving coordination between the european external action service, the member states and the community institutions; by strengthening the high representative's powers through political deputies and an advisory council; by using member states' ministers in tasks entrusted to them by the high representative. a good example was the egyptian task force; and by seeking synergies between the different administrations. there is a fundamental element, which is to draw on all the experience of the diplomats of the member states, recycling them in such a way that they reason in the interests of the eu and also motivating the officials of the institutions. and in this context, mr president, the key element is the mobilization of political will so that the european union can act and speak with one voice and we can have a foreign policy that is more effective, more coherent and more visible, and for this, the member states - in order to avoid undesirable situations such as that which has occurred in the debate on syria - must understand that they have to look for their advantage, mr president, in the common advantage.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. the european parliament has always been very much aware of the need to ensure that the european union's external action is not only coordinated, but also coordinated. in general, the foreign policy of any member country is, of course, subject to the control of the national parliaments: this is not the case. and we have a very serious problem because the foreign policy services of the member states and of the european union itself overlap. it is a structure in which the european parliament should play a much more important role. we are also very far from having a coherent and united foreign and security policy - this is a reality - and it is therefore very difficult to have a foreign service which is the support of a common foreign and security policy, a security policy which, insha'allah, is a foreign policy based on disarmament, demilitarisation, cooperation and the political settlement of conflicts.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, i should like to begin by thanking the group's alternate rapporteurs for their much-needed cooperation on this report, which is essentially divided into two parts: one on relations between the european union and the united states and the other with a view to the whole atlantic basin, including its southern dimension. president obama's second term should be used to strengthen the already very important relations between the european union and the united states, at a time when there is also much talk of washington's shift towards the pacific. the report calls for the forthcoming annual summit to be held as soon as possible. but in any case, the negotiations on the trade and investment agreement will be a major revitalization of the bilateral relationship. it is a historic opportunity, and one that is particularly timely, to promote growth and employment in a period of crisis. the overall impact of the programme goes beyond its bilateral significance. the report also calls for close coordination between the eu and the us on a number of global and regional issues of particular relevance: the arab spring, syria, afghanistan, the rise of china, russia, etc. it also supports the creation of a transatlantic political council as a forum for dialogue and coordination of the foreign policy of both actors and stresses the importance of the transatlantic dialogue of legislators. the report also refers to cooperation in justice and home affairs, visas, cybersecurity, the fight against terrorism, etc., while stressing the need to preserve fundamental rights and freedoms. i have had to update this bilateral part of the report by a series of short amendments which i have tabled in the last few days. the second part of the report contains a broader atlantic perspective. in an interdependent and globalised world, i believe that all the atlantic countries increasingly share common challenges and interests. there should therefore be greater cooperation between them to manage this increasingly common problem. i think the attention that the asia-pacific region is currently receiving has been a stimulus for think tanks, some governments and the european commission itself to be reflecting on the desirability of promoting this broader atlantic cooperation. and there's a new fact, too: china's growing penetration in latin america and africa. the report proposes that the european union and the united states - two key players - should study this prospect of overall atlantic cooperation, while exploring it with the other atlantic countries, i.e. first of all with latin america and the caribbean, a region with close ties to the union and the united states; we could also extend this cooperation to the african countries on the atlantic coast. in addition, given the extensive network of trade agreements that both the european union and the united states have or will soon have with several american countries, if the negotiation of the trade and investment agreement is successful, there would be a huge triangular economic space between the european union, the united states, canada and several countries in central and south america in the future. in addition, triangular cooperation would be of particular interest in other areas: climate change, development, security issues, global governance, un reform, energy, disarmament, piracy, drug trafficking and a long list of others. the latin american integration and cooperation organizations would be the instruments through which this triangular dialogue and cooperation could be carried out with these countries: celac, unasur, sica, caricom, the andean community, the pacific alliance and mercosur. in addition, account must be taken of the african countries on the atlantic coast; with them, through organizations such as ecowas or the african union, such comprehensive atlantic cooperation in several of the matters mentioned would be of interest. this part of my report offers ideas and possible lines of action for global atlantic cooperation. the atlantic brings together a very heterogeneous set of countries, with different agendas. today there may not yet be a sense of belonging to an atlantic community which brings together all the countries bordering the atlantic. i think that creating such awareness would be beneficial for the european union and the united states and i hope that this report can also contribute, modestly, to this objective.
member of the commission. − madam president, thank you for giving me the opportunity to take part in this debate. i want to thank mr millán mon for his report, which is excellent in itself, but it is also interesting that in a way it is a follow-up to the report of 2009, adopted at the beginning of the first obama administration. in a rapidly changing world, where political and economic power is shifting, both the european union and the us must adapt to a new global landscape that includes the forces of globalisation, new technologies, faster communication and also new challenges to peace and prosperity, such as a global challenge like climate change. more than ever, close cooperation is needed, especially with partners that share the same values, outlook and interests as ourselves. there is a simple fact. once undisputed centres of military and economic power, the us and europe cannot face these challenges alone. the european union is thus clearly looking beyond the north atlantic to work harder to engage with the rest of the american continent and the rest of the atlantic basin, which, as you rightly point out in your report, will be an important component of our efforts. in that regard, the european union has established, and is strengthening, its ties to address the very extensive and complex global agenda with strategic partners belonging to this basin like brazil and mexico, but also canada and south africa. as you rightly emphasised, at the heart of such broader transatlantic cooperation lies our strategic partnership with the united states, based on shared values and a highly convergent worldview. sometimes our approaches can differ, but this continues to be irreplaceable. cathy ashton is in regular contact with secretary of state kerry on the major foreign policy and security challenges, and we share the view that none of these challenges can be solved by any players acting alone. efforts to reinvigorate the middle east peace process and finding a diplomatic solution to the syrian crisis are obvious examples, but there is also iran, where the eu and the us are working together to seek a solution following a dual-track approach of negotiations and targeted sanctions. we are exploring new areas of cooperation as we are beginning to broaden out our strategic engagement vis-à-vis the asia-pacific region. the european union and the united states have a major stake in the prosperity of this region as a source of future growth, and therefore in the stability on which growth depends. there is much to do together in terms of promoting rule-based approaches in the region: freedom of navigation and the peaceful resolution of maritime disputes, for example. we are working more closely with the united states on improving our energy security by promoting diversification of sources of supply and transparent global markets, as well as trying to tackle the problem of energy as a source of conflict by coordinating our approach to energy-rich, but governance-poor, nations. through joint research and better policy coordination on new technologies and energy efficiency, we aim both to boost energy security and to contribute to fighting climate change by reducing greenhouse emissions. regarding counter-terrorism, we have begun to explore ways in which we can cooperate to face emerging challenges such as cyber-security. eu-us cooperation is already excellent and, therefore, it allows us to raise our concerns if and when needed and to stress the importance of the respect of the fundamental rights of individual citizens regarding data protection. we are also in the process of obtaining our respective mandates to negotiate a ground-breaking and ambitious transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the aim is to tap the potential of further liberalising the transatlantic market in goods and services in order to create jobs and growth, and to set high standards in terms of removing regulatory barriers. the ttip will have a much broader significance than just trade and investment. it represents a reaffirmation of confidence in the transatlantic partnership. it is rooted in our common values and interests and is part of the modernisation of the transatlantic relationship to meet the challenges of the 21st century. trade negotiations can be long and difficult. as commissioner de gucht underlined here during the last session, we need to see the broader picture and put all our energy and political will behind these negotiations. the support of the european parliament is definitely an asset. this brings me back to the issue of the ‘broader atlantic’. the continued economic growth of latin america and sub-saharan africa is welcome news. however, the challenges of a growing population and increased pressure on energy, food and water resources require solutions to be found. this opens up opportunities for cooperation, and the european union has very strong expertise in a lot of areas. furthermore, as underlined in the report, we are still facing some serious security challenges in the atlantic region. in the latin american and caribbean context, the levels of violence are alarming, in particular in central america and mexico, where organised crime groups sometimes challenge and rival state structures. in this context, security and the rule of law need to be ensured. the european union, together with the united states, has been active on this. for instance, since the may 2011 lisbon symposium on dismantling transnational illicit networks, the eu and the us have been working to strengthen cooperation on fighting trafficking along the so-called ‘cocaine route’ via capacity-building projects in west africa, latin america and the caribbean, and the promotion of south-south cooperation. in close coordination with the us and canada, we are working on giving more coherence to our security cooperation in central america and the caribbean. the eu’s comprehensive approach to security challenges and crisis situations draws systematically on all of the various diplomatic, economic, humanitarian, security and development instruments at our disposal. we are cooperating closely with the united states to address the underlying causes of the security challenges we face, as well as dealing with the symptoms. in west africa, for example, we are developing ‘joint programming’ together, where we try and deliver our aid more effectively. over the years, eu-us relations have become much more about how we project our values and interests together in the world, and rather less about just ourselves. increasingly, we are pushing the boundaries and tackling new frontiers in the transatlantic relationship. i look forward to continued cooperation with the european parliament on these issues.

on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, today we will vote on a proposal which was created to revise the 2003 directive on the re-use of public sector information. rules and practices around the re-use of public sector information differ between the new member states and some of them have still not modified their law. only a harmonised set of ambitious rules can enable the market to take full advantage of the commercial and non-commercial opportunities that the re-use of public data represents. opening up governmental data for re-use can have major benefits for citizens, businesses, society and for the governments themselves. let me state the main modifications in the report. with this new proposal, we extend the scope to museums, archives and libraries. we also limit the maximum charge that public sector bodies can apply to the marginal cost of disseminating the information. we try to foster the use of machine-readable and open formats where possible, to accelerate the transfer and use of information. the exclusive arrangement for the digitisation of documents held by cultural institutions will not in general exceed ten years, with a regular review in the following years, preventing open-ended contracts. last, but not least, the new ruling will introduce an impartial body whose decision will be binding on the public sector body concerned. this body should have the appropriate level of expertise and will review the decision on re-use. i would like to finish with some data. the eu public sector information market for digital content products and services was estimated to be worth eur 28 billion in 2008. opening up data to access has the potential to add eur 40 billion per year in revenue. the proposed revision aims to correct differences arising among member states, improve access and ensure effective cross-border use of public sector data, kick-starting the development of new services based on novel ways to combine and make use of such information to stimulate economic growth, which will help us a lot, especially nowadays. i would like to finish by thanking the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteur for the good job they did.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr kalfin, for his excellent work. we all know the added value of transferring and reusing public sector information to drive innovative value-added production. and not only that, but also, as has been said, there is a great economic potential behind the reuse of this information. i would remind you that the direct and indirect overall economic benefits of this activity are estimated at eur 140 billion across the european union. the 2003 directive on the re-use of public sector information introduced a common legal framework governing the provision of information by public bodies, as well as measures to remove obstacles to the dissemination of information. ten years later, the kalfin report amends this directive, improving transparency and efficiency in the transfer of public sector information. given the importance of public information, not only for promoting innovation but also for improving the economic sector, i think it is vital to approve this report.
madam president, the reuse of public sector data is part of an information society for all and adds value by generating more valuable recycled information: with this we can create maps, projects, networks. the report, which improves on the commission's report, is based on security, safekeeping, use and transparency, as well as on limiting business; it sets out objectives: the right to information, accessibility and internalization. access to public sector information is a fundamental right, something that has been taken away from the greek people by the closure of public television. and the same is true in the valencian community (spain), where mass layoffs of public employees are also curtailing democracy itself.
madam president, i would like to congratulate my colleagues on the committee, and in particular mr kaczmarek, on the excellent report we are voting on this afternoon. the message we are sending from this parliament today to the commission, the member states and the world is clear: we have not failed. it is true that we will not be able to meet many of the commitments in the year and a half that remains, but millions of people who have overcome the disease, millions of people who are entering schools or who are no longer hungry know that the commitment has borne fruit. but, as always, we can do more and better. the debates that are taking place today at international level about the future of cooperation, framed in the crisis, can affect the way we fight poverty, and cooperation: how we have designed it and what we want to do in it in the future. a future, that of development cooperation, which involves making the process more universal and more participatory, especially with the developed countries; maintaining the 0.7; for an agenda that includes eradicating inequality, hunger, imposing sustainability and ensuring access to clean water and health, including sexual and reproductive health, as well as education to which millions of people still do not have access. what we have ahead of us is a huge challenge and a huge responsibility, and again the european union must demonstrate its leadership in this process, including its responsibility to not only value middle-income countries for their growth, but also for other indicators such as vulnerability and inequality, remembering that 70 percent of the poor live in those countries.
madam president, commissioner, this year the united nations will review the millennium development goals and their results, and will begin to consider new cooperation for the period after 2015. when the millennium declaration was adopted in 2000, we could not have imagined that the landscape would change so much: at the moment it is very difficult for many countries to maintain their level of development cooperation due to the crisis they are going through. we must therefore propose new forms of development aid with clear, coherent and integrated objectives. eradicating poverty must be the highest priority. it is essential that the post-2015 agenda focuses on improving the quality of life of the most disadvantaged populations, with particular attention to access to safe drinking water, nutrition, health and education. private initiative also needs to be supported, as we need to help developing countries to move forward on their own. initiatives such as micro-credit are very useful in promoting local development, and so is support for smes, which are also the main engine of economic growth. finally, i would like to remind you that today, more than ever, it is essential to carry out a thorough monitoring of aid to ensure that the funds we allocate to cooperation are properly managed and thus maximise their impact. i would not like to end without congratulating mr kaczmarek on his excellent report.
madam president, can we continue to tolerate in the world that half the world's population lives in the indignity of poverty? can we continue to put up with children dying of hunger? can we continue to endure the failure of access to education, of equal rights to health, to water, to food? can we continue to endure deaths from aids without access to medicines? it is also in our european conscience to have a global agenda, the agenda of the millennium goals, challenges in peace, the environment, human rights, gender equality and democracy, leaving aside the hypocrisy we have translated into european trade agreements. this report is a call for indifference, because the millennium development goals are only achievable if the rich countries commit themselves to a better distribution of the world's wealth with social justice. because it is immoral that two-thirds of the developing countries spend more on paying off their foreign debt than on basic services. it is immoral for european countries to reduce their contributions to the millennium development goals under the pretext of the crisis, while investing in armaments and worrying about the health of the financial system.

in writing. - i voted against this report because it seeks to deepen the liberalization of trade relations with central africa. during centuries of colonization, africa has exported both its natural resources and its own population to the european powers, leaving a continent that has been expropriated of its economic development to boost europe's. this report seeks to promote trade with europe as a means of growth in the region, but it is nothing more than a new neo-colonial offensive which seeks to reinforce the dependence of the central african economies on the european common market. the export of natural resources and agricultural products does not necessarily imply real economic development and reinforces inequality in these economies. in view of the fact that this agreement can only strengthen the eu's imperialist role in this region of the african continent, i have decided to vote against it, as has my group in this parliament.
in writing. − against. greens share the very critical view on epas largely defended by acp countries and civil society organisations. briefly: the acp region needs very different agreements, which ensure sustainable development within a context of peace, stability, security, solidarity, respect for human rights and the development of the region as a whole, and do not unilaterally seek profits in exploitable areas such as mining or agrobusiness, including for agrofuels. in the particular case of cameroon, greens point at four particular drawbacks: first, inside cameroon, parts of the executive and the legislative branches are not convinced of the benefits of this interim epa. second, the central african region members heavily criticise cameroon for breaking solidarity. presumably, the iepa will further destabilise the region. third, a number of the central african region members are highly unstable themselves (the countries are: cameroon, central african republic, chad, congo, democratic republic of congo (drc), equatorial guinea, gabon, são tomé and principe). fourth, the iepa contains provisions which have already been eliminated from the full epa pattern, after heavy criticism, in particular the standstill clause, export restriction provisions, including quantitative ones, and safeguard provisions. this creates inconsistencies in the event of transition from the iepa to the epa.

president of the commission. − mr president, regarding the european council issues, the question that was directed to me was about what the european union has been doing regarding the implementation of the growth compact. before the european council i sent to all heads of state and government, and also to the european parliament through its president, a very clear and transparent report on the implementation of the growth compact, where i signalled, in very clear terms, what has been done, what has not been done and what is in the process of being completed. i invite all of you – those who have not yet seen that report – to look at it attentively because i think it is a very important exercise in transparency as regards the real implementation of the compact for growth and jobs. as i said in my introductory remarks, the ‘bilan’ is rather mixed. there are, it is fair to say, important points of progress, but there are still matters where we need to do more, namely in terms of implementation. most of the bottlenecks, if you look at this report, are mainly in terms of national implementation. this is the fair, objective assessment we can give to you. the commission, apart from many initiatives that it has taken – from the initial proposal to the increase of the eib lending capacity, to the project bonds, to the youth guarantee scheme and many other initiatives – has committed to redirect and redeploy the structural funds for growth. i would like now to report to you more concretely. i am pleased to confirm that the eur 55 billion representing the last tranche of the european union budget to complete current programmes – the 2013 tranche – has now been allocated to all programmes. in other words, the full budget of cohesion policy for the period 2007-2013 – eur 346 billion – has been made available to member states. the commission is now working with member states to ensure that these resources are mobilised rapidly and efficiently to support growth in investment and jobs. several member states – belgium, cyprus, estonia, greece, hungary, ireland, luxembourg, the netherlands and sweden – have reported on frontloading their programmes and have already allocated all the 2013 funds or will do so soon. other member states have indicated that selection processes are well underway – for instance germany, france, poland and the uk. i urge those member states who have not yet done so to accelerate selection processes for prompt implementation. concerning structural fund reprogramming to date, i would like to remind members of this house that, since 2009, more than eur 39 billion has been reprogrammed to support the most pressing needs and reinforce effective measures – with the european regional development fund (erdf) and cohesion fund accounting for eur 32.7 billion and the european social fund (esf) accounting for eur 6.5 billion. these measures have been accompanied by exceptional increases in the european union cofinancing rate for nine member states, reducing national financing by eur 19 billion by may 2013 and adding a further cofinancing top-up for the programme countries, namely paying eur 1.7 billion. these measures have reduced national cofinancing requirements by eur 20.7 billion. this takes pressure away from national budgets in the most vulnerable countries at a time of crisis. i could go on at length explaining some of the measures, namely the action teams for tackling youth unemployment and many other concrete measures. i invite you to look at this report on the compact for growth and jobs where you will see afterwards, in a very graphic way as well, all the measures that were announced by the european council and the council where we have shown the different levels of implementation in green, yellow and red. i believe that when we speak about transparency and accountability this should not be only words, but we should really put them into practice. i think this is clearly important. if i may now make a more general political remark, i hope that members of the european parliament, namely those coming from the pro-european families, resist the temptation that is unfortunately very common among some national politicians when there is a problem in the economy to put the blame on brussels or on the european union, instead of doing their own homework and instead of doing what they should do at home to reform their economies, to promote investment and in fact to make our economies more competitive. i think this point is very important bearing in mind the european parliament elections we are going to have next year. because if the main political forces, those with the great tradition of supporting the european project, start criticising the european union, if they think they will gain or make points with that, they are completely wrong. because in the business of attacking the european union there are others that are much better than the mainstream political forces and at the end they are going to be the ones who will benefit from these kinds of populist attacks. that is why i want to conclude, and since i cannot mention all the statements, by praising one statement that i particularly liked during today’s meeting. it was ms mcguinness’s remark. it was brief but she touched on a very important point. we have to deal with these matters with a great sense of responsibility. we should not ask the european level what the european level cannot deliver now. i can assure you that at european level, together with the european parliament, we are using to the full all the instruments we have to promote growth and stability in europe. however, we have to do it in a spirit of responsibility on a step-by-step approach; highlighting what has been achieved and also being honest about what has not yet been achieved. it is true that there are many matters where we need to do more and in a more determined and quicker manner. but i think this is the language of truth. this is the only way to reconnect europe to citizens; to talk with them responsibly; to tell them the truth and not to create illusions that we are not able to fulfil and to avoid the narrow vision of some nationalism or some chauvinism that can only do harm to our european union – a european union that, despite all the difficulties, is indeed showing its resilience and its very strong power of attraction. not only has croatia now joined the european union, but also the union is giving the green light for latvia to become the next member of the euro family. my dear friends of the european parliament, i remember that more or less one year ago people were speaking about the implosion of the euro and now i see new members for the euro, new members for the european union. in spite of all the difficulties i see this europe has a great future if we do it in a responsible constructive way.
the european council - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank all those who have spoken. i would like to thank in particular those who have spoken positively about the conclusions of the european council. it's so rare that i cherish these moments and hold them. some of you have spoken of the failure of the policy being pursued - the so-called austerity policy. well, the policy we have is much more than a policy of austerity. i explained it all at the beginning of my introduction. it is a policy, a strategy, in four parts: ensuring financial stability, promoting the restoration of sound public finances, restoring - as far as possible - competitiveness, working on economic and monetary union and taking direct measures to promote employment and, above all, the employment of young people. there has long been a consensus on this strategy in the european council, and it is governments of the centre-left, governments of the centre-right, coalitions other than those i have just mentioned, which have endorsed it in the continuity of recent years. so it's not a strategy imposed by a few institutions, by a few stubborn people. no, it is a strategy shared by governments, supported by their national parliaments. i want to say it again. as regards the policy of fiscal consolidation, it is a policy which is of course still being pursued. the management is still the management that was established a few years ago. it is being achieved through stability plans, but given the economic situation and the results achieved - that is, a reduction of 50% on average in budget deficits - we have been able to ease the pace and have given some countries time to meet budgetary objectives. in the case of six or seven countries, the direction has been maintained, but the pace has been changed to take account of the results achieved and the recession that is affecting them. but so, keeping the course is extremely important, also to maintain credibility. this policy is therefore much more consensual than is generally believed across europe - the europe of national governments, supported by national parliaments. but we know very well that this takes time and that we cannot wait for, say, the return of strong growth without working on employment, and especially on youth employment. that is why we need, in addition to a general policy - and i hope no one is in favour of a policy of increasing budget deficits - a direct policy, a specific policy. and i find that the countries with the lowest rates of youth unemployment in our european union are precisely those which have this specific policy, focused on training, on good education and on cooperation between the business world and schools at all levels. and it is these countries that are more successful, even in a period - also for them - of recession or near-stagnation. we must draw the full consequences of the policies pursued in certain countries. we must learn from what some countries have been able to achieve. and this is the exercise we are conducting, this is the work we will also continue in the next few days in berlin. so, as far as economic and monetary union is concerned, is the pace too slow? ladies and gentlemen, in june last year we voted in favour of a single supervision, a single supervision, of all banks. six months later we have the legislative framework, at least at council level. six months is not enough time for a reform which is, in fact, in this financial world, a reform that is almost revolutionary! i said that in this parliament a year ago. of course, this must now be done on the ground. we need to hire people. you need infrastructure, you need logistics. it takes time. we have worked at a very high rate, and we continue to work at a very high rate. a few days ago we agreed on the harmonization of crisis resolutions in the various countries, with a criterion on how to proceed. it will also be very useful when the commission presents its proposal for a single crisis resolution mechanism for the whole of the european union. this is also an extremely important step because the two central components of a banking union are supervision and resolution. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rules on the protection of the financial interests of the union are respected. the commission's proposal is awaited and work will be done in the second half of the year in the council and parliament to ensure that the whole procedure is completed before the european elections. but of course, it takes time, as i said, because we have to fight financial fragmentation within the euro area, and we cannot wait to have a full and complete banking union. here too, specific measures are needed, and that is why we have asked the european commission and the european investment bank to work, to share the risks, so that we can help small and mediumsized enterprises as much as possible to have access to credit. so, as with youth unemployment, specific policies must be put in place until structural reforms bear fruit, and i would like you to understand this approach, which is indeed a gradual approach, a step-by-step approach, but which requires keeping the course, keeping the direction. it has been said that there is no solidarity in the european union. in the european budget, which i hope will be approved, there is a lot of european solidarity. the financial rescue mechanism, the esm, is a solidarity mechanism. we also spoke at one point about development aid. we haven't cut development aid. we have mentioned syria. who is the biggest donor of humanitarian aid to syria? it is the european union and its member states, with a total of €1 billion. we beat every other player in the world by a long shot. the european union remains, in general terms, the largest donor of development aid in the world, with over 50% of the total. i'm not a masochist. i'm not exactly euphoric either. but you have to tell it like it is. and so i'm not asking for understanding, but i insist that we always see the truth in all these aspects. on the recent incidents and revelations, which several of you have mentioned, we must first have a complete clarification, have all the information before we launch accusations. if, of course, these accusations prove to be true, then the time will have come for me to act and i will use, at that time, different words than i am using today. but the us authorities have been asked for further clarification on these suspicions and accusations. the european council has taken concrete action on various fronts in accordance with the philosophy i have outlined, a philosophy based on a four-point strategy, without expecting that strategy to produce all the desired results in the areas of youth unemployment and access to credit. that is why, in the meantime, direct, specific measures are being taken to tackle the problems wherever possible, while being aware that, for example, when we talk about employment, most of the competences are national competences. it is too easy to blame europe for problems that have not been solved at national level. we must put an end to the saying that 'if it rains, it is europe's fault'. no, we must see where the responsibilities lie, particularly when we talk about employment policy.

in writing. − against. our group has decided to vote against the staff regulations on the grounds of the failure to burden officials in higher grades progressively and fairly. this is evident not just in the allocation of the sacrifices demanded but also in the privileges and allowances that this reform does not touch.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it approves the council decision to allow the parties to approve the protocol to the 1997 vienna convention. this convention provides for the compensation and liability to which the citizens of a signatory state are entitled for damage caused by a nuclear accident. there is a certain lack of homogeneity between eu member states where there are parties that have not yet signed the said protocol, this could lead to multiple legal problems, especially in the case of accidents or events with a cross-border dimension within the eu. the report is only intended to approve the proposals and procedures necessary to bring about greater uniformity in the member states' rules on the treatment of victims of damage caused by nuclear technology. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because it is based on improving market principles. this report seeks to improve and standardise the criteria for competition complaints, given the high number of complaints, some 300, lodged in this area each year. the report also includes the possibility for the commission to collect information on its own account from market operators, freeing member states from liability and the possibility of being sanctioned for failing to provide the information requested by the commission. the aim of this report is to speed up and improve the efficiency of the commission's work in the field of competition, to improve its functioning and to relieve the member states of an unnecessary workload. but i did not vote in favour because it only seeks to improve competition in the single market and to dismantle member states' state aids.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a good assessment of the first year of application of regulation (eu) no 1233/2011 of the european parliament and of the council on export credit agencies. under this regulation, agencies are to increase their transparency and accountability to the ec, including on their compliance with environmental law, human rights, sustainable lending and eu anti-corruption rules. almost all member states have their own export credit agency, which provides government-backed credits, guarantees or insurance to private domestic companies doing business abroad. some of these agencies are wholly public, others are privately or jointly owned, but always sponsored by governments. after one year of application of the abovementioned regulation, it was to be expected that member states would have increased the transparency of these agencies, but this has not been the case. this criticism is reflected in the report and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it provides a good regulatory framework for public-benefit foundations in the context of the european union. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity and is therefore in line with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. the commission proposal is not problematic and goes into the technical terms of the functioning of this type of social organization even with some reference to the need to protect the labour rights of the workers of this type of foundation. the report improves some of the definitions in the proposal by providing a homogeneous framework which will provide legal certainty for the sector in which social foundations operate. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this proposal for the harmonisation of foundation regulations is a very good thing for the citizens of the european union. the new regulation will be clearer and basically similar in all member states. this will increase the scale of fundraising within the european union while reducing the operating costs of these same foundations. we must recognise the essential role of foundations in the european union and we must also give our full support to the efforts to develop them. the result of my vote is positive, as is this new regulation on european foundations.
in writing. − in favour. the aim is to facilitate the cross-border activities of public benefit foundations by laying down the conditions for the establishment and operation of a european foundation. foundations cannot channel funds efficiently on a cross-border basis in the eu. when they decide to operate across borders, foundations have to spend part of the resources they collect on legal advice and fulfilling legal and administrative requirements laid down by the different national laws. the present initiative creates a new european legal form intended to facilitate the establishment and operation of foundations in the single market. it will allow foundations to channel private funds more efficiently for public-benefit purposes on a cross-border basis in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a significant legislative step forward in ensuring accountability in ship inspections and in defending the rights of seafarers. this report comes at a time when the rights of seafarers are increasingly being violated and flag states are trying to shake off their responsibilities. these workers, who are in a situation of complete helplessness, in a place other than their place of origin and abandoned by the administrations, suffer terrible conditions. the report includes the proposal that member states should be responsible for carrying out checks to verify that each ship complies with the regulations on the conditions of seafarers. in this way, legal certainty for the rights of seafarers is sought, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a simplification of the administrative requirements for the technical inspection of vehicles which all european vehicles must meet. the report is technical in nature and aims to ensure that member states recognise the technical documents and accreditations of other member states immediately, providing legal certainty and convenience when crossing borders between different member states of the union. the report includes specific measures for member states such as the exchange of information in their respective national electronic databases or the possibility of removing cars from national registration registers to avoid liability. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves improvements in the control and inspection systems for commercial vehicles within the european union. the report requires each member state to inspect 5% of heavy commercial vehicles registered in its registries to ensure that they comply with safety regulations and do not endanger european citizens. the report improves the commission's proposal to include tractors not used for agricultural purposes, as well as other significant progress towards the member states implementing safety control systems for commercial vehicles that are homogeneous across the union. the improvement in the security conditions which this represents has led me to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. whatever the technical measures in place, we all know that the effectiveness of road safety policy depends ultimately on the users’ behaviour. for this reason, education, training and enforcement continue to be essential. however, the road safety system also has to take into account human error and inappropriate behaviour and correct it as much as possible. all components, in particular vehicles and infrastructure, should therefore be ‘forgiving’, so as to prevent and limit the consequences of these failures for the users, in particular the most vulnerable users.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it involves improvements in the control and inspection systems for motor vehicles and trailers within the european union, it does not do so effectively enough. the report deals with the control obligations on motor vehicles and their trailers, but during its discussion the commission proposal has lost many of the most important controls to ensure that safety rules are complied with, leaving and giving priority to those which do not represent a determining factor of safety, thus putting european citizens at risk, and this has been the view of the majority of groups. the report makes the commission's proposal worse by increasing the workload on issues that do not show flaws while forgetting about fundamental controls. i have therefore decided not to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because of the clear influence of the interests of certain industries on the exclusion of certain substances. the water framework directive establishes a list of substances that can pose a significant risk to water quality and use. this report presents the commission's review of the list of substances which affect water quality. while the commission's initial proposal increased the list to 15 substances, following the trilogue negotiations the number of substances was reduced to 10 with the possibility of gradually increasing the list by one substance at each review. there is growing scientific evidence on the dangers of industrial chemicals, but the eu seems to ignore it. in addition, three pharmaceutical substances are among the substances removed from the list, demonstrating the political influence of this sector. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because it is based on improving market principles. the report seeks to improve and facilitate the capacity of public authorities to grant public aid. activities that may be eligible for public support are included, such as cultural activities, those related to natural disasters, innovation, conservation of marine resources, among others. however, the report maintains an absolutely neoliberal approach, considering public aid as something temporary, which must be eliminated because it distorts competition. i did not vote in favour of this report because it seeks only to improve competition in the single market and to dismantle the member states' state aids.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a new attack on marine resources under the pretext of generating 'sustainable growth'. this report focuses on the 'blue growth' of the maritime dimension of strategy 2020, by subordinating the natural resources of the seas to the objectives of competitiveness in the international market. the report proposes a series of measures to promote and facilitate economic activity in marine areas. the aim is to promote the profit of the large monopolies linked to the marine industry which will compete with the rest of the small players in the economy by making them disappear by the very nature of economic competition. the aim is to improve their performance through tax exemptions, measures to encourage the mobility of workers, all sorts of improvements to competitiveness, and by eliminating the livelihood of the communities in the maritime zones. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour. mankind is turning towards the sea and oceans in the hope that they will be able to provide answers to the growing critical challenges we are now facing. new technologies, such as robotics and advanced underwater equipment, now allow eu researchers and enterprises to turn to the sea to help combat climate change, to develop treatments for serious diseases, to secure rare minerals, etc. building on its long and powerful maritime tradition, europe is now developing new activities such as offshore wind power and aquaculture. but if the eu is turning towards the sea, it is also because it is driven to do so by broader concerns. the need to reduce carbon emissions has rekindled interest in short-sea shipping and is opening the way for renewable forms of offshore energy. the overexploitation of land resources is raising prices on global markets and reinforcing the economic incentive to explore the mineral resources of the seabed.
we have supported this report because we can attest to the contribution of the social economy to the crisis in the basque country. there, our largest industrial group, powerful, diversified, innovative and with its own financial institution is called mondragon cooperative corporation. it has demonstrated the capacity to take initiatives, to locate jobs in the area and to maintain flexibility to suit the needs of the people. we are talking about a group that provides a country of two million inhabitants with almost as many jobs as all the shipbuilding in spain and values and ways of doing that, by their presence in the basque economic reality, influence above all our economic fabric. commissioner andor was able to see on the ground, and he said so in the employment committee, how this type of entrepreneurship, the existence of an active and sound regional industrial policy, and a responsible administration of public funds are one of the factors that explain why the basque country has less than half the unemployment rate of spain. the social economy is definitely a first-rate tool against the crisis.
in writing. i have voted in favour of this resolution because it recognises the ability of workers to carry on production without the need for an owner of the means of production, although this is a resolution which is likely to have little practical effect because it does not oblige the states. it recognises that european cooperatives are a key factor in overcoming the economic crisis; in the face of the bankruptcy of capital, it is labour that must take the reins of production. the resolution provides for a number of financing and support measures to boost this sector, which is a key pillar for job creation in the european economy. it also envisages a mechanism for the transfer of companies which are unable to meet their obligations to their workers by the creation of cooperatives. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. cooperatives, along with other social economy enterprises, play an essential role in the european economy, especially in time of crisis, by combining profitability with solidarity, creating high-quality jobs, strengthening social, economic and regional cohesion and generating social capital. the report recognises, furthermore, that social economy enterprises should benefit from a clearer and more coherent legislative framework, taking due account of the wealth of diversity among social economy institutions and the specific features thereof.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because the bioeconomy involves risks that need to be assessed more rigorously. it is an own-initiative report on the commission communication setting out the strategy for sustainable growth and the development of the bioeconomy. the bioeconomy is the economy that is based on the exploitation of biological resources with application in sectors such as agriculture, health, chemistry, or the energy industry. the report, in line with the commission communication, is too complacent about the advantages of the bioeconomy, as it believes that it will help to solve the social, economic and demographic problems facing europe today, such as the lack of raw materials or the need to ensure food security. i have therefore not voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. over the next 40 years europe will have to address a number of social challenges. the constant increase in the world population, the rocketing growth of demand for food and energy and the scarcity of natural resources worldwide mean that europe will have to reflect on the new approach to take in terms of production and consumption, in order to deal with these new requirements efficiently and sustainably. the bioeconomy is a major opportunity to meet those challenges by ensuring not only greater sustainability but also support for rural development, a potential reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, improved sustainability of the production cycle and the spread of industrial innovation along the entire value chain. the bioeconomy strategy could be the solution to our dependence on fossil fuels and the road towards smart growth. if it is forward-looking, it could also provide the answer to food security, economic growth and the creation of new jobs.

member of the commission. − madam president, i wish to thank members very much for an excellent set of comments. let me try to sum up in four points. firstly, the solidarity fund – how it works, how it should work and its size. secondly, other sources of support for affected populations and for action to increase preventive measures. thirdly, very important, how we think of flood management in the context of environmental sustainability, and how crucial this is. last but not least, the issue of highest vulnerability and the social impact on the most vulnerable populations. let me start with the solidarity fund. this is often thought to be an emergency response instrument, but unfortunately it is not. it was not designed to be one. nobody feels the deficiency of that more than me, because as the commissioner for humanitarian aid i can provide overnight assistance to moldova, but i cannot do it for romania, because in moldova we would use humanitarian aid, whereas in romania we would apply the solidarity fund. currently, the way the solidarity fund is designed, it requires up to ten weeks for a country to make an application, and then it takes another six to ten weeks to assess the application and the damage identified. our experience shows that it takes between four and eight months, or six months on average, between the moment a disaster strikes and the solidarity fund is potentially triggered, and the moment help gets to people. when help gets to the affected countries, it is substantial. let us just remind ourselves that after the floods in 2002 the solidarity fund granted eur 134 million to austria, where the damage was 2.9 billion; eur 129 million to the czech republic, where there was damage of eur 2.3 billion, and eur eur 444 million to germany, with damage of over 9 billion. one may say that the damage is much bigger than the amounts granted from the fund, but these are significant funds made available to countries and communities at a very difficult moment. as regards size, today it is up to eur 1 billion a year. in the new mff that is likely to be voted through tomorrow, unfortunately this goes from that eur 1 billion down to eur 500 million a year. it is a tough time, and obviously we have to be careful with claims on our member states’ money, but hopefully in the vote which takes place tomorrow there will also be a clause on revisiting the parameters for the fund mid-term. i am confident that this issue will be looked into again. then comes the question of whether procedures should be changed so that there can be accelerated assistance to countries. the commission currently is putting forward a proposal which would do two things: firstly, it would create immediate early-response drawing rights when it is obvious that the solidarity fund is going to be triggered, as it is right now. secondly, there would be some changes and streamlining of provisions so that we can indeed cut down on this processing time. i certainly hope that we will get support in the council and here in this chamber for this proposal. but the solidarity fund is not the only source of funds from the european union, and i want to stress that the structural funds, the cohesion fund and funds from the common agricultural policy and the social fund can be – and have been – used to help countries to be better prepared for disasters, and also to alleviate the impact on the most affected communities. currently we have over eur 5 billion in funding for flood management that our member states are using to improve their capacity to cope with rapidly increasing risks. we are also looking into other ways to help europe be more prepared for disasters to come. we are working with commissioner barnier on how the insurance industry can play a bigger role as a signalling tool to businesses, individuals and households in terms of where they should or should not live and build and develop, and how best to do that. thirdly, ecological conditions. i could not agree more with those speakers who stressed the importance of thinking of climate change not as some hypothetical threat in the future, but as a reality today, and the importance of our wetlands not as space that could be used for urban development and intensive agriculture, but as a means of protection of lives and property. this makes it so very clear that we must work hand in hand with commissioner potočnik on making sure that we introduce concepts of river basin management – points were made in that regard – and ecological sustainability as a factor, especially in flood disaster risks but also other disaster risks. last but not least, in every disaster i have been to, it is usually the poorest and most vulnerable people, whether in europe or elsewhere in the world, that are most devastated. that puts a premium on us to think hard about how to make sure, as we have a system to support victims of disasters, that we target the most vulnerable people with assistance first. that is something on which we have good experience in some member states, and we want to spread that and make it more broadly used. finally, on the point that i believe mr cofferati made about our needing a mindset change, i could not agree with this more. we are living in a world of more frequent and more devastating disasters. for us in europe, floods are the costliest thing. over 50% of damage in europe is due to floods. by the way, the biggest killer is not floods, it is summer heat waves. these kill elderly people and children. in this world of higher risks, we can only cope if we change our mindset to a risk management mindset. this is what we are striving to achieve, also with the new civil protection legislation that mandates risk assessments for our member states. i can say that there is not a day in which i, as the commissioner responsible, do not think hard on what we can do more of so that the lessons of the past are learnt and integrated, more lives are saved and there is less damage. one euro invested in prevention means seven euros of damage saved. of course, that does not even capture the pain and suffering of the people that are affected.

the next item is the debate on the report by mr sven giegold , on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs , on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2009/65/ec on the coordination of laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) as regards depositary functions, remuneration policies and penalties (com ((2012) 0350 c7-0178/2012 2012/0168 cod)) (a7-0125/2013).
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you, mr sven giegold, as rapporteur, for doing this important work. these are important parts of the regulatory arsenal or architecture that we are building together, with the council, but first with you, on the basis of the proposals that i have put forward for the last three years, to draw all the lessons, as sven giegold said, from the crisis and, in particular, to ensure that we respond to this crisis of consumer confidence. one of our priorities is to ensure that retail markets are better regulated and that they put the interests of their customers at the heart of their business. it is precisely the neglect of this principle, in all the previous years, that has been one of the structural causes of the financial crisis. this is of course essential for funds for retail investors in europe, ucits. as sven giegold said, the madoff affair - which we must not forget, because we must not have a short memory - has also had repercussions on our continent. and it is the inadequacy of regulation, and sometimes the damage of self-regulation or deregulation, that this madoff case has shown in terms of investor protection. the rules on the liability of the depositary are insufficient. this fraud has caused many european investors to lose very large sums of money. furthermore, the current remuneration policies of ucits managers do not sufficiently take into account the interests of investors, because they encourage, as the sven giegold report demonstrates, excessive risk-taking. that is all we want with this proposal: to put an end to all this, to put the interests of investors at the heart of the concerns of managers, to ensure that the rules are properly applied and to that end we are proposing a common approach to the sanctions associated with the main infringements of the ucits framework. i would like to thank the european parliament, the rapporteur sven giegold, and also the fictitious rapporteurs for their commitment and the very consensual work they have managed to build around the text which has been submitted to you. i would like to recall three main lines of this work: the task and responsibility of the depositary of the ucits, which need to be clarified, and a responsibility which needs to be better stated. consumers do not have to bear the consequences of a loss of assets, as may have been the case with the madoff case. that is why ucits proposal v requires the return of the lost assets. i would also like to emphasize the ambition and pragmatism of the sven giegold report. three basic principles should be stressed. first, the depositary must be liable for the assets it holds, without the possibility of contractually discharging that liability. second, assets held must always be protected, even in the event of the depositary's insolvency. thirdly, consumers should not be deprived of their right to complain directly to the depositary, without having to go through the manager. here's the first axis. the second aspect raised by your rapporteur is the remuneration policies of ucits management companies. the remuneration of managers must take the long-term interest of the consumer into account. that is why we have proposed strict rules on the structure of fees and the limitation of the variable part of the manager's remuneration. i share the parliament's aim, which is to ensure a high level of consumer protection through its proposals. that is why i am prepared, as i have done in the context of crd iv, to work with parliament and the council to reach a compromise, while expressing the hope that the debate on pay, which i know is important, will not prevent this important matter from being finalised during your term of office. and so i am prepared, mr giegold, to work with you and the council to find the most dynamic and clear compromise possible on this issue. third, the sanctions. i have ensured that the rules introduced on penalties are consistent with other similar texts, such as crd iv. it is obvious that certain provisions need to be adapted to take account of the specificities of the asset management sector. the proposed rules on ucits depositary liability and remuneration policies already exist in the aifm directive. this directive regulates alternative fund managers funds primarily distributed to professional investors. with the entry into force of the aifm directive this month, professional investors in europe will be better protected than investors in ucits, which are mainly retail investors. that is why this situation, this lag, cannot be sustained. i am convinced, mr giegold, that we will be able to finalize as soon as possible this future legislation to adapt and secure this product which was created in 1984 and which is objectively, throughout the world, a success story of the european financial industry.
