i am not saying that the european parliament should be a political body, but i am saying that it should be a political body, and i am not saying that it should be a political body, but that it should be a political body. we have done so, i would say, quite a few times, but always at inappropriate times: when we voted on budgets or when we voted on other matters, some kind of amendment was introduced which ended up voting on this question. this is the first time that it's been approached with a somewhat novel approach. we have expressed on several occasions in parliament a majority position in favour of the single seat and, above all, a position in favour of parliament itself being able to decide on its own seat. in fact, the last time we voted, not in the plenary but in the committee on constitutional affairs, the majority in favour of this matter was clear: 22 votes in favour and 4 votes against. this report by mr fox and mr häfner is intended to enable the european parliament to decide on its own seat and it obviously recognises that this enabling of parliament can only be done through a reform of the treaties. the report therefore proposes a single seat and that parliament should decide on it, and it recognises that the treaties must be amended, for which purpose it proposes an initiative by parliament aimed at amending the treaties. we have tried on occasion to organise our work in an autonomous way, for example last time, by grouping two partsessions into one week, and yet the court of justice of the european union ruled that we could not do so because we did not have the competence which parliament is now asking for in this report. i do not need to go into the reasons behind this proposal: there are economic reasons, environmental reasons and reasons for saving the effort of members of parliament and the people who work in parliament. i would also like to point out something which has been repeatedly stated: the report does not say what the single seat of parliament should be; in fact, the essence of the matter is that it is parliament which can and should decide on that seat. despite the title of this report, it does not take a position on any other issue than the seat of parliament, although it acknowledges that if a decision were to be taken on this issue, this would also affect the balance between the various institutions of the union. in short, we are in favour of a single seat, in favour of parliament being able to decide which seat to choose - without specifying in this report whether it is brussels, strasbourg or a third seat - and in favour of a rebalancing of the seat of the union's institutions.

multilateral trading system. for the first time in many years we are close to reaching agreement on certain elements of the doha development agenda. if members of the wto manage to achieve consensus, a central element of the outcome of the ministerial conference will be a trade facilitation agreement. such an agreement would provide tremendous benefits to traders around the world by improving customs procedures, increasing transparency, reducing red tape and allowing goods to move faster across borders. all members of the wto will benefit from this agreement. the biggest beneficiaries will be the developing countries and, particularly, smaller developing countries and the least developed countries. the agreement will help them to improve the functioning of their customs administrations, encourage the rapid development of regional trade and foster their integration into global value chains. the european union will provide assistance to those countries to help them with the process of implementing the agreement. an agreement on trade facilitation will go hand in hand with outcomes on a limited number of agricultural issues and on development issues, including those of particular interest to the least developed countries. agreement has already been reached on guidelines regarding preferential rules of origin applicable to imports from least developed countries, and on the implementation of the service waiver which sets out a number of ways in which we could help service providers from least developed countries and thereby contribute to the development of their service markets. although limited in nature, such a package should not be considered small. apart from the economic benefits it would provide, it would also have a tremendous systemic impact as it would constitute the first step towards the conclusion of the doha development agenda and would do justice to the development objectives of the doha round. if this conference is successful, it will open the door for further negotiations on the core issues of the doha round, including agriculture and market access for industrial goods, which need to be addressed at multilateral level. it will also help to move on to addressing further issues which, although not included in the doha mandate, are of tremendous importance to trading companies. a central element of the outcome will be a work programme in extension of the information technology agreement, negotiations on which resumed recently and are moving forward towards a substantive outcome. finally, considering the importance of the ministerial conference, the commission welcomes the fact that members of the european parliament will attend this event as part of the eu delegation, and the commission looks forward to further exchanges on the conference with members.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, it is a great pleasure to present to this house the commission’s work programme for 2014. this work programme is the culmination of an intense political dialogue between our two institutions, drawing on the state of the union debate, the meetings with the conference of committee chairs and the conference of presidents in october, this parliament’s resolutions and discussions at committee level in the form of structured dialogues. the political dialogue helps to generate a real consensus around key political priorities. this will mean that, as we enter a year of institutional transition and elections, citizens will see that there is a real sense of direction in the european union, a sense of purpose centred on the goals of completing the banking union and delivering on growth and jobs. the work programme underlines the commission’s determination to keep up the pace of work to deliver the reforms we have all agreed to over the past five years. in addition to a limited number of new initiatives, the commission has put the focus firmly on concluding legislative work on key proposals that are already on the table. we count on parliament’s strong support for this, and we also call on the member states to implement what has been agreed without delay. nowhere is that more important than on the multiannual financial framework. parliament has played a key role in reaching agreement on the eu budget, which is a catalyst for reforms, investments and support to communities across europe, and i warmly welcome the positive vote on this chapter of the mff yesterday. we now need to get the mff programmes off the ground as soon as possible to produce concrete results for citizens and businesses hit by the crisis. honourable members, we have worked hard under difficult circumstances to support the economic recovery and to restore the confidence of citizens and markets. we see positive signs today but we cannot afford any complacency. we can and must go further together. the commission launched the 2014 european semester last week. this is now a well-established exercise with a reinforced social dimension. but this year is, of course, the first time that the commission has delivered its assessment of the draft national budget which it published last friday, and work continues on the deepening of emu while ensuring full democratic control. that option of the single supervisory mechanism is transforming the banking landscape and this needs to be accompanied by an agreement on a single resolution mechanism as well as the bank recovery and resolution and deposit guarantee directives by the end of this parliamentary term. we also need to focus on how the eu can help those for whom recovery still seems a distant prospect rather than a reality. support for the young and unemployed is a particular priority. we must keep the pressure on member states to implement the youth guarantee and to use european funding intelligently and efficiently to help young people. six member states have already shared their draft youth guarantee implementation plans with us and we are working with the remaining member states to ensure that the plans are in place by the end of the year so as to ensure that the eur 6 billion of the youth initiative can be spent accordingly. further work on labour mobility and networking between public employment services is also underway. access to finance is another top priority. we have agreed changes to the cohesion rules that will pave the way for the new sme financial instruments. the commission will also follow up on the green paper on the financing of the economy with a new initiative in 2014. with economic recovery still fragile, we need to exploit the full potential of the single market and our trade agenda and force competitiveness across all sectors. europe’s economy needs a modern industrial base and streamlined regulation. this parliament has given much attention to the proposals in the two single market acts. adopting legislation in areas like electronic signatures, payments and switching bank accounts will not only have a direct economic knock-on for the digital single market; it will also be felt directly by citizens. energy is a major preoccupation for many european citizens. that is why we need to keep up the work to deliver a real single market for energy. we also need to look to the long term with a long lead time for investment in energy generation. this is reason why the commission will move ahead to start putting in place a clear framework for climate and energy policies beyond 2020. honourable members, we are a community of values and at a time when our attention is directed at the economy we must not lose sight of this. our freedoms sustain our prosperity. to grow and create jobs we must continue to safeguard and expand the freedoms of our citizens. the eu must also protect its citizens by adapting to new threats and challenges. concrete action in the coming months to finalise the data protection framework will have to ensure that citizens and companies can exercise their freedoms and rights in security. the commission will also be taking forward the reflection on the rule of law as well as feeding into the debate on the future of europe. and let us not forget our common objective to conclude discussions on the statute and funding of european political parties in good time before the next elections. in 2014 the commission will continue to defend european values and interests around the world and to show that it is a positive force worldwide through effective development and humanitarian aid directed to those most in need and through an active enlargement and neighbourhood policy that will continue to make the eu an anchor of peaceful development in our region and beyond. mr president, honourable members, this is the time to direct our energies towards making the most of the rest of this legislature, bringing all key proposals to conclusion and ensuring the smooth and timely start of mmf programmes. from the beginning, this commission has worked very closely with this parliament, its shared objectives and its common sense of the european good. let us maintain this spirit over the final months of the legislature and ensure that we do the maximum to show citizens what our union can achieve: a europe that is stronger, more united and open to the world. thank you very much for your attention and am looking forward to our discussions.
i would like to thank the rapporteur for his excellent report. we must be effective in showing the european citizens in the coming months that we are able to respond to their concerns and needs. my group does not want the commission to suffer from the 'symptom of the lame duck' - we want it to use the remaining year to fulfil its task and we would like it to think more about its legacy than about the difficulties of the present, and we would like that legacy to be a turn, a political turn towards some priorities. firstly, a shift towards growth, job creation, quality of employment and protection of the rights of all workers, especially those posted within the union who, at the moment, see their rights at risk in different countries. secondly, a shift towards the fight against youth unemployment: at present, fifteen countries in the union have a youth unemployment rate of between 20% and 30%; six of these countries have a rate of over 30%; four have a rate of over 40%; two have a rate of over 50%. only six countries have adopted their youth employment guarantee schemes; i ask the commission to keep pushing them. thirdly, a shift towards the fight against inequality and towards territorial and social cohesion. the decision to apply conditions and requirements of macro-conditionality, with possible sanctions on the countries which need the funds the most, is a wrong decision, it goes in the opposite direction to what we need. the decision to reduce the european social fund at a time of maximum crisis is also going in the wrong direction and in the opposite direction. only if we reach 25% of the total funds will we be able to maintain the current social policy of the european social fund and not to reduce it in the coming years when we are faced with an unprecedented social crisis within the union.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would also like to thank all those honourable members who appreciated the brevity and the structure of the commission work programme for 2014. i can assure you that it was not an easy task to set the correct priorities because, out of several hundred legislative proposals on the table of the legislator, we had to select very clear top priorities, and there are 26 of them. i think members can see that we have tried our best to focus our work for the remaining months of this legislature on really delivering on the proposals which can bring the highest eu value added or which contribute the most to economic growth and job creation in europe. as you will see from our annexes, we have included for the first time a very clear section on the refit programme. this is how we are approaching the reduction of administrative burden priorities. you will also see the proposal for the directives or regulations which we are suggesting that we can get rid of in the next period. i believe that this is the model which the commission will also follow in the future. mr duff referred to the need for better programming for the future. i have to say that his remarks very much echo the thrust of the discussion i had yesterday with the foreign and european ministers in the general affairs council, who also realised that if we want to better tackle our implementation gap and to be more efficient, we need to work on our programming and planning and to align the work of the working groups in the council, as well as the committee sessions in parliament. so we are moving with our priorities at more or less at the same speed. i also appreciated the call made by several ministers for the three institutions to sit down together, after the next european elections, to look at the current framework agreement which we have signed between parliament and the commission, and of course to start work on the agreement which would involve the council because this would allow us to plan our work much better and provide much better efficiency in the future. i can, of course, assure you that it will be very important for the commission that the communitarian method is followed and that the right of initiative of the commission is respected in any future arrangement. mr szájer highlighted the importance of industrial policy. i would like to reassure him that in january the commission will come forward with an appropriate communication as well as our in-depth analysis on the main drivers of energy prices, because we see energy prices as being a very important factor in the competitivity of the european economy. therefore we would like to bring forward both of these communications at the same time so we can adopt appropriate measures. mr guerrero salom very rightly pointed out that unemployment is the key problem in the european union. we know that to tackle it appropriately we need bigger and more robust growth. we also have to reflect the fact that the creation of jobs usually lags six months to one year behind economic growth. therefore, it must be our top priority, and i would like to assure you that we are doing our utmost to motivate the member states to work on the youth guarantee schemes because we really want all those member states where youth unemployment especially is very high, to be ready and to use the potential of the eu funding as of 1 january next year. the commission will be ready and we hope the member states will be ready as well. i can say the same to mr paksas about labour taxation. we are pushing very hard and he will find it in most of our country-specific recommendations where we advise the member states to move away from overly-high taxation on labour to more growth-friendly taxation because very often these taxes prevent labour mobility and they prevent job creation. therefore, there must be concerted action on support for creation of new jobs, but taxation policy must also be adjusted when it comes to labour. thank you very much for highlighting the importance of the administrative burden, and the importance of legislating only in those cases where we can clearly demonstrate eu value added. as i said yesterday to the ministers, and as we have discussed many times here in this house, this must be a common effort. we will make the proposals – we have already made quite a few on how to reduce the administrative burden and of course these proposals must be approved by the co-legislator – but most importantly they must be transposed correctly at national level. the member states must avoid the gold-plating which very often complicates the application of eu law and increases the administrative burden. we will do this with a lot of energy. we will do it on a regular basis. we will have annual reports and we will also have, this time, scoreboards which will focus on the efforts of the member states – on how they are doing and on what kinds of efforts they are deploying to reduce the administrative burden at national level as well. we hope that healthy competition will come out of this and that we will be able to report good progress at eu and national level, hopefully in one year’s time. mr borghezio referred to the tragedy in lampedusa. i would like to inform him that the task force for the mediterranean is working very hard. they will report on their findings and their proposals for further action at the beginning of december already and i believe that this will be debated here of course, in parliament, but also in various council configurations. a last word on ttip and the negotiations between the european union and the united states. we know how important these negotiations are. we know what the potential price is of adding an additional eur 119 billion to the eu’s gdp on a yearly basis. we know how important this would be for setting new standards for new products and for new technologies, and i know how important it is to defend european priorities and to negotiate in a very ambitious spirit. this is exactly what we are doing, because our top priority is to get the best possible deal for eu citizens and eu businesses.
i do not want to close the debate without emphasizing how comfortable and pleasant it has always been to work with you. we will certainly miss you. the vice-president has referred to the forthcoming elections and it is common knowledge that whenever elections of this kind take place, there is usually a minister who holds a seat in parliament and a minister who holds a seat in the commission. i hope that the arrival of these ministers in parliament and the commission will enable them to learn a great deal, to understand and to develop - with the same enthusiasm as they have shown in defending the intergovernmental method - the community method, which is the basis of the project of european construction.

in writing. - i voted against this draft budget because it implies the implementation of the policy of austerity at the level of the european institutions. in a context of crisis, and in the face of evidence that the austerity policy implemented in the countries of southern europe is being the mechanism for the destruction of the welfare state from which financial capital is the only beneficiary. the budget adopted accepts the cuts proposed by the council except for some items which it even increases, including the item to allocate more funds to frontex. parliament approves more funding for the walls of fortress europe and less for the inside. this is the austerity of the european economy in the name of financial interests. that is why i voted against this draft budget.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to reduce the negative impact that cuts in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 may have on the reduction of structural funds for cyprus. the report notes the mobilisation and approves the mobilisation of the flexibility mechanism to compensate for losses on certain items of the 2014 budget and welcomes the proposal to ensure that within this mobilisation the funds needed for the implementation of the structural policies so necessary for the cypriot economy are unequivocally guaranteed. the report approves the proposal to mobilise these funds for cyprus as quickly as possible. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves the release of funds to mitigate the serious consequences of the disasters in romania, germany, austria and the czech republic. the eu solidarity fund should continue to function properly and as effectively as possible to ensure the capacity to respond to any disasters that may occur on the continent. the european budget must be a tool for improving the lives of citizens, and if it is not able to cover emergency aid, such as floods and droughts, it cannot be considered as such. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it mobilises funds to mitigate the serious consequences of the disasters in romania, germany, austria and the czech republic. the eu solidarity fund has proven to be the most effective way possible to ensure the capacity to respond to disasters that may occur on the continent. this mobilization of resources to cover the reparation is the least that the different european peoples can do for any disaster that has occurred in europe. global warming is expected to increase the likelihood of such climate disasters, which will require such mechanisms to help people who are suffering from the crises caused by climate change. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves the release of funds to combat the most serious effects of the crisis in spain, italy and france. the european social fund, in its normal functioning, should ensure the financing of projects aimed at combating poverty and social exclusion in the member states. the european union is being forced to make all these budgetary adjustments because the payment commitments made during the year were greater than the funds actually available. with the reduction of the next multiannual financial framework these funding problems will become more serious. if we are to fight poverty, we must mobilize resources, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it involves the allocation of almost 8 billion euro within the multiannual financial framework, at the same time as the most basic rights of european citizens are being denied. this is a technology that can have interesting applications and also, without a doubt, important military applications. but i voted against it because it involves a transfer of public funds to technology companies, 9 billion euros could make a fundamental difference in solving problems of ordinary european citizens. if there are indeed scarce resources, as austerityists suggest, why not devote them to the most basic needs, instead of enriching an industry which is incapable of creating jobs for citizens? that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it is a macrofinancial assistance which is linked to the jordanian government implementing economic and political reforms geared to the economic interests of the european union. in this line, at the end of 2012 taxes were introduced on the consumption of diesel which led to major protests of the population by attacking the basic needs of the population. this aid will always be conditional on the imf having previously granted the country to deepen the neoliberal economic reforms whose effects have led to the economic crisis we are suffering today. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a step forward in preventing drug producers from operating within the member states of the european union. the report seeks to sanction this agreement to prevent the import of chemicals which are used in the manufacture of drugs. there are 23 drug precursors that are routinely imported at the border between russia and the eu, representing a trade of almost 5 million euros. this is a very small amount but it can allow the manufacture of large quantities of drugs. europe is a big consumer of drugs and this kind of import is the first step towards manufacturing them. attacking imports means attacking production, and preventing final consumption. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it rejects the council's proposal on cooperation with third countries through europol. this agreement would pose a major risk in the area of data protection for european citizens, since it establishes cooperation with third countries with much more lax legislation in this area. the report calls on the council not to implement its decision because any exchange of personal data with third countries must be carried out in compliance with the guarantee of respect for the privacy of european citizens in accordance with union law. since these guarantees have not been met, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because the current model of european research infrastructure consortia is not working properly as no associated or third country has participated in them to date. this report approves a minor amendment to council regulation (ec) no 723/2009 with the aim of allowing the participation in such consortia of entities from associated and non-associated third countries. the amendment to the wording of the regulation aims to remove the limitation on the participation of more countries in such consortia and to encourage a positive impact on the research sector. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
madam president, i believe that the report by mr van nistelrooij and mrs krehl on cohesion policy is a good report which will help the member states to get out of the crisis and will certainly increase social cohesion and economic growth. that is why the vote was in favour, logically, and above all because progress has been made in the possibility of covering several funds. the creation of crossborder regions has also been made possible; co-financing has been increased, especially for the most disadvantaged regions and also for regions in transition, and it is in line with the thematic concentration that marks the same objectives of the 2020 strategy. macro-conditionality has been decaffeinated and will therefore not be an obstacle to access to funds. as regards ex ante conditionalities, compliance with the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in relation to the removal of barriers to disability is particularly important.
in writing. - we cannot accept that citizens continue to pay for a crisis that they did not create, we cannot allow the austerity measures that the conservatives propose as a solution to continue to be applied when it has already been shown that they are counterproductive and lead only to social suffocation and the destruction of the welfare state. i have therefore opposed the proposal on the common provisions on european funds, because a cut of eur 7 billion in the european social fund would mean an increase in the problem of unemployment and thus more hunger, more social exclusion and more inequality in europe.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it makes the cohesion funds into a tool for blackmailing the member states of the european union. the so-called macro-conditionality implies that the council or the commission can request the blocking of the above-mentioned cohesion funds if the member state in question does not comply with the neoliberal policies set out in the specific recommendations. it is the instrument which will make it possible to threaten any member state which has an economic policy which is different from the suicide which austerity policies involve. i reject this report in the strongest possible terms because it is a weapon with which to extort the sovereignty of the member states from the troika.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it seeks to ensure that the objectives, which i share, of the european social fund are met, it is ultimately about implementing the objectives of the 2020 strategy. the report contains many very worthy positions, but it also includes coordination with the other economic policies of the european union. the report includes an amendment which makes the operation of the esf subject to the development of projects aimed at economic growth. although i agree with the approach, in practice it will mean that the esf will finance private enterprises and disregard social inclusion duties. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - as the european social fund is the largest budgetary item of the european structural and investment funds and the european union's main instrument for job creation and labour market support and, by extension, for combating social exclusion and inequality, i fully support any renewal and extension of its scope. the new regulation, among other things, envisages strengthening the eu's social dimension by obliging member states to invest 80% of esf resources in social investment priorities and the remaining 20% in the fight against poverty and social exclusion, which i consider a major step towards achieving the europe 2020 objectives. i sincerely believe that, however, there is still a long way to go and a lot of money to be spent, although i am pleased with the outcome of the negotiations with the council and the commission, for example the extension of the eligibility criteria for age and unemployment in the youth employment initiative and the greater flexibility in the macroeconomic conditionalities.
madam president, i want to say that the report is a positive report, and that is why we voted in favour of it. basically, it is interesting the thematic concentration and the derivation that is made, whether it is a developed region, in transition or less developed, to the fight against climate change, to low-carbon economies. for the first time, 5% of these erdf funds are being allocated to cities, which we find very interesting, and integrated territorial strategies are also being put in place to enable several funds to participate in the same operational programme. the only point on which i disagree is that corsica, sardinia and the balearic islands - where i come from - do not have the possibility of flexibility on thematic issues and that is therefore the only point on which we would disagree with this report. we also believe that everything that this report can do to combat the crisis is positive.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains amendments which could improve the functioning of the erdf, it does not adapt the erdf to the neo-liberal objectives of growth. the report approves at first reading the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing regulation (ec) no 1080/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. it introduces very important changes which may allow the financing of projects which may have a positive impact on many regions, such as the commitment to local community development, infrastructure development, etc. this source of finance is indispensable if there is to be real cohesion in europe. however, by subordinating the objectives of this fund to strategy 2020, it is overridden by the objectives of the markets. that is why i voted against.
madam president, we have supported the report by mrs riikka pakarinen because we believe that the increase in funding, especially in the areas of transnational, transregional and crossborder cooperation, is particularly important for europe at this time. however, i must make one caveat: the maximum distance of 150 kilometres for access to these funds has not been removed - in the case of many islands, for example, but especially the balearic islands - even though the abolition of this maximum distance for access to these funds was advocated in several resolutions of parliament and in other statements by the committee of the regions and the european institutions. this limit has not been removed and therefore the balearic islands and many other islands are excluded from these crossborder cooperation funds. i wanted to report him at this moment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, unlike the previous report, it has the clear aim of supporting european territorial cooperation, rather than supporting the neoliberal agenda of the markets. the policy of cooperation in europe is more fundamental than ever, the peoples must be solidarity mechanisms to face the crisis. the report introduces key points such as emphasising lessons learned from other regions or projects to improve the effectiveness of projects developed or ensuring that projects financed with erdf funds involving third countries also benefit member states. there are many provisions which will improve the functioning of this fund. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
madam president, i would like to stress the positive aspects of mr boştinaru's report on the cohesion fund, basically because, without any doubt, concentrating the cohesion fund on the thematic objectives already set out in the 2020 strategy will lead to greater progress with regard to the implementation of this programme in the past. the important new features of this fund would be everything related to energy efficiency which was already included in the thematic objectives of the general regulation and the use of renewable energy in the housing sector, as well as support for improved efficiency of district heating and cogeneration of heat and electricity. we are very positive about all this and therefore believe that the approval of this fund with these changes to adapt it to the 2020 strategy will help to combat inequalities between member states and to make progress in the fight against the crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be a suitable commitment to a type of integration which allows for balanced territorial development which is socially and environmentally sustainable. the report proposes a way of working for the cohesion funds that introduces ambitious environmental objectives while ensuring action in all those member states whose gdp is less than 90% of the european average. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the legislative package for cohesion policy 2014-2020, comprising five european structural and investment funds, was adopted today in plenary. the composition of the individual funds and the overall plan has been simplified to achieve better targeted programmes with a high degree of visibility of results and a more appropriate distribution of funds. i strongly support these budgets in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, which provide the eu and spain in particular with great development opportunities for both the most advanced and the most punished regions. for example, we have unrivalled advantages from the european regional development fund (erdf), which applies to different innovation, research and sme support programmes to reduce regional disparities between the eu, or the cohesion fund, which applies to europe's less developed and transition regions (with less than 90 per cent of gdp of the european average) and focuses on sustainable development projects such as energy efficiency, decontamination, infrastructure and green transport systems.
madam president, the commission and parliament have proposed in this report to amend the regulation on the european grouping of territorial cooperation, and we think that this has been very positive. there are many projects under way, and i would like to highlight one in particular: there is a hospital on the border between france and spain, and it was clear during the challenges of recent years that there were difficulties in the application of labour legislation and also in the application of the regulation itself. the legal framework has therefore been adapted to these challenges. in particular, these amendments make more specific application of labour law, which has undoubtedly given much greater legal certainty. so we think it's very positive that we can use the instrument safely.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it amends the regulation on the functioning of european territorial cooperation groupings in a positive way. such crossborder groupings make it possible to set up cooperation instruments around specific objectives bringing together actors from different territories of the union. the report seeks to adapt the legislation on crossborder groupings of this type to the new cohesion policy framework for the next financial period 2014-2020, seeking to facilitate and improve their functioning. that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a commitment to try to achieve equality for men and women in working conditions, a fundamental condition for the rule of law. this report focuses on the need to achieve gender balance in non-executive administrative posts in public and private enterprises by 2018 and 2020 respectively. the report arises from the fact that there are significant gender gaps in this area. it is very clear that this is not the main gender issue we are facing on the continent, but at least this report is trying to make progress towards equality in this sector. that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted against the amendments calling for the exclusion of family businesses from the scope of the directive, since they are only listed companies; moreover, the legislation provides for a margin of manoeuvre for member states to adapt the obligation to national circumstances.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it means the final approval of the proposal for the new common agricultural policy, which means a massive cut in the funds available while lowering the requirements to allow landowners to apply for funds for their uncultivated land by redefining 'permanent pasture'. we reject any cuts in the cap budget, as this is a sector which needs support because of the high rates of abandonment of farmers. this policy is intended to leave behind an agricultural policy that does not allow the benefit for economic, social and environmental sustainability, and to continue to allow the futility of guaranteeing unfair rents and agribusiness. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - parliament, for the first time, has decided jointly with the council on this important matter for the european union as a whole. the improvements introduced in the new common agricultural policy are intended to enable all regions of europe, whatever their type of agricultural activity, to improve their competitiveness. the new policy aims to strike a balance between food security and environmental protection, to encourage support for active farmers and to encourage young farmers by increasing extra support by 25%. the aim was to ensure a fair distribution of funds, but as far as spain is concerned, the european funds have not been maintained and this will be detrimental to catalonia, which will receive less of this aid and will therefore lose resources with the consequent impact on its competitiveness. from my position, i will continue to advocate rural and agricultural development programmes in order to promote regional competitiveness.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive provisions for the financial sector in relation to the obligation to report, i do not believe that this will provide a definitive protection for customers. this report comes after the scandal of preferential shareholdings where thousands of people were defrauded, despite the fact that there was already a european directive and spanish legislation prohibiting this type of practice. the previous legislative framework has shown that there is no political will to prosecute such infringements. the report seeks to improve the requirements for information distributed to customers, a positive measure, but one which comes too late and too lightly and without condemning the previous excesses of the sector, after the multimillion-dollar scams that are being carried out today. that is why i could not vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - although we have not achieved the reform of the common agricultural policy that the socialists would have wished for, we have achieved a more satisfactory reform than the one initially proposed. it benefits young people and small farmers and leads to a fairer distribution of aid, since it will be specifically targeted at active farmers. it also reconciles food safety with environmental protection, by achieving greater flexibility in direct payments conditional on environmental measures. it is now the turn of minister arias cañete to reflect these improvements effectively by defining the role of the active farmer in accordance with our guidelines.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it proposes the operation of the european agricultural fund for rural development, which enables large companies and landowners to enrich themselves at the expense of funds intended for the development of rural communities. thanks to this proposed regulation for the period 2014-2020, there is no reference to the main issues facing the sector: food security and food sovereignty, as well as the maintenance of the public sector in agriculture, etc. but all this has not been included, allowing public funds to be used to enrich agro-industry while farmers continue to disappear in rural europe. that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. i voted against this report because it is another missed opportunity to maintain a misrule which allows the continuation of the common market organizations which serve to allow very low remuneration for farmers and the enrichment of the dominant groups in the marketing system. we have advocated the establishment of maximum margins for the profits of intermediaries, and we have also proposed that the labour rights of agricultural workers be protected, including the location of production and consumption, etc. a policy has been maintained to ensure the profits of the distributing companies which can continue their price-fixing practices on farmers. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it allows for an unfair distribution of aid and direct payments among european farmers. the legislation adopted allows the large landowners to continue to enrich themselves, in contrast to proposals to set maximum limits on the receipt of direct payments; parliament has vetoed them to maintain the privileges of rentier families. some measures are introduced, such as increased support for small farmers, which should be the centre of such a policy, but is a marginal part of it. our commitment to a living rural world is not reflected in these rules and that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a proposal to allow a gradual transition from the 2007-13 cap to the 2014-2020 cap. the new cap should start to be implemented from 1 january 2014, but this report proposes a framework to smooth the changeover both in the policies relating to the first pillar, i.e. direct payments and market measures, and the second, which is aimed at rural development. we consider it a positive step that the member states should be able to benefit from this system in order to be able to adapt to the changes entailed by the profound change that the new cap entails. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it allows the implementation of numerous regional policy projects in member states with economic difficulties. the report proposes to relax the conditions for the implementation of eu-funded projects in these member states. in particular, they provide for the possibility of increasing the cofinancing rates and extending the release periods. these two measures should help the above-mentioned states to be in a position to meet their obligations and implement these projects which are part of cohesion policy. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it concerns the mobilisation of funds to meet the emergency situation which the economic crisis is causing in some member states. the report proposes to activate the european social fund to combat discrimination and the increase in poverty caused by the crisis in some member states. it is a palliative measure which does not put an end to the economic policy which is imposed and which is the cause of these situations; it is a small cure which does not solve the problems which austerity creates, but which is an effective help to the millions of europeans who are having a very difficult time. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against the amendments calling for the european social fund to be increased to include other countries with similar needs so that the interinstitutional agreement could be adopted and enter into force quickly; however, i support the underlying criticisms in the amendments regarding the lack of transparency of the eu council's procedure in the mff negotiations and, in particular, the positions taken by a member state threatening to leave the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is the fruit of a fair negotiation process between the european union and the republic of kiribati. the report is an improvement on the protocol allocating eur 1 325 000 per year to support the fisheries policy of kiribati. this report covers an agreement allowing access to the exclusive economic zone of kiribati. as kiribati has signed a number of tuna fisheries agreements, the agreement imposes an obligation on vessels from portugal, spain and france to comply with the sustainability criteria for tuna fishing in kiribati's waters when operating in those waters. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - as a socialist rapporteur, i voted in favour of the protocol between the european union and the republic of kiriwati, initialled by the commission on 3 june 2012. the protocol, which fixes the fishing opportunities and the financial contribution, has been provisionally applied since 16 september 2012 for a period of three years. the first fisheries agreement with kiriwati in 2003 made it possible for the european fleet to be present in the pacific. the new protocol builds on the 2007 fisheries partnership agreement and enables 10 european vessels (including four purse seiners) to exploit resources responsibly in the kiriwati exclusive economic zone and contributes to the development of a sustainable fisheries policy. the financial contribution is eur 1 325 000 per year for the period, including eur 350 000 per year in additional support for the fisheries sector in kiriwati. the protocol, according to the conclusions of parliament's legal report, is compatible with the nauru agreement, a multilateral agreement between eight countries in the area, which establishes the vessel day scheme (vds) methodology, provided that it is implemented in line with the international commitments undertaken by the eu. the european commission has made an explicit commitment to this end.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is an attempt to rationalize the expenditure involved in the existence of three seats for the european parliament. since the treaty on european union provides for the existence of the three seats, parliament cannot decide on its own location. this report seeks to give parliament's position on this, the multiplication of expenditure it entails and the need to avoid waste in these times of crisis. this report makes clear parliament's position in favour of a single seat to reduce the economic and environmental impact of the institution. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it raises the question of the rational functioning of this public institution.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, the new horizon 2020 framework programme comes at a crucial moment when europe must rely on research and innovation if it is to increase its competitiveness and create quality jobs. it's been almost two years of intense work. but i think we can all be proud of the agreement that has been reached, which also comes just in time for the programme to be implemented on time at the beginning of 2014. ladies and gentlemen, our scientists and european industry are going through very difficult times, especially in some of our member states, and it was our responsibility that horizon 2020 should not be delayed. we have drawn up a framework programme adapted to the difficult socioeconomic situation and the needs of the union. a knowledge-based economy requires scientific excellence and innovation-driven industrial leadership, as well as innovative responses to the social challenges that most concern citizens. the core of the programme will remain pre-competitive, medium-sized transnational cooperation projects, which will have a broader focus to cover the whole innovation chain. the parliament, thanks to the coordinated efforts of all the groups, has improved the original text proposed in several respects which i should like to stress. first, by reinforcing the excellence of our science and our research staff. we cannot continue to tolerate talent being wasted or forced to emigrate for lack of opportunity. we have therefore proposed measures to strengthen our capacity to attract, retain and promote the best talent. we have increased the budget for the marie curie actions and included a human resources indicator so that this factor is taken into account in the evaluation of horizon 2020. secondly, we have strengthened the channels of participation, with measures to support excellence wherever it is found. the new priority 'spreading excellence and widening participation' will help to open the programme to a wider range of participants. the agreement will also ensure a better and wider participation of smes, as we have increased the budget devoted to them and strengthened the new sme instrument. this was one of parliament's priorities because smes, ladies and gentlemen, are the main job creators and an essential player in bringing research results to the market through innovation. thirdly, clean energy and energy efficiency have also been strengthened by the agreement. in support of the eu's co2 reduction targets, parliament has secured 85% of the total budget for the social challenge 'energy' for research and innovation in these areas. fourthly, fundamental principles have been strengthened. in the area of gender equality, we have extended the new article 15 to cover a two-fold dimension: strengthening the presence of women and integrating a gender perspective into the content of research. and for the first time, an article has been included guaranteeing free and open access to publications arising from research funded by horizon 2020. both of these elements also have a clear impact on the excellence and efficiency of the programme and on the profitability of its budget. ladies and gentlemen, i would not like to end without thanking the work of all those who have made this agreement possible. thank you all for what has been a fruitful team effort.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission’s communication on strengthening the social dimension of economic and monetary union (emu) proposed a new scoreboard of key employment and social indicators to be used during the european semester. the scoreboard consists of five headline indicators: the unemployment rate; the neet (not in http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/education" \o "education" , http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/employment" \o "employment" , or http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/training" \o "training" ) rate in conjunction with the youth unemployment rate; real gross household disposable income; the at-risk-of-poverty rate; and income inequalities. the commission presented the scoreboard and its first analysis in the draft joint employment report on 13 november 2013. to answer your first sub-question, the commission believes that the scoreboard should identify the most serious employment and social problems and developments at an early stage, and before a country diverges too strongly from its past performance or from the rest of the european union. the scoreboard does not include statistical thresholds, meaning indicative values supporting and clarifying the interpretation of the indicators themselves. the commission has been cooperating with the relevant committees of the council to this end by presenting its proposals on a technical level. regarding your second sub-question, the commission believes that the five headline indicators which i mentioned will indeed allow for better identification of major employment and social difficulties that need to be addressed in the interest of the eu as a whole and, particularly, the sound functioning of monetary union. further analysis based on the scoreboard should draw upon the existing battery of indicators already used during the european semester, in particular the joint assessment framework, the employment performance monitor and the social protection performance monitor. as the commission pointed out in the draft joint employment report, it is open to considering possible refinements of the scoreboard in future editions, taking into account parliament’s views. on your third sub-question regarding the age brackets for the youth unemployment and neet rates, i recall that the council recommendation on establishing a youth guarantee refers to young people under the age of 25. it is this age group for which robust policies and measures addressing the school-to-work transition are most crucially needed, although unemployment and inactivity also affect a substantial number of young people aged over 25. member states are free to expand their youth guarantee schemes to include those over 25, where relevant, and can use the resources of the european social fund or the youth employment initiative to that end. on your fourth sub-question: as i mentioned, the commission has integrated the scoreboard of key employment and social indicators in the draft joint employment report. this will serve better to inform the setting of policy priorities for the 2014 european semester, as well as the process of multilateral surveillance and the preparation of euro area and country-specific recommendations. this brings me to your fifth sub-question, on how we detect alarming levels. the commission’s assessment of the scoreboard’s headline indicators was considered for each member state: firstly, the change in the indicator compared to earlier periods (i.e. the historical trends); secondly, the difference against the eu and euro area averages, which provides a snapshot of existing employment and social disparities; and, thirdly, the change in the indicator between two consecutive years relative to the change at eu and euro area levels. this comparison indicates the dynamics of socio-economic convergence or divergence. in your sixth sub-question you ask to what extent the commission acknowledges that there is specificity in the eurozone countries in relation to social challenges. this is a complex question on which i can only refer you to the commission communication on strengthening the social dimension of emu. on your seventh sub-question regarding the link between the commission communication and the wider agenda on emu completion, i would remind you that the commission’s ‘blueprint for a deep and genuine emu’ distinguishes steps to be taken in the short, medium and longer term. in the medium term, it identifies the need for deeper coordination of euro area labour markets. in the longer term, the possibility of an autonomous euro area budget, providing the euro area with a fiscal capacity to help member states to absorb shocks, is being considered. one possible stabilisation tool identified in that context was an emu-level unemployment insurance scheme. measures of that nature would, however, require a treaty change as the eu currently does not have the competence to adopt them. in any event, the october 2013 european council welcomed the commission communication on the social dimension of emu as a positive step. finally, on your last sub-question, i can confirm that the commission is continuing to pursue its analysis on the longer-term possibilities and options for completing emu, as presented in its blueprint and its communication on the social dimension of emu. part of this technical work concerns the feasibility and the possible design of an automatic fiscal stabiliser operating at emu level.

mr president, commissioner, president of the court of auditors, i share your view that the error rate of 4.8% in the expenditure of the 2012 budget of the european union is high. the data show that the error rate has been increasing over the last three years, but the court of auditors' annual report also reveals that the areas where the highest percentage is recorded are those of shared management between the member states and the european commission, such as agriculture and cohesion. these figures show that both the control system and the supervision system need to be improved. while we share the need to improve these managing authorities everywhere, we also need to look at the figures in depth and not be simplistic: it would be wrong to take this error alone into account to talk about expenditure control in the european union as something that is not being done well. the citizens should know that 'error' does not necessarily mean 'fraud', and this is what the court of auditors itself says. on the other hand, we should not lose sight of the fact that we are at the end of a programming period, which means that in recent years, in particular in 2012, there has been an increased demand for expenditure - which must also be taken into account when analysing these data - and we should not overlook the change in sampling methodology, something that has also been recognised by the court of auditors itself. i would also like to stress the part that is done right, namely that 130 billion euros have been spent correctly - which means 95 per cent of the expenditure is free from error - and the taxpayer also needs to know this to be at ease. we must work together to correct those mistakes which may overshadow the good results achieved, which are many.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, first of all i would like to thank all of you for this very good debate on the report of the court of auditors. we have to be very clear that the report by the court of auditors revealed that more than 95% of the eu budget is spent correctly. it is very important to take that into account. we also have to take into account that in 2012, the commission corrected 3.2% of the spending made in the member states. just add up to 95.2%, the figure which i just presented and you will see that really we have a relatively good system in dealing with eu spending. we should not forget that the court said very clearly that the accounts of the commission are clean and that they present a true picture of the accounting system in the european union. of course, we have weaknesses, and i acknowledged that very clearly in my introductory remarks. and of course we have to address these weaknesses in a proper way. but we also have to work and to act within the legal framework which we have and which was adopted by the co-legislators, namely the european parliament and the council. we cannot invent actions which are not foreseen in the existing legal framework. thanks to our joint action in the preparation of the legislative framework for the next programming period, we really are moving in the right direction and will be able to better address problems related to errors, particularly in the area of shared management. actually, all of you who spoke today said that we still face problems in shared management. we have to tackle those problems. first of all, a very important tool is the net financial correction, which was agreed during the negotiations. we are working with the rapporteur on how to introduce this new instrument in the most efficient way and to use it in a targeted way in order to address serious problems. we should also remember that we introduced in the financial regulation management declarations of the member states. member states will now have to present these declarations to the commission and to this parliament. we are working in close cooperation with jan mulder on the design of national declarations and i and am a strong supporter of this approach and believe that the working group which we established together with this parliament, and together with the council, will provide good ideas on how we can better use this instrument at national level too. we should also remember simplifications which we introduced in the new legal framework, and it is very important that member states use those simplifications in the correct way. the report of the court of auditors this year clearly revealed that in those cases where member states use already existing simplification instruments, the level of error is negligible or even non-existent, so i think that it is very important that we encourage member states to use these simplifications. mr gerbrandy raised the issue of performance, and i think that the new programming framework really addresses very thoroughly the performance management issues. the programmes in shared management are based on performance criteria, is our common objective to ensure that eu spending is based on performance and not just on input. having said that, i want to stress once again that we are taking the report of the court of auditors very seriously. we have analysed very seriously their findings and are preparing the implementation action plans for the court’s recommendations. i believe that working together with this parliament, together with the court of auditors, we will ensure better spending of eu money.
court of auditors. − mr president, honourable members, i want to thank you firstly for the kind words you addressed to the court and those who work there. i note the requests you have addressed to us today calling for more insight at member state level, for a review of our approach to the annual report, possibly questioning our material threshold, and also for a more performance-oriented approach to what we do. i take good note of these requests and i can tell you that we are already taking them seriously. i want to make it very clear, however, that there has been no manipulation whatsoever of the nature of the findings in this report. the court is an independent professional audit institution and we stick to the highest standards of our profession in addressing and reporting on our findings. so i have to reject strongly the claim that our error rates are politically manipulated. the fact is that some of the errors the court finds are considered not quantifiable for purposes of determining the most likely error. the method used here is very technical, and i will not waste your time this morning explaining it, but it means that some of the errors taken into account in our estimation of the frequency of errors found in our sample are not extrapolated for the calculation of most likely errors. we are not sweeping these errors under the carpet. they are taken very seriously into account. the majority of them relate to procurement situations in which certain rules were not observed without making the tendering procedure as such ineligible – i.e. the tender has been assigned correctly but some rules were not observed, thus creating an erroneous situation. that said, i note strongly that everyone must assume their responsibilities, and the court will assume its responsibilities. we want very much to be part of the solution – we have been calling for several years for a clear approach to the management of the restes à liquider – the outstanding commitments. we know that there is a structural gap between commitments and appropriations; that gap increased over the period and we ended 2012 with a major gap in terms of the liabilities recorded in the accounts. the balance sheet of the union does indeed record a gap between commitments and appropriations which is very serious. that should not prevent all those responsible for adopting the budget, the commission with its management responsibilities, or the member states as contributors from their own resources to the budget, from exercising proper management of cashflow needs over the next programming period, in order to avoid precisely the pressure we have experienced during the past five years in relation to our payment budget. we addressed that question this week here in parliament. everyone has to assume their share of responsibility. the court cannot present its report earlier because we need the accounts to be available, and the final accounts of the union are ready only in july. only after that can we do our final work. discussions were held when we changed the financial regulation – which will enter into force in january 2014 – and we must respect the timetable agreed by all the eu institutions. let me emphasise in conclusion, mr president, that, as i said at the beginning, we need a new approach to the management of eu funds. we need everyone, at member state level and in the european institutions, to focus on a performance culture. there are lessons to be learned from the previous programming period and i believe that the work the court has done already on the first phase of closing the period 2007-2013 will be updated when the 2007-2013 programme is closed. we will then provide an overall picture of the results and the lessons we have to learn. but just this week you adopted the new high-level framework for 2014-2020. this week and next, you will decide as a parliament on the direction to be taken in future in relation to the eu’s financial management and use of funds. if we want to be more performance-oriented, more focused on results with clear objectives and simple rules, you now have the opportunity to state that. we are, of course, looking closely at the next stage of the implementing rules and implementing regulations, the so-called ‘delegated acts’, to ensure that the right path is being followed there. at the end the rapporteur. - mr president, just a minute to emphasize that the new framework programme we are about to vote on comes at a crucial moment for europe. this is a time when the european union must invest in research and innovation if it is to increase its competitiveness, grow and create quality jobs. i would also like to highlight the enormous work done by this parliament over the last two years and thank all my colleagues, the commission and the council for making possible an agreement of which we are all proud. while some of our member states are wrongly turning their backs on research and innovation, this parliament, thanks to fruitful teamwork, has achieved a horizon 2020 that is truly an opportunity for research and innovation in europe and, more importantly, an opportunity for our researchers.
mr president, as co-rapporteur with professor moreira of this motion for a resolution, i would like to table an oral amendment to amendment no 5 by the socialist group to remove the references to non-tariff barriers, as it is not appropriate, from our point of view, to include them here. the second sentence of the amendment would thus read as follows: 'welcomes the resumption of negotiations on the expansion of the information technology agreement, which increases both the range of products covered and the number of countries within its scope'.
in writing. − while national governments such as spain underestimate investment in r & d & i as a solution to the current crisis, the european parliament has opted for a horizon 2020 strategy that is adapted to europe's current needs in this area. in my region of cantabria, we are suffering an industrial decline which is forcing massive redundancies and dozens of industries to cut back or close their doors in the face of the passivity of the current regional government. innovative projects such as the cantabrian science and technology park or the promotion of research at the university were launched with the socialist government. in horizon 2020, although we do not agree with the cuts imposed by the council, the socialists have achieved through our rapporteur achievements such as strengthening the role of women in science and innovation or the greater participation of smes.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it introduces the competitiveness criteria and the participation of private enterprise in the successors to the european research framework programme no 7 (fp7). the report introduces the objectives of the horizon 2020 strategy in the definition of the objectives of the research programme. this implies that the relevance of research will be assessed in terms of its potential to generate benefits for the private sector, and that private participation in the co-financing of the actions of the programme will be enhanced. excellence, which can be understood as a form of discrimination based on the ideological position taken by research, is becoming a requirement, at the same time as funding is being cut in many european universities, preventing them from competing for it and relegating them to the background. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. − this new framework will cover all the programmes that have existed in the field of research and innovation to date. it aims to simplify the rules for obtaining funding, improve research and increase the participation of both industry and smes, with a view to creating jobs and improving the economy. it is important to note that the aim is to encourage all types of innovation in smes with the aim of stimulating economic activity. this will include facilitating access to seed funding, granting grants, assisting with commercialization and investing in technologies to make smes market leaders and thus boost economic growth. this new measure is intended to create 3.7 million jobs throughout the eu and i therefore welcome the adoption of this budget.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it extends the criteria for competitiveness and private enterprise participation in the successors to fp7 and in the dissemination agreements under these framework programmes. the report contained an amendment which could mean the cancellation of collaboration agreements with israeli universities with facilities in the occupied palestinian territories, but the majority groups have prevented its vote. the report therefore allows the establishment of research agreements with entities that violate international law to continue with total impunity. this cannot be allowed to happen in the use of european union research funds and that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive points aimed at boosting research and technological development in europe, it includes the criterion of excellence as the only bridge to achieve the quality of research work. the report includes many positive measures which can give a boost to the development of research in the european union. however, by identifying 'excellence' as the sole vehicle for ranking universities, it can serve as a tool to divide european university systems into two categories, those marked by excellence on the one hand and those not. this would be an attack on cohesion by locating research in the most favoured areas of the continent. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − today, the european parliament adopted the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme) programme for the period 2014-2020 with a budget of eur 2.030 million. i am particularly pleased with this result, as it will improve access to finance and the internalization of smes and facilitate more favourable conditions for entrepreneurs and the setting up of new businesses. in addition to the benefits in terms of innovation and growth that can be achieved, the immediate consequence will be job creation. it should be remembered that smes generate 67% of jobs in the european private sector, a percentage which is likely to increase thanks to the contribution of this initiative.
in writing. − i would to stress once again my concerns over the situation of credit to smes in europe. as the crisis deepens, credit to the real economy continues to fall and to be more and more expensive. not because of the financial situation of the smes, but because of their location inside the eurozone. this situation has to be tackled as the transmission mechanism of monetary policy is de facto broken. another distortion is created by the fact that some banks receiving state aid use this money to buy more sovereign debt when at the same time they reduce the credit to smes and households.
in writing. - i voted against this report because our group is totally different from most of the other groups in this parliament in describing what creates insecurity in the world and what force must be used to bring about security. we don't share the majority line at all. nato, its bases, its extrajudicial executions and western imperialism are the cause of world insecurity, not the solution. the occupation of a member state, cyprus, by a turkish military force is also creating insecurity in europe, and there is no response to that. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because our group is totally opposed to the development of armaments as a means of increasing the security of the european union. europe is one of the world's leading arms exporters and a boost to its arms industry does not mean an improvement in european security, but rather a further increase in instability in the regions to which its industries export. the report proposes harmonization and cooperation of the criteria governing the arms industry in the various member states. however, the arms industry should not be treated as a normal sector because of the consequences of these industries. i am opposed to the development of this industry, and i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the amendments calling for a balance between social and macroeconomic indicators in the evaluation of national policies because it is more and better defined than in the motion for a resolution; on the other hand, the social dimension must be very much present in the framework of the newly adopted clause on the conditions imposed for macroeconomic reasons in cohesion policy.

on behalf of the ppe group mr president, for the group of the european people's party, the negotiating process after the first reading has made it possible to incorporate into the future cfp aspects which were essential to us and which, while not taking away from its ambition, add to it the realism and flexibility which were absent both from the commission's initial proposal and from the rapporteur's report. since the council's position was closer to the approaches of our group, the result of the tripartite dialogues is much more satisfactory to us, particularly on key issues such as exploitation models, discards, the content of multiannual plans, fleet capacity management and attention to the situation of mixed fisheries, which are overlooked despite the fact that they constitute the majority of the union's fisheries. the commission has also taken note of the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a regulation on the management of the stocks of certain species of fish in the baltic sea. in another of the most complex issues, the prohibition of discards, a more realistic timetable has been achieved, as the epp proposed, taking into account mixed fisheries. solutions and transitional periods are also being considered for cases where increasing selectivity is extremely difficult or landing costs are disproportionate, and an outlet has been sought for fleets which do not have quotas for certain species or which are too low to be able to combine discard policy with maintaining activity.
