mr president, we have reached the end of the process of reforming the common fisheries policy as far as its basic regulation and also the market regulation are concerned. we will adopt the new cfp by vote tomorrow. it has been a long, and at times complicated, period, covering this entire legislature, and which began in 2009 with the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy. the great push given by the irish presidency, together with good interinstitutional cooperation, have been fundamental to getting us where we are today. and i think the political objective has been achieved. we shall have a fisheries policy which ensures ecological, social and economic sustainability, based on the best available scientific data, and in which discards will no longer be permitted. the member states may also, through regionalisation, propose conservation measures and agree on them with other coastal member states. this is the end of the process and marks the beginning of a new way of fishing and managing. the member states have a lot of work ahead of them if they want to be part of a genuine regionalisation.

mr president, for some people, in politics everything seems to be worth it. and commitments are worthless. what a pity! unfortunately, there are those in this house who want to be the sole guardians of fisheries resources, ignoring the fact that the real guardians of fisheries resources are the fishermen themselves. the same fishermen who are being pushed into an irreversible situation by the commission's proposal. if, as he claims, the deep-sea trawling and bottom trawling are banned, the consequences will be economically and socially catastrophic for many fishing-dependent communities who cannot afford it. four examples: the united kingdom estimates that about 400 british vessels would be affected by the proposal; in france, taking into account only four ports, about 500 direct jobs related to the 32 vessels licensed to fish for bottom species would be lost; portugal would also be significantly affected by a ban such as the proposal; and, if we refer to spain, it is clear that it would make it impossible to operate the nafo, neafc and norwegian trawling censuses in international waters and the union's trawling censuses for the 300-ton fleet, as well as the flying and scallop censuses in the north-western cantabrian. but what is more serious is that this proposal for a ban on trawling has been tabled against the opinion of the member states, the ccrs, the scientific committees of nafo and neafc. trawling has not been banned in any country in the world, not even in new zealand, which is a model for the world of sustainable fishing and which is very close to the barrier reef. nor has it been banned by any regional fisheries organization or by the united nations general assembly itself. think about it. it's compatible to protect and fish. protect and fish. let's do it like this.
mr president, i want to say that the european union is indeed committed to ensuring that by 2020 its marine ecosystems are in good condition and will remain so in the future. the marine strategy framework directive establishes this obligation for member states. we all know that deep waters are especially sensitive because they have habitats with biodiversity that has been formed over long periods of time and because there are vulnerable species that, in the event of loss, recover over very long periods of time. that is why, after ten years in which the measures adopted have not worked, we have welcomed the commission's position, which included drastic measures. we think it is not necessary to use the saw in this case. we have to make a surgery, and that is why we have reached a compromise in the committee, defining the deep-sea fisheries policy, establishing a list of vulnerable species, establishing conditions and limits for authorizations, establishing a list of sensitive ecosystem areas and establishing an assessment. we think it would be good if parliament had broad support to get the council to agree and to avoid measures which would divide our position.
mr president, the preparation of this report has been a difficult process and i will make the most of the compromise reached, because i believe that this is the way forward. the basque country has four vessels that fish below 600 metres, but this does not mean that it is a fishery targeting deep-sea species. they don't fish for sharks, just for turbot. they do it during the day and only for two or three months a year, with a more artisanal character than the rest and hardly have discards, as stated in a report by the azti institute made at the request of the sector itself. they should therefore be exempted from the application of this regulation and used, madam commissioner, as an example of good practice to be applied at european level. the amendments tabled at the last minute may destroy a sector which is and should be an example. it is clear that the sector itself is most interested in maintaining sustainability, and this we must do in collaboration with scientific institutes and with objective data to make our sector a profitable and sustainable sector.
madam president, let's focus the debate. scientists are warning us - and this is something we have all known about these days - that vulnerable deep-sea species and habitats are the subject of some of the most destructive fishing practices by some of the european union fleets. and not only that, but we are doing it with european union funds. deep-sea bottom trawling causes considerable environmental damage and does not offer any positive economic returns. this is the kind of activity, which is also subsidised, and it is precisely this type of activity that we want to put an end to with the amendment which we have tabled for tomorrow's sitting. i believe that we have a great opportunity, as we have done in the past, in passing the reform of the fisheries policy. we did that in due course when we passed a much stricter regulation to protect sharks. we have also done so on a number of occasions in a very clear way, when we have sent a message in favour of a much more responsible management policy, not to feed the overfishing. and tomorrow we have a new opportunity to show that this parliament is on the side of: (1) common sense, and therefore scientific analysis; and (2) future generations and their right to continue to enjoy that sea, those oceans, which, let us not forget, are a common good.
the rapporteur, mrs lulling, has already said that the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments proposed by the rapporteur. the council's mandate to the commission to open negotiations included similar demands to those of this parliament. the basic aim was to improve the economic efficiency of the protocol so that the price paid for access to resources would have an adequate return for the european union, favouring the full use of the fishing opportunities obtained. in addition, criteria were included concerning commitment to sustainable development, negotiating only on fisheries surpluses; the incorporation of a human rights clause and the inclusion of guarantees that the protocol complies with international law and, in particular, with the commitments entered into by morocco within the united nations. the commission has negotiated a protocol which, in the opinion of the committee on fisheries, meets all these requirements and which has also been approved by the committee on budgets and the committee on development. it also has the support of the eu and moroccan fisheries sectors and of european trade unions. i would now like to highlight some of the progress that best demonstrates the consistency of the european parliament's requests: fishing opportunities have been negotiated for 126 vessels flying the flag of 11 member states, which will employ 1 500 crew, of which approximately 500 will be local; on behalf of the ppe group madam president, the negotiated protocol fulfils the council's mandate, fully complies with the european parliament's 2011 resolution and satisfies the european fisheries sector by allowing sustainable, long-term and profitable fishing that is beneficial to both parties. the protocol grants 126 fishing licences to be distributed among 11 countries of the european union, of which 100 would be for spain. from the labour point of view, this protocol would provide jobs for 1,500 crew members - 500 of whom are moroccans - and 3,000 workers in related activities. and, speaking of spain, it would support more than 800 families, mainly andalusians and canarians. as far as the cost-benefit ratio is concerned, it is much better adjusted. it is a much better deal for fishermen and cheaper for the union. and for those who have doubts outside of the strictly fisheries aspect, i want to say that this agreement, which is also fully in line with international law - as the legal services say - is also fully in line with the mandates. it contains the obligation to respect human rights and democratic principles and also allows the european union to suspend its application in the event of a breach of any of these rights or principles. so much policy can be made at the expense of this protocol, which was not done with the agricultural protocol, for example. but of course, what cannot be questioned is some of the questions that are being questioned. there is not a single legal argument, or one of fisheries interests, that can be called into question. it's good protocol and deserves our approval. and mrs fraga deserves our thanks for her excellent report.

in writing. − the 'justice' programme for the seven-year period 2014-2020 has as its main objectives the effective and coherent promotion of union legislation in the fields of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters, the facilitation of access to justice and the prevention and reduction of drug demand and supply. in particular, it is precisely this last of the three objectives that we wanted to emphasize and strengthen by means of specific amendments in committee. for these reasons, i believe that the overall package proposed by the rapporteur is valid.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it means the adoption of a common justice programme for the period 2014-2020 which is not based exclusively on the legal guarantees of citizens, but on the objectives imposed by the european union. the report proposes funding for the eu's crossborder justice programme in the face of the increasing number of cases of a transnational nature in the union. it proposes positive measures for necessary cooperation in civil and criminal matters, such as training, mutual learning, etc. however, the financing of the programme is conditional on the development of indicators for monitoring the implementation of the programme. these indicators are outside any kind of judicial basis and imply political interference in judicial systems. that is why i voted against.
in writing. − in favour. the proposal is a part of the mff. it seeks to establish the justice programme for 2014-2020. originally it was planned that this programme would replace three current programmes: civil justice (jciv); criminal justice (jpen); the drug prevention and information programme (dpip). the general objective of the programme was to contribute to the creation of a european area of justice by promoting judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters with some specific objectives, to promote effective, comprehensive and consistent application of union legislation in the areas of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters among them. we, the greens, agreed that the programme is necessary. we had some reservations about the inclusion of drugs, as this might create a wrong perception that drugs should be primarily addressed from the justice perspective. we suggested ensuring that fundamental rights play a central role in the implementation of the programme. we also supported promotion of judicial training, as well as development of indicators for a better assessment of the implementation and ensuring a stronger role for the parliament in its implementation (through delegated acts).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a slight improvement in the implementation of the fundamental rights of european citizens. this report proposes a programme for the next budgetary period which for the first time covers the subject of full european citizenship. there is no european instrument to date which guarantees that fundamental rights and freedoms are respected in the member states. this programme will finance actions aimed at the development of citizens' rights, the implementation of non-discrimination, the rights of the child, etc. although this report will prove incomplete in guaranteeing fundamental rights in the union, it does promote these rights and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − this new programme aims to create an area for the promotion, development and protection of the rights of persons as recognised in the european treaties. it aims to strengthen rights such as equality between men and women, non-discrimination and combating violence against children, young people and women, but also aims to ensure the protection of privacy. i welcome the fact that funds are being efficiently managed to develop and continue these programmes and that public awareness is being supported on issues of such importance to society.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it complies with international law and allows trade flows with moldova to continue, it will have serious effects on the wine sector in many european countries. the european union is also committed to the development of the internal market and the free movement of goods. however, the fact that wine is produced in moldova at a much lower average cost will allow large wine-growing groups to buy the product in that country and bottle it in european countries at the expense of local producers and for the benefit of these large business groups. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. in 2008 the eu removed all tariffs for industrial products from moldova and improved access to the eu market for some agricultural products. these autonomous trade preferences (atp) are valid through to end 2015. such unilateral actions which go against the wto principle of non-discrimination (because they positively discriminate in favour of moldova) need to be accepted by the entire wto membership. this ‘waiver’ was valid for five years and runs out on 1. january 2014. however, the eu did not just want to turn to the wto with the request to prolong the waiver. it also wanted to enhance market access for agricultural products from moldova, especially wine, which is the major export product of moldova. the addition of wine to the list of zero tariff products came in the wake of the russian import ban for moldovan wine. the import ban was justified with ‘phytosanitary problems’, but indeed is part of the current russian threat strategy against eu eastern neighbourhood countries. greens support the measure as a concrete sign of solidarity with eastern european countries that are presently pressured by russia. greens also supported the shortening of the due legislative process, which in this case is justified by the urgency of the measure.
mr president, i voted with my group, but that does not prevent me from joining those who, like mr cofferati, mr milana and others, call for the inevitable involvement of europe in the solution of the sahara conflict. and that the people who have been forcibly occupied should achieve freedom, an initiative which was in the original position of the s&d group negotiators as a parallel political agreement. and today, on human rights day, on the funeral of mandela, whom i had the honour of meeting in oviedo, my home town, and on the centenary of willy brandt, we should be encouraged to keep a close eye on the situation of saharawi political prisoners, in particular those convicted in the rabat trial, which i found to be a complete sham. these brutal, indiscriminate and arbitrary sentences and the treatment of the moroccan occupier in prison are very much to be feared in the light of this very agreement voted here.
in writing. - the agreement between the european union and morocco also covers the waters of western sahara. the economic interests of some member states have outweighed the rights of the saharawi people and international law. this agreement is in clear violation of international law. morocco is an occupying force and has no sovereignty over western sahara. according to the united nations, western sahara has the status of an autonomous territory. consequently, morocco has no right to dispose of the natural resources of western sahara. that is why i voted against.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it makes the european union complicit in the plundering of the saharawi natural resources by the moroccan occupying force. my group is not opposed to a fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco, agreed by both parties, which guarantees the sustainable exploitation of marine resources. but we cannot show our support for the usurpation and theft of the resources of a people who, despite morocco's efforts to eliminate them, still exist and have the right and international legitimacy to exploit their natural resources. morocco continues to violate international law and the eu is acting as an accomplice by sanctioning an illegal agreement. that is why i voted against.
in writing. - i voted against because the european parliament has looked the other way and ignored the demands of the saharawi people to approve this controversial agreement. the fisheries agreement between the eu and morocco is the most shameful episode in europe's neocolonial fisheries policy. under the agreement, the moroccan government illegally grants fishing rights to the european fleet to fish in western sahara waters, in violation of international law. in addition to the flagrant violation of western sahara's rights, the agreement does not guarantee sustainability from the fisheries point of view and its economic basis is doubtful. this agreement will remain a black mark on the eu's foreign and fisheries policy.
in writing. - i appreciate the efforts made by the european commission to improve the agreement. support the reduction of financial cost in accordance with the cfp criteria, the possible improvement of profitability for the spanish fleet and measures to adapt fishing capacity to surpluses, ensuring sustainable management. i abstain because the question of western sahara remains unresolved: the agreement does not explicitly exclude its territorial waters or guarantee respect for the legitimate interests of the saharawi people. it also lacks a mechanism to verify the respect of human rights by the kingdom of morocco, which is a serious matter when one considers the constraints on sections of the population such as workers, journalists and other professionals.
in writing. - i voted in favour because this proposal will enable states to ratify ilo convention no 170, which will lead to greater safety at work and the correct use of chemicals.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify ilo convention no 170 on the safety of chemicals at work. convention no 170 is of fundamental importance for the protection not only of workers but also of society and the environment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it implements an international labour organisation convention in european law, improving the safety conditions of workers on the continent. ilo convention 170 regulates the safety of the use of chemicals at work and improves the protection of workers who have to handle such substances, trying to prevent diseases and health problems. the report seeks to implement in european law all the provisions of the convention which fall within community competence and calls for the member states to be allowed to ratify the convention in the areas which fall within national competence. i voted in favour of this report because it improves the safety of workers.
in writing. − the desire for the protocol against the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms to achieve more accessions by member states is the basis for this report on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. the protocol calls on the member states to proceed and to commit themselves to the establishment of an effective and harmonized system of export or import licences and authorizations. this is desirable, however, if we move towards greater simplification and not towards further complication of the existing legislation in this field.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it introduces the ratification at european union level of the protocol on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. the protocol complements the united nations convention against transnational organized crime, with the aim of enhancing the international commitments of the european union as a whole in the fight against organised crime and its activities. ratification at european level implies implementation throughout the union because the legal obstacles preventing full ratification in the member states have been removed. i voted in favour of this report because of the improvement it brings to the fight against organised crime.
in writing. − in favour. the proposal seeks to conclude on behalf of the eu the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, supplementing the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. the united nations convention against transnational organized crime (untoc), adopted on 15 november 2000, is the first global instrument in the fight against transnational organised crime and trafficking in firearms. three protocols supplement the convention, providing for specific measures against specific crimes. the protocols cover respectively trafficking in persons, smuggling of migrants and illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms. the european community signed the convention on 12 december 2000. we approve the agreement. we welcome the efforts by the united nations in the fight against transnational organised crime and believe that the european union should join those efforts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents the correct implementation of the agreements reached by the european union in international fora. with the accession of romania and bulgaria, the eu agreed to negotiate mutually compensatory agreements with the members of the world trade organisation for both countries and with the other countries which had trade agreements with the new eu member states. the agreement is not problematic and favours the maintenance of relations with china, since trade volumes are low, mainly in agri-foodstuffs. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it represents a fundamental improvement in the quality of meat imported into the eu, it does imply a step forward in trade relations between the two blocs. because of differences in the hormone content of beef between us and eu beef, the eu blocked imports and the us retaliated with sanctions that have seriously affected the livestock sector. the agreement provides for progress to be made in this area by 2015 without compromising on the maximum hormone content of beef, but allowing trade relations in the sector to be normalised. however, such standardization will in turn lead to dangerous competition for european farmers. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − against. the european union and the united states have been engaged in a long-running dispute over the eu’s ban on hormone-treated beef. nevertheless, on 13 may 2009, the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding (mou), paving the way to a definite resolution of the so-called ‘beef hormone dispute’. so far, for us the greens, we are far away from an acceptable text.
in writing. the first fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of côte d'ivoire was signed in 1990. this agreement, renewed in 2013 for a further five years, concerns fishing opportunities and defines the financial counterpart between the two entities. the majority of ivorian tuna production, with an average of about 55 000 tonnes per year, is exported to the eu. i am voting in favour of this protocol because it is beneficial for both parties, in line with the expectations of the european institutions (promotion of aquaculture, combating iuu fishing and data confidentiality) and because it also offers the possibility of creating new jobs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it contains a balanced fisheries agreement, negotiated sovereignly between the two parties and which does not contain any violation of international law. this is an agreement which started in 1990 and involves a relatively long-term partnership which brings benefits to both parties, with côte d'ivoire sharing in the benefits of the agreement. this collaboration agreement will allow 28 freezer tuna seiners and 10 french and spanish flag longliners to participate in the sustainable exploitation of these waters and provides economic compensation for the country. as a result of fair negotiations and no violation of the law, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this agreement because it is part of the commitment of the european institutions to the outermost territories such as the canary islands, which prove by deeds and not just words that europe is a territory of values where solidarity is practised and sustainable activities and sectors of activity that seek profitability are encouraged even in the most difficult conditions. this decision supports the canary islands fisheries sector, extends the existing tariff agreement and ensures that the local fisheries sector meets the needs of internal supply, while allowing the import flows to the union under these conditions to remain predictable and clearly identifiable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a measure of economic support to an outermost region in line with the treaty. the report proposes authorising import quotas for certain fishery products from third countries free of customs duties from the european union. spain has requested the extension of these import quotas which would otherwise expire on 1 january 2014. this measure is designed to guarantee internal consumption and to compensate the islands' fishing industry for the transport costs incurred by their access to the common market due to their geographical location. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it is a measure to support the economy of the canary islands.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it allows the mobilisation of resources to alleviate the consequences of unemployment in the mobile telephony sector in finland. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the european union. in particular, eur 9.81 million is being mobilised to finance programmes for the 3719 workers made redundant in various subcontractors of the nokia company due to the relocation of production to asia. these scarce funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama suffered by the workers. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it allows the mobilisation of resources to alleviate the consequences of unemployment in the renewable energy sector in germany. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the european union. in particular, eur 2 305 357 is mobilised to finance programmes for the 875 workers made redundant in various subcontracting companies of first solar due to the fall in demand in the sector. these scarce funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama suffered by the workers. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. according to the german authorities, the measures initiated on 1 january 2013 combine to form a coordinated package of personalised services and represent active labour market measures with the aim of reintegrating the workers into the labour market. it has to be noted that more than half of the egf support will be spent on allowances – 875 workers are said to receive during their active participation in the measures a subsistence allowance (estimated cost eur 2 714 per worker over nine months). parliament further notes that the application includes a lump sum of eur 1 869 activation premium for 200 workers who quickly find a job without further assistance after the conclusion of the measures. this is not in line with the spirit of the egf regulation which foresees that the egf support should primarily be allocated to job search and training programmes instead of contributing directly to financial allowances.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it allows the mobilisation of resources to alleviate the consequences of unemployment in the renewable energy sector in denmark. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the european union. in particular, eur 6 364 643 is being mobilised to finance programmes for the 611 workers made redundant in various subcontracting companies of the vestas company due to the fall in demand in the sector. these scarce funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama suffered by the workers. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although the association agreement introduces numerous measures for the promotion of human rights and the fight against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, it represents a boost to transatlantic trade which will introduce aggressive competition for european small and mediumsized enterprises. international trade between relatively similar economies such as canada's and europe's only increases competition between industrial systems. in the serious situation of the european economy, such treaties will only lead to more closures and more unemployment. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − against. contrary to what the rapporteur suggests, we greens oppose to the conclusion of such an agreement.
in writing. - i voted against this report despite the fact that it includes new control measures for the banking sector, because it assumes the rescue of financial institutions as a fundamental measure for economic development. financial bailouts in the southern european countries have caused the current state of the economy, squandering public resources to secure funds for private entities that are financed through the interest on public debt. the rescue of financial institutions is an attack on european citizens, since it means that the common resources are being put into the pockets of a financial sector which has been defrauding and impoverishing europeans. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − in favour. the rapporteur, currently taking a market infrastructure file through trilogue (central securities depositaries) and having been shadow on another key market infrastructure file (‘emir’) concerning clearing houses, had focused exclusively on these types of firms. our main aim was to: call for the use of the vast amount of reporting data now required under a plethora of legislative acts to monitor the flow of risk throughout the union and identify hotspots; stress that any recovery and resolution mechanism requires supervisors to develop a ‘ladder of intervention’ – relevant and comprehensive dashboards of key indicators to monitor the health of financial institutions and trigger early intervention; call for consideration of r&r mechanisms for insurers and re-insurers as well (following iais and fsb principles). the final compromise text was satisfactory for us, covering all our desiderata.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it proposes a multi-billion dollar investment in the space industry, while europe has important industrial sectors which are suffering from the crisis and laying off thousands of workers. the companies that make up the fabric of the space industry are strongly linked to the arms industry and it is striking that the european union is supporting this sector while leaving many industries within the member states of the union to their destruction. this policy includes support for the galileo programme, with future military applications, which is the main interest behind support for this industry. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − against. we believe that calling for better integration and coordination of eu space programmes is a positive aspect, along with the establishment of a european sst programme, but the overall purpose of the report is to justify investment of more public funds into the space industry, without presenting evidence that this will truly result in a general interest positive effect, an aim that cannot be supported by our group.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an important boost for the development of the information and communication technologies sector which could generate many jobs on the continent. europe must adapt to technological change in a way that creates jobs and copes with the serious economic crisis we are going through. the cloud, as an open way of locating information, offers unlimited potential for business development by providing unlimited access to virtually all of the world's information. because i believe that this report represents an important boost to a sector which can generate thousands of jobs on the continent, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. − in favour. cloud computing has a huge potential and should provide benefits for business, citizens and the public sector but, as a new model of networked computing, poses some legal and contractual risks. also, we must not forget that when developing any strategic framework of action, and in particular this future cloud computing strategy, we have to try and be as horizontal as possible without taking for granted any circumstances that might not seem to directly affect its development. accordingly, infrastructure policies are crucial: strong fixed and mobile communication networks are prerequisite in order to grasp the full potential of the cloud and consequently it is regrettable that the connecting europe facilities communication will not be able to perform adequately if they are not provided with proper financial resources. the report achieves a balanced approach in promoting the use of cloud services while setting for the commission minimum guidance on protecting citizens’ interests especially in regard to openness, transparency and data protection.
in writing. - i have today supported the adoption of the report on cloud computing in europe, which highlights its untapped potential but warns of the need to protect data from third country surveillance and to inform consumers of their rights in terms of privacy and responsibility. without an adequate communication infrastructure and community standards, the growing potential for competitiveness of the cloud will not be exploited, although it should not be forgotten that it must be accompanied by a common regulatory framework for protection as there are considerable risks in security and data protection. i personally believe that smes can take advantage of this instrument to reduce agency, administration and time costs, albeit with strict contracts and terms of use.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it approves the report of the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec). the report argues that this regulatory body should be larger in order to coordinate the sectors in the different member states and to guarantee its independence from the national sector bodies and the european institutions. the report focuses on the importance of independence in regulators to prevent the influence of private actors and to operate for their benefit. to defend the functioning of this important sector of the economy it is essential to develop independent regulators. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. overall, the report states that berec as such is generally functioning well. berec (and its predecessors) appear to have enabled a gradual deepening of mutual trust between nras contributing towards the effective achievement of the berec objectives. in order to improve that, a series of good proposals are being put in and this adds to the generally favourable opinion, therefore our group voted for the report in the committee on industry, research and energy. the proposal is to also vote for it in the plenary.
in writing. - today, my report on the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec) was adopted in plenary. in it, i propose a redefinition of the mission of this office to make the most of its potential role in consolidating the electronic communications market at european level. the operation of berec can be improved, but it is on the right track, especially in view of the limited resources at its disposal. i therefore urge the eu institutions and the member states to ensure adequate funding for this body while maintaining greater independence where possible.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a missed opportunity to achieve a common fisheries policy which would give the sector a boost without destroying marine stocks. our parliamentary group is trying to defend the natural and social environment of fishing communities, including fishermen as a fundamental part of it. small-scale and artisanal fishing is the sector which generates the most employment and allows for a more sustainable relationship with the environment, but it does not seem to have a place in this common fisheries policy. i voted against this report because the fishing communities throughout europe need a policy that meets their needs, creates jobs and maintains the marine stocks on which they depend, rather than proposing an economic area where large fishermen can exploit marine resources without restrictions.
in writing. − today, the reform of the common fisheries policy, which will enter into force on 1 january 2014, was adopted in plenary. after intensive negotiations, this regulation has been adopted, introducing sustainable fishing as a priority objective: discards are gradually prohibited, the maximum sustainable yield of a fishing area is required to be respected in order to maintain the fish stock in the long term, and small-scale fishing is encouraged. in addition, more importance is attached to regional decisions. given spain's long tradition in the fisheries sector and its great importance for production and employment, i welcome this sustainable fishing strategy to ensure a future for this activity and for marine species.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the report by mr stevenson on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation on the common organization of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products. among the most important issues, i would like to stress, with regard to products from catching fisheries, that the report takes account of the need to regulate the provision of information on the type of gear.
in writing. - i voted against this report because the cmo for fisheries is one of the instruments which could make it possible to achieve a fisheries policy which would create jobs without destroying marine resources, but this proposal does not seek to intervene in the market which is causing the disaster, but to further deregulate it. our parliamentary group is trying to defend the natural and social environment of fishing communities, including fishermen as a fundamental part of it. this proposal allows large companies to destroy local artisanal production networks, which should instead be encouraged through market regulation. it is a cmo for the benefit of the big companies and that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it imposes restrictions on high-altitude fishing and on large-scale fishermen, whose activity is the most aggressive against the stocks of the marine environment. the big fishermen take advantage of their great capacity to operate in international waters where, in theory, there is no agency responsible for ensuring the implementation of fishing rules. deep waters are of fundamental importance for the entire marine ecosystem as there are many migratory species whose replacement rate is affected if they are exploited above their maximum sustainable yield. the report amends the existing rules on deep-sea fishing so that fishing vessels must exploit fishery resources in a more sustainable way in deep waters. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against because the devastation caused by these indiscriminate fishing practices on sensitive environments - such as the seabed and reefs - as well as on threatened species is well documented. contrary to the false arguments against phasing out, used by a strong but unrepresentative lobby, these proposals would affect a handful of eu vessels and would have enormous environmental benefits. unfortunately, meps have given themselves over to lobbying. overfishing has driven fishermen into deeper and deeper waters. as the united nations has stressed, these deep-sea environments are ecologically fragile, with unique biodiversity and slower life cycles. the new proposed rules aimed to protect deep-sea species, with sustainable quotas and management plans. however, all this is massively undermined by the lack of support for the gradual disappearance of destructive trawling and gillnets.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it introduces the authorization of the use of military units in humanitarian disasters, such as the very serious situation in the philippines after typhoon haiyan. the report stresses the need to use all available means in the event of tragedies such as the one mentioned. however, the intentions of militarizing disaster relief are obvious. the concept of 'humanitarian' in reference to military interventions has been used as a justification by the imperialist forces of nato for several years now. the use of the same terminology in disasters is the justification for allowing military deployments of european forces in strategic areas, under the pretext of 'humanitarian aid'. i consider it essential that all available means be deployed in the philippines, but i voted against because of the real military intent contained in this report.
mr president, the first european mortgage directive was adopted this morning with over 86% of the votes in favour. i would therefore like to express my satisfaction as rapporteur for this robust birth and, at this time, my thanks to all those who have contributed to making it possible during these three years in parliament. i explained - in the plenary session last september - the reasons for supporting this directive. the mortgage market is very important for european families. it is the biggest financial commitment of his life, the largest and the longest lasting, and it represents 53% of the european economy. this directive can therefore contribute to the recovery of the european economy. it is an important first step in addressing the problems of responsible lending, fair lending and avoiding private over-indebtedness at european level. and, in addition, the member states have a two-year period to develop it. nothing in the directive precludes member states from adopting social measures, measures which seek to address the problems arising from solvency difficulties in the private sector and which also address the needs of the most vulnerable population. i therefore urge the member states to draw inspiration from the principles of this directive and to take the opportunity to develop it to address these problems.
mr president, i would like to congratulate mr sánchez presedo on his work and to stress that this directive adds value to the regulation of a market which in 2009 represented 52% of the european gross domestic product. it does so because it adds a framework of minimum guarantees for customers which starts from the basis of considering housing a basic right and should put an end to abuses, such as evictions, which are experienced, for example, in spain. it also includes measures to make contracts with special risk and the solvency assessment processes more transparent and provides that customers are not penalised for early repayment of loans. we also encourage more informed decisions, protecting a process of reflection and effective advice to clients. in short, we are taking an opportunity to show that europe is worth a lot. let us now be extremely vigilant in ensuring that this directive is transposed accurately and rapidly, especially in those states which are currently experiencing the most problems.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains many well-intentioned measures, it does not include any reference to legislation on the payment of a fee. the lack of control of the mortgage sector in europe has allowed a sector to operate in the most absolute illegality, which has driven more than 400,000 people from their homes in spain alone. this legislative amendment does not take into account the demands of european citizens or even the fundamental right to housing. the european union has allowed the spanish financial sector to operate illegally for almost 20 years by applying the spanish mortgage law, in violation of its obligations as guardian of european law. the only answer has been this decaffeinated proposal which contains only voluntary concepts but without any political will to change the situation. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr paul murphy on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on imports of rice originating in bangladesh, as imports of rice from the least developed countries are now fully liberalized.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it implies the correct implementation of the rules in the field of international trade, avoiding overreaching the sovereignty of third countries. the rapporteur has considerably softened the european commission's interventionist proposal to impose a tax on rice exports to bangladesh. we recognize the right of the people to implement such taxes, but not the eu's right to demand them. the report, once this problem of interference with third countries has been removed, seeks only to regulate trade in a way that is consistent with international law and regulations. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it recognises the ineffectiveness of the eu's emissions trading system. the report credits the surplus that occurred in 2011 of almost eur 1 billion and that has continued to increase due to the establishment of limits well above the actual emission levels so that companies did not have to pay anything and even generate profits from the exchange with these rights. these are the real reasons for the deep failure of the emissions trading system, which has proved to be a poor tool for meeting the emission control objectives. because it recognizes that failure, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it opposes the adoption of the council regulation on the criteria for determining when paper ceases to be waste. the council regulation will make it possible for paper with a high content of other substances to be disregarded as waste and, as a product, to be exported to third countries, with the adverse consequences this can have for the environment in many regions. in this proposal the commission has not been able to demonstrate a valid justification for considering that such recovered paper can be considered as 'product' before its processing, allowing in practice the export of waste. it is further proof of a european commission at the mercy of lobbyists. i therefore voted against this report.

unprecedented by its depth, breadth, and strength – not only by the letter, but by the spirit of this association agreement, which is maybe worth a million times more than a simple stroke of the pen. agreement is also a framework for some of the investments that ukraine will have to make if it is serious about its modernisation pledge. modernisation and investment go hand-in-hand. there can be no modernisation without genuine effort, political will and adequate investment. the speculation we have seen about the alleged cost of ukraine’s modernisation is unfounded and unjustified, as are the maidan on the night of 29 to 30 november. a panel with experts from government, opposition and from the council of europe will hopefully very soon be formed to monitor these investigations. i call crisis. the european union is called upon by all sides to be helpful in such a situation. president barroso has already discussed the european support that is needed and high representative/vice president of the commission, cathy ashton, has arrived in kiev today. we stand ready to help and support ukraine on its modernisation journey, including through topping up imf loans with macro-financial assistance, stepping up the european union’s financial assistance programmes to help ukraine implement the agreement, when signed, and helping to bring on board other international partners. we are also willing to use our dialogue with russia to clarify that the agreement with ukraine will not harm russia’s economic interests. however, the agreement itself is a bilateral issue between the european union and ukraine. as president barroso stated in vilnius, times of limited sovereignty are over in europe. the developments around ukraine have marked the vilnius summit to a considerable extent. this should not however cloud the fact that vilnius was an important step in the development and advancement of the eastern partnership. vilnius was the first summit delivering tangible results, based on the steady work on political association and economic integration that the european union has been doing with partners since the adoption of the prague declaration in may 2009 and the warsaw declaration in 2011. let me enumerate them: 1. we initialled the association agreement/dcfta with georgia and the republic of moldova;2. we signed the visa facilitation agreement with azerbaijan (after a similar agreement had been signed earlier this year with armenia); 3. we signed a framework participation agreement for eu-led crisis management operations with georgia;4. we initialled the common aviation area agreement with ukraine and endorsed the eastern partnership transport network and list of priority projects agreed by transport ministers in october 2013; 5. we had a very successful eastern partnership business forum meeting and civil society conference in vilnius on the eve of the summit; and 6. belarus finally expressed its readiness to take up our offer to begin negotiations on a visa facilitation and readmission agreement. this is very important indeed for the citizens of belarus. we also agreed a joint summit declaration which sets ambitious goals to be reached by 2015. let there be no doubt that respect for our common values will remain at the centre of our partnership: an independent judiciary, tackling corruption, and effective and accountable public administration will be essential to ensure agreements serve those for whom they have been negotiated – namely the citizens. looking ahead, we will intensify our support for broader society – business communities, local and regional authorities, parliaments and, most of all, civil society which is vital for building the constituencies for reforms. vilnius has also proven that differentiation is at the heart of the eastern partnership. we will be as ambitious as our partners are willing to be and we will deliver to the extent to which our partners are able to deliver on reforms. but combined with greater differentiation is our strong determination to pursue our common agenda with all six partners through multilateral dialogue and cooperation. the eastern partnership is all about creating the conditions that will unlock and fulfil the potential for growth, enterprise, and creativity of citizens in eastern europe. the partnership is being tested by the decision of ukraine not to sign the aa/dcfta at this stage, but the european union has come out stronger because it did not compromise when faced with external pressure. it stood firm. it stood united and keeps the door to finishing the transformation of partner countries, within a clear rules-based framework, firmly open. the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing my gratitude to the political groups, the representatives of the commission and the council, and also to the services of parliament and those of my group, because they have really helped me a great deal in the preparation of this report on the association instrument. it was not easy, we were starting from scratch and there was a lot to deal with, a lot of expectations to be reconciled, but i think that in the end the vote in the committee on foreign affairs showed that the work of everyone together has made this report a success. i shall not go into technical matters, madam president, ladies and gentlemen. i would like to touch a little on the issues that affect this report in this world in which we live, which is becoming increasingly volatile, complex and uncertain. we live in an interconnected multipolar international system in which no country is big enough to impose its interests alone and in which the nature of power is changing. moreover, today global competition is increasing. if we have lived for years in the globalization of opportunity, with the outbreak of the economic crisis we have experienced the lessons of the dangers of this globalization. in this global competition, it is sometimes difficult to keep a job or to find one. and all this creates fear and uncertainty in our citizens. in this context, i believe it is of the utmost importance that the european union has an external action instrument - the association instrument - which is intended primarily to provide financial support to the european union in developing our relations with our strategic partners, whether national or regional, as well as with third states and regional bodies, in order to meet global challenges and threats. i would also like to say that there is often a temptation to look the other way, to try to escape from this globalising phenomenon, to seek refuge in populist nationalisms which lie and promise well-being and prosperity through the re-establishment of frontiers and outdated protectionism. ladies and gentlemen, the world today needs actors and policies that generate stability and predictability. the european union, through its various instruments of external action, must be an effective actor in meeting these needs. we must be effective as global actors in the defense of peace and development in the world - especially in our immediate neighbourhood - and, as the region with the world's largest gdp and the largest global trading bloc, we must be key actors in the defense of market stability and in the promotion of global trade rules, as well as in the promotion of energy and food security and environmental and social standards. this requires working with our strategic partners. in this respect, the countries of latin america, as in my case, deserve special attention. we share with them a very similar way of approaching issues of global concern; it is the only region in the world with which we have a bi-regional partnership as a whole; we maintain with them an extensive and dynamic network of association and trade agreements and they can be part of a renewed transatlantic triangular agenda as well as a bridge between the european union and the pacific, both through our bilateral agreements and through possible partnerships with regional bodies such as the pacific alliance. as i said, the world today is a much more competitive place: the rise of emerging powers and the entry into the market of millions of new workers and consumers, together with the struggle for resources - to give a few examples - are good evidence of such competition. the european union must therefore, if it is to remain the same economic and commercial power it is and at the same time maintain its welfare model, its jobs, go out into the world and become more competitive. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of commitments remaining to be settled from previous years under the pilot project on the european territorial cooperation goal. i would like to conclude, madam president, by welcoming the creation of this instrument of association, a specific and relevant instrument for supporting and promoting the values and interests of the european union in the world.
opinion of the committee on development and cooperation. - madam president, the scope of the association instrument for cooperation with third countries has been extended: it used to be limited to the most industrialized countries, but now it also includes middle-income countries. and from the point of view of the development committee, in middle-income countries there are now more poor people than in the least developed countries. what's the reason? because some large countries, like china, india and nigeria, for example, have had great development and have reached this middle income level, but they have very large pockets of poverty and underdevelopment. and that is something the union must take into account when cooperating with those countries, trying to channel aid towards sectors, territories and minorities that need to continue to enjoy or continue to have that cooperation. of course, in this case, as in all development cooperation, the fight for human rights, good governance and democracy must be maintained. the european union must encourage the emerging and developing countries to take on the fight against poverty in their own countries, using their own resources and efforts.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. - madam president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the council and commission teams on the important work they have done in updating the european neighbourhood instrument, having succeeded in reflecting the new regional realities and in structuring this instrument in such a way that the basis for the implementation of the principles enshrined in the new neighbourhood policy, such as the principle of 'more for more', has been strengthened. the application of this principle has been rightly established taking into account the needs, the commitment to democracy and the level of ambition in its will to associate with the european union, as well as the commitment to political, economic and social reforms. the promotion of new governance, institutional consolidation and market economy principles, as well as the opening of goods and services markets and legal certainty for investments by both sides, are elements that will foster the political and economic development of the partner countries, thus facilitating the processes of democratic consolidation and political transition in which they are engaged.
the committee on budgets' rapporteur for the opinion. - madam president, eur 63 billion, which is 6% of the current multiannual financial framework, 3% more than the previous financial framework, but 16% less than the commission's initial forecasts in relation to the supposed needs of external action. the crisis should not be an excuse for relegating the european union's foreign policy, because the european union does not run out of internal resources; on the contrary, it has an inescapable external dimension. and the resources for external action are on an already historic trajectory, which is their insufficiency. this is particularly true of the association instrument, whose main objective is nothing less than to implement the external dimension of the 2020 strategy for growth and jobs with all developed countries and with developing countries with which the european union shares strategic interests. for that work, it has only nine hundred and fifty-four million euros. it's clearly insufficient. in any event, the socialist group is particularly pleased that this instrument is not only applied to the brics or the so-called g-groups, but has been extended to other countries, namely those eight latin american countries which have left the development cooperation policy and can now benefit from this instrument. in any case, the question now is how and when we are going to spend or how and for what we are going to use these instruments that have been improved over the course of an agonizing negotiation process. there is more transparency, there is a greater role for civil society, there are - let us hope - greater synergies between the instruments and policies of the european union, and let us hope there is also greater coordination. all of this will be to the benefit of the union's budget and, above all, to the benefit of the european union's external action, so that we can finally be the relevant actor we want to be.
madam president, we are against the majority in this house who argue that what we need to do in the world at the moment is to globalize the economy without globalizing rights. the majority of the house agrees with this principle and applies, for the european union and beyond, the deregulatory principle - in the economic sector, in the financial sector, betting on privatizations - which is leading the european union to a dead end and to unprecedented social aggression. this principle is to be applied to the neighbourhood policy and the pre-accession policy. and from our point of view it is unacceptable. what we do not want for the people of europe we cannot want for other peoples who are not yet part of the european union. that is why the principle of conditionality is intended to bring to its knees people who want to join the european union on the basis of the deregulatory principle. we disagree. we also do not agree with the european neighbourhood instrument being used in a torturous way, incorporating territories such as the occupied palestinian territory and forgetting the autonomous territory of western sahara. we do not agree with that line of thinking.
madam president, i welcome, firstly, the fact that the amount foreseen for external action in the next financial framework has been increased by three per cent compared with the previous one. in an increasingly complex and poorly governed world, the new partnership instrument will be useful in strengthening relations with our strategic partners, but also with third states and regional bodies that share our vision of tackling global challenges. in this connection, i would like to stress the importance of latin american countries, for example, for the european union. the arab spring and the strategic repositioning of the united states are forcing the union and its member states to assume greater responsibilities towards their neighbours, both east and south. i hope that the definition of the 'more for more' principle in the european neighbourhood instrument will help to accompany the transition processes of neighbours. the union remains the largest donor of development cooperation and i welcome the commitment of the development cooperation financing instrument to the fight against poverty in low-income countries and also in middle-income countries. the european union must be a provider of peace, development, stability and integration and a guarantor of respect for human rights. i hope that the instruments we are discussing today will help to maintain these hallmarks of the union.
madam president, i thank the rapporteur for the development cooperation financing instrument and the negotiating team for the work they have done, especially in view of the amount of time devoted to delegated acts and that we have only five months left to negotiate an instrument of about 20 billion euro. anyway, the result is positive. we will have more control over every euro that the taxpayer contributes to development cooperation and this parliament will guarantee transparency, efficiency and better coordination of aid to development cooperation with the aim of eradicating poverty. aid will be directed to those most in need, including in middle-income countries, especially in latin america. countries such as colombia, peru, ecuador, cuba and south africa will be able to continue to benefit in the medium term from european union aid, especially because this parliament considered it crucial from the outset. it is important to note that 20% of the benchmark will be dedicated to basic social services with a focus on education and health. i believe that a new period for development cooperation is opening up in the coming years and that the european union has achieved an instrument that is up to the challenge.

president-in-office of the council. − madam president, i would like to thank those who have participated in this debate for both their constructive and critical remarks. i consider that this afternoon’s debate has demonstrated the eu sending a clear signal to its partners of its commitment to an efficient and coherent external policy. many of you mentioned delegated acts and accountability. in this regard let me just mention that, since the beginning of the negotiations, the council expressed its readiness to look at where amending delegated acts could be appropriate and of added value. it would mean that they would be considered on an instrument-by-instrument basis and that there might be an instrument for which there would be no delegated act. however, having said that, let me also mention that actually we found agreement by which a number of delegated acts were introduced into the specific instruments. this agreement is complemented by the introduction of the mid-term review in order to revise, if appropriate, the content of the annexes subject to the delegated act. in addition, a strategic dialogue between the european parliament and the commission has been agreed in order to provide for political oversight of the parliament on the programming process, in accordance with article 14 of the treaty on the functioning of the eu. the strategic dialogue will be conducted by the commission represented at the appropriate level and it will take place prior to the programming phase and after the initial consultation of the relevant beneficiaries. after more than two years of negotiation, i feel that we can be proud of the outcome of our shared efforts. the external financial instrument package will offer a solid and efficient framework for the union’s external financial aid. once again, i would like to express my sincere thanks to you all for the excellent cooperation between our institutions.

rapporteur. − madam president, first of all i want to thank my shadow rapporteurs for all their good cooperation during these months, especially andreas schwab and antolín sanchez presedo. thank you very much for your kind cooperation. i would also like to particularly thank commissioner almunia and his team for our constructive work together. i very much welcome the fact that the 2012 european commission competition report celebrates and focuses on the eu single market and its 20th anniversary. i share this priority. in fact a lot remains to be done in several sectors, such as banks, telecommunications, energy, competition authorities and transport, in order to achieve a non-discriminatory well-functioning single market in europe. in this report i have tried to push for more transparency and cooperation between the parliament and dg competition and i also ask for more human resources for dg competition in order to do a better job. regarding the banking sector, there is a clear problem of concentration, in my opinion, in some member states. after receiving eur 1.6 trillion of state aid and public guarantees, the banking sector in europe is still not working properly. credit for smes in many parts of europe is scarce and expensive, delaying the return to economic growth in the near term. in spain, for example, credit to non-financial companies has fallen again by 11% during this year. there is a huge crowding-out effect. banks which are purchasers of public debt are expelling credit to the private sector. regarding the transport sector, we deplore the lack of competition in the european rail market and state aid to national incumbent airlines. the eu rail market is not functioning properly, due to incorrect or incomplete transposition of community law by member states. too often, incumbent railway operators are protected by their own member states. in this respect, i welcome the infringement procedures launched by the european commission in the last few years in several member states. regarding state aid to airlines, i understand dg competition is paying a lot of attention to regional airport subsidies to ryanair, but we should also make sure that the rules on state aid are applied correctly with regard to national carriers such as iberia, alitalia and others. rules should be the same for all actors and we should not accept the ‘too big to fail’ doctrine for airlines. european citizens should not be the ones who always end up paying. i also think the commission should investigate the 1 000 bilateral agreements in various member states in the air transport sector that restrict competition by imposing, for example, the requirement that any flight between two countries must stop in a given airport. in spain, for example, 23 bilateral treaties oblige planes to stop only at madrid airport. on the energy sector, this parliament is asking to fully investigate the demand effect. why is fuel so expensive on some days and so cheap on others? i believe it is not the consequence of market forces and my guess is that some sort of cartel is behind it. to solve all this, we need independent competition authorities and we need their reports to be completely non-political, otherwise we keep on supporting a system which, although theoretically in favour of competition, in practice protects the oligopolies. finally, on the google case, i have two questions for the commissioner regarding the procedure. does the commission believe that the adoption of google’s proposals as they stand will effectively address the commission’s concerns about fair competition and protect consumers? if not, will you finally send a statement of objections to google in order to impose truly significant remedies, once and for all? i call on the commission to take our report fully into account and to act in the coming months. thank you very much for your kind attention and i look forward to your comments and answers.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr ramon tremosa, on his excellent work and constructive spirit, and also to thank the other rapporteurs for the fact that we have reached a motion for a resolution with a high level of consensus in parliament. the socialist group will support it because it considers that it reflects the essence of its approaches. we wanted to emphasize the importance of transparency and cooperation in the development of competition policy. transparency leads us to call for the updating of statistics on state aid to financial institutions since the beginning of the crisis and to ask the european competition network to disseminate its work programmes and conclusions. and cooperation leads us to emphasize the role of the judicial authorities in the development of competition policy and cooperation, also, with the national regulatory authorities. we would also like to stress the importance of competition policy in overcoming the crisis, in implementing the europe 2020 strategy and in achieving the union's objectives. competition policy has helped to ensure a fair distribution of the restructuring of banks in difficulty. it must do the same for financial innovation, it must continue to perfect the internal market and it must help to meet the challenges of globalisation and change. for this reason, we will support it.

mr president, at the beginning of his speech, mr swoboda made a mockery of the comparative growth and employment figures between the united states and the european union. sad irony, because there they are robust, they are positive, and here they are either negative or stunted. in fact, there are more than ten countries in the european union that have unemployment rates so high that they will not be able to bring them down below ten percent for a couple of decades. this shows that in 2008 and in 2012 there have been, and there will be next year, better policies on another continent, not in the european union. it shows that the policy of austerity alone has not produced the positive results that other policies are producing elsewhere. but it's not just about politics. it is also about decision-making processes. there, decisions are made overnight when a quick political agreement is reached. it is true that the united states has also experienced the so-called "shutdown", that is, it has been paralysed for a good number of months. but let us return to the european union. the banking resolution mechanism is still being discussed today and we do not know whether agreement will be reached at the next council. but the data shows that the single resolution fund won't come until a decade from now or until 2026. with that timetable, it is difficult to tackle a banking union that is really understandable to the rest of the world economies. so we need to change policies and we need to change the way we make decisions on those policies.
mr president, the great efforts and sacrifices to ensure the sustainability of our public accounts and the structural reforms undertaken over the last two years are bearing fruit. however, the recovery from the crisis is still extremely fragile and challenges and concerns persist. in our view, at least five things are needed to get out of the crisis: differentiated fiscal consolidation, more flexible and growth-friendly; structural reforms to make us competitive and enable us to grow and create jobs; further progress in european integration and further reforms at european level - in this sense it is vital to make rapid progress in the banking union and in the development of the internal market and in this respect it must be said, contrary to some of the things that have been said here, that we think the preliminary agreements are absolutely hopeful; a decisive approach to the employment situation, especially for young people, and that the funds for the youth guarantee are now available; and solving the credit and liquidity problems affecting small and mediumsized enterprises. the european council must reach an agreement which is fundamental to consolidating the recovery from the crisis, namely the banking union. it is urgent, ladies and gentlemen, to reach agreement on a single resolution fund and a single authority, which could be the council or the commission. i am glad, ladies and gentlemen, that the european council is going to have an in-depth debate on the future of european security and defence policy. the union will not have a complete foreign policy until it has fully developed operational capabilities in defence. strong, generous leadership is needed from member states to be able to pool our capacities in favour of shared and viable objectives, thus avoiding duplication and shortcomings. the complementarity of the union's civil and military actions must also be improved, in order to increase its capacity to react, its efficiency, effectiveness and visibility, thus giving the european union credibility as a provider of regional and global security and stability.
mr president, a european council is always a political meeting at the highest level and the debate within it must be as well. we have talked about the reflection that will be concentrated on the common security and defence policy in order to increase the effectiveness, the defence capacity, the strengthening of the industrial sector and the strengthening of the european defence agency. but it's worrying that the reason is economic. the cuts, the budget cuts, which force the member states to optimise their defence efforts, because the reason should be political: the belief in a shared project. and the same is true of the progress that has been awaited for too long in the banking union. the european supervisory mechanism and the deposit guarantee are not enough. the commission's powers in the management of this new banking union system must be strengthened, but so must the democratic control which this parliament must exercise. i say this because the european elections are very close at hand and it is impossible to lose sight of them for a second. the year 2014 will see a real choice between europeans and growth - as many surveys already indicate - and anti-european or outright anti-european attitudes. it must therefore be very clear that the forthcoming european elections represent a last chance to relaunch the european project, which means that we have to review the economic policy that has forced these cuts, the economic policy that has led the european union to the worst hour in its history, and to boost growth, the social agenda and job creation all at once.
